jobs.title: Finance Manager II - Payroll Payments & Audits, Payroll
jobs.description:
Finance Manager II – Global Payroll Payments & Audits

Job Title

Finance Manager II – Global Payroll Payments & Audits

Location: Hyderabad, Telangana, India
Work Model: Work from Office
Job ID: 10512609
Level: 5
Job Type: Full-Time, Regular
Function: Finance & Accounting
Team: Global Payroll Payments
Department: Payroll – VAR

Role Overview

Amazon's Global Payroll Payments team is hiring a Finance Manager II to lead and scale payroll payment operations across APAC and North America.

The role sits at the intersection of payments, banking, controls/audit, and technology transformation. You will own the end-to-end payroll payment lifecycle, lead a team of 20+ professionals, manage strategic banking and payment-service-provider relationships, strengthen financial controls and audits, and drive automation and payment modernization through APIs and standards such as ISO 20022.

This is a senior leader who operates at both strategic and operational levels — moving comfortably from executive stakeholder management and banking-partner negotiations to payment incident resolution, operational deep dives, and people leadership. Payroll experience is valuable but not required: strong leaders from payments, banking operations, treasury, or financial operations with people-management and controls depth are encouraged to apply.

Key Role Objectives

Lead global payroll payment operations across APAC and North America.
Manage and develop a high-performing team of 20+ professionals.
Manage strategic relationships with banks, payment service providers, fintechs, and vendors.
Ensure payment accuracy, timeliness, security, reliability, and operational resilience.
Own payment controls, audits, reconciliations, risk management, and compliance mechanisms.
Lead payment infrastructure readiness for new countries and entities.
Drive automation, API-based integrations, monitoring, and payment modernization.
Lead resolution of critical payment incidents and recurring defects.
Build scalable mechanisms, standard work, playbooks, and operating rhythms.
Drive continuous improvement using data, metrics, technology, and customer impact.

Key Job Responsibilities

Global Payroll Payment Operations

Own the end-to-end payroll payment lifecycle across APAC and North America, including payment file generation, validation, bank submission, transaction monitoring, exception management, settlement, and reconciliation.
Establish mechanisms to monitor payment health, service levels, control performance, operational risks, and critical dependencies.
Review operational dashboards and payment metrics to identify emerging issues and prioritize corrective actions.
Lead resolution of payment batch failures, rejected transactions, bank exceptions, processing delays, and other payment-related issues.
Ensure payroll payments are processed accurately, securely, and within defined service-level expectations.
Develop mechanisms that improve payment reliability, resilience, scalability, and employee experience.
Identify systemic issues and drive permanent corrective actions rather than recurring manual fixes.

People Leadership & Team Development

Lead and develop a team of 20+ finance and payments professionals.
Build organizational capability across payment operations, audits, banking controls, reconciliations, monitoring, and issue resolution.
Establish clear goals, performance mechanisms, operating rhythms, and development plans.
Create a culture of ownership, accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Coach and mentor team members and build a strong leadership pipeline.
Develop technical, analytical, and business capabilities within the organization.
Build a diverse, inclusive, and high-performing team capable of operating at global scale.

Banking & Payment Partnerships

Build and manage strategic relationships with global and regional banking partners.
Manage relationships with payment service providers, fintechs, financial institutions, and third-party vendors.
Partner with banks on service levels, payment requirements, file specifications, connectivity, format changes, testing, and issue resolution.
Manage payment methods including RTP, ACH, wire transfers, and other applicable payment rails.
Coordinate payment-format and connectivity migrations while maintaining business continuity.
Represent Amazon's payroll payment requirements in discussions with external banking and technology partners.
Lead escalations with financial institutions for critical payment failures and service disruptions.

New Country & Entity Launches

Lead payment infrastructure readiness for new Amazon countries, entities, and business expansions.
Coordinate bank-account onboarding and payment infrastructure requirements.
Define payment-file specifications, banking connectivity, testing, UAT, and go-live requirements.
Partner with Payroll, Treasury, Finance, Technology, Compliance, and other stakeholders to identify dependencies and risks.
Develop reusable launch-readiness frameworks, playbooks, standard work, and deployment mechanisms.
Ensure new markets launch efficiently while maintaining strong financial controls and operational resilience.

Automation & Payment Modernization

Identify opportunities to eliminate manual processes and improve payment scalability, accuracy, control effectiveness, and efficiency.
Partner with Technology and Finance teams to implement automation and scalable payment solutions.
Drive adoption of API-based integrations (REST APIs) and modern payment technologies.
Support adoption of ISO 20022 and other modern payment standards where applicable.
Leverage monitoring frameworks to identify payment issues proactively.
Evaluate and implement AI-enabled solutions for exception management, monitoring, root-cause analysis, and operational productivity.
Reduce operational risk through technology-enabled controls while improving the employee payment experience.

Critical Escalations & Incident Management

Serve as a senior escalation point for critical payroll payment incidents.
Lead resolution of bank-side failures, payment batch rejections, service disruptions, and high-risk exceptions.
Lead structured root-cause analysis for high-impact incidents.
Coordinate cross-functional resolution across Finance, Payroll, Technology, Treasury, Operations, and banking partners.
Establish mechanisms to prevent recurrence and track incident trends to identify systemic payment risks.
Develop and maintain escalation and incident-management playbooks.
Improve payment resilience through lessons learned and continuous improvement.

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence

Use data and operational metrics to identify improvement opportunities.
Prioritize initiatives based on customer impact, financial risk, operational risk, and business value.
Simplify complex payment processes and eliminate unnecessary manual activities.
Improve payment accuracy, timeliness, reliability, and control effectiveness.
Establish scalable mechanisms that support increasing payment volumes and geographic expansion.
Drive cross-functional transformation initiatives.
Measure and communicate business impact to senior leadership.

Stakeholder Management

The role works closely with:

Global Payroll
Finance & Controllership
Treasury
Technology / Engineering
Banking & Financial Institutions
Payment Service Providers
FinTech Partners
Compliance
Risk Management
Internal Audit
External Audit
Operations
Country and Entity Launch Teams
Senior Finance Leadership
Business and Corporate Stakeholders

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field.
8+ years of experience in finance, payments, banking operations, payroll operations, treasury, or financial operations — including work in complex, high-volume, or multi-country environments.
5+ years of people-management experience, including leading teams or managing managers.
Experience managing relationships with banks, payment service providers, fintechs, financial institutions, or external vendors.
Experience designing or operating financial controls, audits, reconciliations, risk, or compliance mechanisms.
Experience using data and metrics to identify operational issues and drive measurable improvements.
Experience working cross-functionally across Finance, Technology, Operations, Payroll, or Treasury.
Experience communicating complex financial, operational, or technical information clearly to senior leadership.
Experience identifying root causes, implementing corrective actions, and building mechanisms to prevent recurrence.
Experience working in a large, multinational, or highly complex organization.

Preferred Qualifications

Global payroll payments or payment operations.
Banking operations or banking infrastructure.
Treasury operations.
Financial technology / FinTech.
RTP, ACH, wire transfers, or other electronic payment rails.
Payment files and banking connectivity.
API-based payment integrations and REST API-based services.
Knowledge of ISO 20022 or modern payment standards.
Payment infrastructure setup for new countries or entities.
Payment-service-provider and third-party vendor management.
Automation, digital transformation, and AI-enabled operational solutions.
Monitoring and exception-management frameworks.
Launch-readiness frameworks and scalable deployment mechanisms.
Large-scale operational transformation in regulated, multinational, or high-volume environments.
MBA, CPA, CA, CMA, or other relevant professional qualification.

Leadership Competencies

Strategic Thinking: Builds long-term payment and operational strategies.
People Leadership: Attracts, develops, motivates, and retains high-performing teams.
Operational Excellence: Owns accuracy, reliability, controls, and execution.
Customer Obsession: Ensures employees are paid accurately and on time.
Data-Driven Decision Making: Uses metrics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities.
Problem Solving: Solves complex, ambiguous, high-impact operational problems.
Stakeholder Management: Influences senior stakeholders without direct authority.
Banking & Commercial Acumen: Manages strategic relationships with financial institutions and payment partners.
Technology Fluency: Partners effectively with technology teams; understands APIs, payment infrastructure, automation, and data.
Change Leadership: Leads transformation across people, processes, and technology.
Executive Communication: Communicates complex issues clearly and concisely to senior leaders.
Ownership & Accountability: Dives deep, challenges existing mechanisms, and drives issues to closure.

Key Success Metrics

Payroll payment accuracy.
On-time payment performance.
Payment failure and rejection rates.
Critical payment incident resolution.
Reduction in recurring payment defects.
Banking-partner service-level performance.
Control effectiveness.
Audit readiness and reduction in repeat findings.
Reconciliation quality and timeliness.
Automation and manual-effort reduction.
Payment-processing scalability.
New-market launch readiness and execution.
Operational risk reduction.
Team performance, engagement, and talent development.
Delivery of strategic transformation initiatives.

What Success Looks Like

Reliable payments. Strong controls. Scalable infrastructure. Fewer recurring defects. Better automation. Strong banking partnerships. Effective audits. And a high-performing team that operates confidently at global scale.

Early on, the leader establishes strong operational visibility, understands the global payment landscape, strengthens critical mechanisms, and builds trusted relationships with key stakeholders and banking partners. Over time, they transform the organization from a primarily operational model into a scalable, technology-enabled, data-driven global payment organization.
A Day in the Life

Reviewing payment-health dashboards, critical exceptions, audit status, and operational metrics.
Investigating recurring payment or banking exceptions with the team.
Working with Technology on API, payment-file, or connectivity changes.
Engaging banking partners to resolve service issues or payment failures.
Reviewing new-country or entity launch readiness.
Challenging existing controls and reviewing audit findings.
Identifying opportunities for automation and process simplification.
Reviewing business and operational metrics with senior leadership.
Coaching team members and reviewing performance and priorities.
Removing organizational blockers and establishing mechanisms for long-term improvement.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The strongest candidate is typically a senior finance, payments, banking operations, treasury, or financial operations leader who has:

Led large teams, ideally 20+ people.
Managed high-volume payment or financial operations.
Worked directly with banks or payment service providers.
Owned operational controls, audits, reconciliations, and risk.
Operated across multiple countries or geographies.
Partnered extensively with Technology and Finance organizations.
Managed critical incidents and complex operational escalations.
Built scalable processes and operating mechanisms.
Delivered automation or digital transformation.
Demonstrated strong executive presence and stakeholder influence.

Payroll experience is highly valuable but is not the only path into the role. Strong leaders from payments, banking operations, treasury, financial operations, or payment infrastructure with relevant people-management and controls experience should also be considered.
Core Search Keywords

Payments · Payment Operations · Banking Operations · Banking Infrastructure · Payroll Payments · Global Payroll · Payment Processing · Payment Infrastructure · Treasury · RTP · ACH · Wire · Payment Service Provider · PSP · FinTech · Financial Institutions · Banking Partner · Payment Connectivity · Payment Files · ISO 20022 · APIs · REST APIs · Automation · AI · Payment Controls · Audit · Reconciliation · Risk · Compliance · People Management · Team Leadership · Operational Excellence · Launch Readiness · Global Operations · Financial Operations
Final Candidate Value Proposition

This is an opportunity to lead a critical financial infrastructure function at Amazon and influence how payroll payments are delivered across multiple countries. The role combines:

Global scale
Large-team leadership
Payments and banking ownership
Finance and controls
Technology transformation
Strategic external partnerships
New-market launches
Operational excellence
Automation and AI
Executive-level visibility

If you are a finance or payments leader who enjoys solving complex problems, working with banks and technology teams, building high-performing organizations, and creating scalable mechanisms, this role offers the opportunity to shape the future of global payroll payments at Amazon.

Key job responsibilities
Key Job Responsibilities

Lead Global Payroll Payment Operations

Own the end-to-end payroll payment lifecycle across APAC and North America, including payment file generation, bank submission, transaction monitoring, exception management, and reconciliation.

Establish operational mechanisms to monitor payment health, service levels, control performance, and critical payment risks.

Review operational dashboards and metrics to identify emerging issues, prioritize actions, and maintain high standards of payment accuracy and timeliness.

Lead resolution of payment batch failures, rejected transactions, bank exceptions, and other payment-related issues.

Establish clear goals, performance mechanisms, operating rhythms, and development plans for the team.
Create a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, data-driven decision-making, and operational excellence.

Build strong technical and business capabilities within the team to support increasingly complex global payment operations.

Drive Banking & Payment Partnerships

Partner with banks to manage service levels, payment requirements, file specifications, format changes, connectivity, and issue resolution.

Coordinate payment format migrations and changes while ensuring business continuity and operational readiness.
Represent Amazon's payroll payment requirements in discussions with external banking and technology partners.

Coordinate bank account onboarding, payment file specifications, connectivity requirements, testing, user acceptance testing, and go-live readiness.

Partner with Payroll, Treasury, Finance, Technology, Compliance, and other stakeholders to identify dependencies and manage launch risks.

Establish scalable mechanisms that enable new markets to onboard efficiently while maintaining strong financial controls.

Lead reviews of banking audits, account changes, payment controls, reconciliations, and operational exceptions.
Analyze audit findings and recurring defects to identify root causes and drive permanent corrective actions.

Eliminate redundant or manual audit activities by addressing issues upstream and strengthening preventive controls.
Maintain appropriate documentation, evidence, and control mechanisms to support internal and external audit requirements.

Drive Automation & Payment Modernization
Identify opportunities to eliminate manual activities and improve the scalability, accuracy, and efficiency of payment operations.

Drive adoption of modern payment standards, including ISO 20022, where applicable.
Explore and implement AI-enabled solutions to improve exception management, operational monitoring, root-cause analysis, and process efficiency.

Develop scalable solutions that reduce operational risk while improving the overall employee payment experience.

The role combines strategic thinking with operational execution—you will need to move comfortably between executive-level discussions, banking-partner negotiations, technology conversations, operational deep dives, and team leadership.

jobs.title: Finance Manager, Ads Agencies
jobs.description:
Amazon Ads is dedicated to driving measurable outcomes for brand advertisers, agencies, and entrepreneurs across our international markets. We offer customers a range of flexible pricing and buying models, including self-service, managed service, and programmatic ad buying. These solutions help businesses build brand awareness, increase product sales, and more.

Amazon Ads seeks a Finance Manager to lead Agency Finance and Strategy across the global expansion portfolio. This role is the primary Finance partner to agency leadership teams supporting a broad portfolio of international locales including Japan, Canada, Brazil, Australia, Mexico, UAE, TR, the Nordics, and others. This locales and reports directly to the Finance Director supporting global expansion for Ads Sales.

A successful candidate will operate independently in a rapidly growing and evolving business. The ideal candidate will be as comfortable building and refining financial models as they are with challenging and refining business strategies.

Key job responsibilities
Financial Planning & Modeling

Own the agency revenue plan across the IX+CA+JP portfolio, supporting rapid multi-year growth targets

Build and maintain financial models supporting long-range scenarios, stepping stones, and sensitivity analyses

Lead quarterly guidance, annual planning cycles, and variance analysis across dozens of deals and locales

Model the economics of incentive structures (rebates, price terms, hybrid) that vary by market

Strategy Development

Partner with agency sales leadership to drive three simultaneous transformation workstreams: coverage expansion, incentive optimization, and partner segmentation

Develop the strategy to significantly expand agency coverage and deepen engagement with agency partners

Build the business case and roadmap for scaling the Independent agency segment

Identify and close advertiser concentration and supply source gaps

Business Partnership

Serve as a trusted advisor across agency leadership teams spanning multiple locales and holdco structures

Translate complex, multi-market financial data into actionable narratives for senior leadership

Challenge assumptions, pressure-test targets, and bring analytical rigor to investment decisions

A day in the life

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, In-Life Services
jobs.description:
In Life service (ILS) is part of the larger Global Fleet Product org ( GFP) with the mission is to enable vehicle readiness across Amazon Logistics’ last mile network by building scalable maintenance, repair, and operational support programs that improve fleet availability, operational efficiency, and Delivery Service Partner (DSP) experience. ILS serves as the central organization responsible for managing and evolving the end-to-end maintenance and repair ecosystem supporting Amazon’s delivery fleet, including vendor governance, repair operations, escalation management, operational tooling, maintenance workflows, and strategic fleet readiness programs. To support Amazon Logistics’ rapidly expanding delivery network, ILS partners closely with Delivery Service Partners (DSPs), Fleet Management Companies (FMCs), Fleet Service Suppliers (FSS), product and technology teams, and external maintenance vendors to ensure vehicles remain operationally ready while minimizing disruption to DSP operations.
As Amazon’s fleet footprint and operational complexity continue to scale, fleet maintenance and repair operations remain a significant operational focus area. Fragmented workflows, inconsistent vendor execution, operational inefficiencies, and manual processes can negatively impact vehicle availability, repair turnaround times, and DSP experience. To address these challenges, ILS is continuously developing and scaling transformative maintenance programs, operational governance mechanisms, vendor management frameworks, and technology-enabled operational solutions that simplify maintenance operations, improve service consistency, and strengthen end-to-end DSP support.
ILS is looking for a Sr. Program Manager to lead vendor governance, operational performance management, and strategic maintenance initiatives across Amazon’s fleet maintenance ecosystem. This leader will work cross-functionally with internal stakeholders, Fleet Management Companies (FMCs), Fleet Service Suppliers (FSS), product teams, and external vendors to improve operational performance, establish scalable governance mechanisms, and drive improvements in vehicle maintenance and repair operations that materially enhance the DSP experience. The Sr. Program Manager will drive operational excellence across maintenance vendors by improving service turnaround time, vehicle availability, repair quality, escalation management, and operational consistency while supporting broader network transformation initiatives including Direct Maintenance Programs (DMP), close-loop repair models, inspection programs, and future-state maintenance operations.
The Sr. Program Manager will partner closely with product and technology teams to simplify workflows, improve operational tooling, and establish scalable operational processes and standard operating procedures that enable Central Operations, field teams, and vendor partners to manage fleet maintenance operations more efficiently. This leader will leverage data-driven insights and operational analytics to identify systemic operational gaps, drive root cause analysis, improve vendor accountability, and develop scalable solutions that reduce operational friction and improve network performance. Responsibilities include sourcing and analyzing operational data, defining and managing key performance metrics, identifying operational trends and risks, and translating business insights into actionable improvement initiatives that strengthen operational execution and DSP satisfaction.
The Sr. Program Manager will additionally support strategic operational initiatives related to vendor readiness, network scaling, hibernation and redeployment programs, escalation governance, and operational automation. Through partnership with business, product, and technology teams, this leader will contribute to development of scalable governance architectures, automated workflows, predictive operational insights, and system-driven operational controls that improve consistency and reduce dependency on manual intervention. Through these efforts, the Sr. Program Manager will enable Delivery Service Partners to focus on what they do best — delivering reliably and safely to Amazon customers.
This role indexes heavily on the Leadership Principles of Ownership, Dive Deep, Think Big, Deliver Results, Invent and Simplify, and Bias for Action. The role requires a combination of strategic thinking and operational execution, including the ability to navigate ambiguity, manage complex vendor ecosystems, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and drive scalable operational improvements grounded in strong data analysis and customer-focused decision making.
Key job responsibilities
• Drive end-to-end vendor governance and operational performance management across fleet maintenance vendors, Fleet Management Companies (FMCs), and Fleet Service Suppliers (FSS)
• Define and manage operational success metrics including turnaround time (TAT), vendor-controllable VORR, repair aging, burn rate, repair quality, escalation response, and DSP experience indicators
• Lead operational deep dives and root cause analysis to identify systemic operational gaps, performance risks, and opportunities to improve maintenance and repair operations
• Partner cross-functionally with Product, Program, Operations, Finance, Central Operations, field teams, and vendor leadership teams to improve operational performance and execution consistency
• Drive corrective action plans and operational improvement initiatives across vendors, stations, and network workflows based on data-driven insights and operational trends
• Support strategic maintenance transformation initiatives including Direct Maintenance Programs (DMP), close-loop repair operations, vendor onboarding, network expansion, and inspection programs
• Develop scalable governance mechanisms, workflows, and operational processes that improve visibility, accountability, and service consistency across the maintenance ecosystem
• Partner with technology and product teams to improve operational tooling, streamline workflows, reduce operational friction, and support automation initiatives
• Manage high-severity operational escalations requiring cross-functional coordination, vendor intervention, and leadership visibility
• Maintain dashboards, reporting mechanisms, and operational analytics that provide leadership visibility into key business indicators and support data-driven decision making
• Identify critical operational characteristics, vendor performance trends, and emerging network risks to proactively improve operational readiness and scalability
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Bachelor's degree
Preferred qualifications:

jobs.title: Senior Design Program Manager, Enterprise, Worldwide Grocery Retail Growth & Development (WWRGD)
jobs.description:
Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Retail Growth & Development (WWRGD), Enterprise Design team is seeking a Senior Design Manager to own the end-to-end design function of the PERF (Project and Equipment Request Form) program across our entire grocery store fleet.

This is an exciting role for a design leader who can operate at the intersection of design quality and operational scale. You are the right person for this job if you are a creative problem solver with a passion for customers, strong program management instincts, and the ability to drive high-volume design work efficiently and consistently. In this role, you will own the entire Design PERF workstream — from deciding which projects need design, to prioritizing and resourcing the work, to executing and delivering design solutions for equipment replacements, brand refreshes, and other in-store improvement projects. Not every PERF project requires design intervention, and a key part of this role is building the judgment and systems to identify which ones do and get them done well.

You will serve as the primary design partner to the PERF Construction Management team, equipment and procurement partners, and store operations stakeholders. You will define the standards and toolkits that make design delivery repeatable at scale, and you will be the senior design voice for the program, ensuring every project is grounded in strong design thinking and delivered efficiently. We are looking for someone who is comfortable moving quickly, communicating clearly at all levels, and taking end-to-end ownership in an ambiguous, fast-paced environment.

We are a fast-moving business unit where everyone is entrepreneurial, wears many hats, and works effectively in a highly collaborative environment. The ideal candidate is a creative problem solver with strong program management instincts, a passion for customers, and the ability to build scalable design systems that work across a high-volume portfolio.

Key job responsibilities
- End-to-End Workstream Ownership: Own the entire Design PERF workstream, establishing the processes and standards that govern how design requests are received, prioritized, resourced, and delivered.
- Design Intake and Prioritization: Establish criteria for which PERF projects require design intervention and own prioritization across the portfolio, triaging requests by urgency, strategic importance, and operational impact
- Resourcing: Match project needs to internal and external design capacity and proactively identify gaps.
- Design Execution: Lead and execute design work for PERF scope, equipment replacements, breakroom and restroom refreshes, and in-store improvement projects to brand standards and operational requirements.
- Design Standards and Toolkits: Develop and maintain scalable design standards and toolkits for PERF project types, enabling consistent, repeatable solutions across the fleet.
- Cross-Functional Coordination: Serve as the primary design counterpart to Construction, equipment, and procurement partners, providing guidance and documentation from intake through installation.
- Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner with store leaders, Operations, Area leadership, and WWRGD partners to align on scope, priorities, and design intent.
- Process Improvement and Reporting: Identify and implement process efficiencies, track design delivery KPIs, and provide regular status updates to WWRGD leadership.

A day in the life
If you thrive in a dynamic, high-volume environment where design rigor and operational pace must coexist, then we want to talk to you. A typical day involves triaging new PERF design requests, advancing active design packages, and coordinating with the Capital Planning and Construction teams to ensure design handoffs are clean and complete. You will regularly interface with store operations leaders to ground design decisions in real store context, partner with procurement on equipment specifications, and advance process improvements that help the team scale. This role requires both design judgment and program management discipline — you will need to move quickly, communicate clearly, and maintain quality across a portfolio of hundreds of active projects at any given time.

About the team
The Enterprise Design team leads the transformation of our existing grocery locations through strategic remodels and innovations. We enhance the shopping experience by modernizing store layout, improving operational efficiency, and implementing the latest brand standards, all while stores remain open for business. Our customer-obsessed design approach focuses on creating seamless shopping experiences for both in-store and online customers, while ensuring our operations teams can work safely and efficiently during and after remodels.

- Experience gathering and analyzing large amounts of data and delivering continuous business improvements

The Sr. Preventative Maintenance PM ensures optimal equipment performance, minimizes downtime, reduces operational costs, and maintains compliance with safety and regulatory standards.

Key job responsibilities
Program Development & Management:
- Design and implement preventative maintenance programs for refrigeration systems, HVAC, electrical systems, plumbing, and store equipment across multiple retail grocery locations.
- Develop maintenance schedules, standard operating procedures, and best practices to maximize equipment lifespan and minimize unplanned downtime.

jobs.title: Finance Manager - SCOT Automated Inventory Management , SCOT AIM Finance
jobs.description:
The Supply Chain Optimization Technologies (SCOT) team sits at the core of Amazon's global supply chain — determining what inventory to buy, when to buy it, how much to order, where to position it, and how to recover value from unproductive inventory — all to delight customers while meeting Amazon's business objectives. Operating at massive scale across hundreds of product lines and billions of dollars of worldwide inventory, SCOT's fully in-house, automated planning and optimization systems are among the most sophisticated in the world. Finance within SCOT is a high-impact function, partnering directly with AI and machine learning engineers, scientists, product managers, and operations leaders to shape strategy, drive investment decisions, and deliver measurable improvements to Amazon's supply chain economics.

--The Role--

We're looking for a Finance Manager who thrives in deep business partnership with senior executives, including Directors and VPs — serving as the financial owner for our Rest of World Automated Inventory Management portfolio, covering India, Japan, AMET (Africa, Middle East, and Turkey), and emerging markets across Latin America and Asia Pacific.

This role sits at the intersection of finance and AI in supply chain — with high agency, a direct line to the regional leaders defining Amazon's inventory strategy across some of its fastest-growing markets, and the autonomy to drive investment decisions as the financial voice shaping how these systems are built, extended, and scaled into new geographies.

We seek a candidate who is curious about how AI-driven autonomous systems shape business outcomes — comfortable interrogating model inputs, challenging assumptions, and asking "is this optimizing for the right thing?" You build trust quickly, partner closely with technical and business leaders, and know how to show up as a strategic equal at the table. You're comfortable operating at multiple altitudes — equally at ease with a data model as you are presenting to a VP.

Key job responsibilities
- Partner with Science and Product teams to develop financial strategies and drive controllership across RoW Automated Inventory Management systems, ensuring technology investments deliver maximum long-term free cash flow and measurable improvements to supply chain efficiency across markets ranging from early-stage builds in AMET to accelerating system maturity in Japan and India
- Navigate high degrees of ambiguity to build financial models that evaluate technology investments in markets at varying stages of maturity — from India, which is undergoing significant network transformation, to Japan, which is scaling rapidly, to AMET, a regional team in its second year of operation with significant growth ahead
- Conduct rigorous financial assessments of identified inventory defects — including entitlement analysis, estimation accuracy, and opportunity costs — translating findings into measurable P&L impact across the network
- Build and maintain metrics and audit mechanisms to evaluate algorithmic decision outcomes in RoW markets, flagging when models underperform and surfacing data-driven recommendations to course-correct
- Develop compelling narratives and financial analyses for regional and global executive reviews
- Leverage AI agents, GenAI assistants, and AI-powered data platforms to accelerate analysis, improve productivity, and continuously explore new ways to deliver higher-quality insights faster

A day in the life
This role sits at the intersection of finance, technology, and supply chain strategy. You'll spend your time working shoulder-to-shoulder with operations research scientists, product managers, and engineers — engaging in model design discussions, stress-testing algorithmic assumptions, and translating system behavior into financial narratives that drive strategic decisions. No two days look the same: one day you're building a financial framework to evaluate a new algorithm with an engineer; the next you're presenting findings in a VP-level review where the outcome shapes how Amazon invests in its inventory infrastructure.

About the team
This role sits at the intersection of finance, technology, and supply chain strategy across some of Amazon's most dynamic and fast-growing markets. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with regional operations research scientists, product managers, and engineers — engaging in model design discussions, stress-testing algorithmic assumptions, and translating system behavior into financial narratives that drive strategic decisions. The problems here are less defined than in mature markets — systems are being extended, launched, and adapted for the first time — which means you'll have real influence over how Amazon builds its inventory infrastructure in these regions. One day you're evaluating the financial case for a new system launch in India; the next you're shaping the financial framework for how Amazon expands its supply chain operations in AMET, or stress-testing assumptions behind Japan's next wave of automation. No two days look the same.
The culture is direct, curious, and intellectually honest. We work shoulder-to-shoulder with scientists, engineers, and product managers, ask hard questions, and show up as strategic equals.

- 5+ years of tax, finance or a related analytical field experience
- 4+ years of creating process improvements with automation and analysis experience
- 4+ years of dissecting financial data and identifying patterns that support business strategy experience
- Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, economics, or a related analytical field (e.g., engineering, math, computer science)
Preferred qualifications:
- 6+ years of identifying incomplete or inaccurate data, identifying the root cause and creating/implementing an escalation plan experience
- 6+ years of solving complex business challenges by delivering accurate and timely financial models, analysis, and recommendations that have a proven impact on business (e.g., financial savings, operational improvements, or customer benefits) experience

- Experience working within a global company, with multi-country responsibilities

jobs.title: Sr. Industrial Engineer, Robotics Manufacturing & Operational Excellence
jobs.description:
As a Senior Industrial Engineer for Robotics Manufacturing & Operational Excellence, you will define and lead the next generation of manufacturing operating systems across Amazon Robotics' production sites. This is not a traditional industrial engineering role — you will merge deep technical expertise in factory operations and lean systems with strategic continuous improvement leadership, serving as the architect of our Operational Excellence operating model and the driving force behind a culture of relentless improvement.
You will lead an Operational Excellence Council, work with and coach a team of Industrial and CI engineers, and champion digital lean practices that transform how we manufacture robotics at scale. If you thrive at the intersection of systems thinking, change leadership, and manufacturing innovation — and want to shape the future of robotics production — this role is for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead the design, deployment, and governance of the Operational Excellence Operating System across manufacturing sites, integrating daily management, standard work, visual management, and tiered accountability structures.
- Champion continuous improvement as a cultural transformation — acting as a change agent who partners with site leaders and managers to adopt and sustain new best practices, behaviors, and mindsets across the workforce.
- Establish and lead an Operational Excellence Council with a team of Industrial and CI engineers, setting strategic direction, prioritizing improvement initiatives, and ensuring alignment to business objectives.
- Drive digital lean transformation by leveraging data analytics, digital tools, and connected systems to enable real-time performance visibility, predictive insights, and automated waste identification across production operations.
- Design and optimize manufacturing systems including process workflows, facility layouts, production line balancing, material flow, and capacity planning to maximize throughput, quality, and space utilization.
- Develop and deploy the CI roadmap — facilitating kaizen events, value stream mapping, A3 problem solving, and structured improvement projects that deliver measurable impact to safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC) metrics.

A day in the life
You start your day reviewing real-time production performance dashboards, identifying emerging trends and opportunities. You participate in a tiered daily management review with site leadership, coaching managers on root cause thinking and countermeasure development. Mid-morning, you lead a cross-functional kaizen event focused on reducing changeover time for a new product introduction line.
In the afternoon, you work with your team of CI engineers to refine the digital lean roadmap — evaluating new tools for automated time studies and digital standard work. You close the day preparing a strategic update for the Operational Excellence Council, synthesizing improvement results and proposing the next quarter's priority initiatives. Throughout, you are on the floor — observing, coaching, and reinforcing the behaviors that build a sustainable improvement culture.

About the team
The Robotics Manufacturing & Technical Operations (RMTO) organization is Amazon Robotics' manufacturing arm for industrial robotics. We manufacture high-quality robotics for fulfillment and transportation centers across Amazon's global network. Our operation works cross-functionally with Hardware Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management teams to deliver products that directly enable Amazon's customer promise.
Our team is building a world-class manufacturing operating system grounded in digital lean principles, data-driven decision making, and continuous improvement culture. We are scaling rapidly, introducing new products, and transforming our production systems to meet the demands of a growing robotics portfolio.

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a foreign equivalent
- Experience with complex MHE and packaging lines or process design based on Lean Manufacturing or Toyota Manufacturing System
- Experience leading engineering design projects and interacting with cross-functional teams
- Experience developing and deploying an operating system or management system framework (e.g., tiered daily management, leader standard work, visual management, KPI governance).
Preferred qualifications:
- Master's degree in Engineering (any domain), Operations, Business Administration, or a related field
- Experience in management of engineering design projects
- Lean-Six Sigma Black Belt certification
- Experience with digital lean tools and Industry 4.0 technologies including IoT-enabled performance monitoring, digital standard work platforms, automated time study tools, or manufacturing execution systems (MES).

jobs.title: Sr. Worldwide Program Manager, Data & AI GTM
jobs.description:
This isn't your typical program management role. You'll be the person who ensures the infrastructure behind AWS's Data & AI sales plays actually works, and works well. That means holding a high bar on sales play templates, bill of materials quality, reporting, and content management so that everything the AWS sales field touches is accurate, up-to-date, and ready to drive impact. You'll own and continuously improve the knowledge base of sales plays, reusable content, and industry use cases that enables our sellers, and the agentic experiences that assist them, to help customers faster and more effectively. Think of this role as running the center of excellence for Data & AI sales plays: setting the standard, maintaining the system, and making sure what we put in front of AWS field teams and assistance agents is always sharp and current.

You'll drive global GTM initiatives from the ground up, identifying where the biggest opportunities are, packaging them into repeatable motions, and making sure they land with impact across regions and industries. If a sales team in financial services needs a sharper AI use case to unlock a deal, or if healthcare needs a data play that resonates with CIOs, that's your infrastructure and content showing up in the field.

What makes this role different is the scope and the leverage. You're not supporting one team or one product. You're shaping how AWS's entire Data & AI story gets organized, maintained, and delivered across the globe. You'll work across product, business development, solutions architecture, marketing, sales, and partner teams to make that happen, and you'll see your impact in real numbers: pipeline created, deals accelerated, revenue driven.

If you like building systems that scale, thrive in ambiguity, and want to work at the intersection of program rigor and GTM execution in one of the fastest-moving spaces in tech, this is the job.

Key job responsibilities
-Serve as the center of excellence for Data & AI sales plays, setting and enforcing standards for sales play templates, completion, bills of materials, use case documentation, content management, and quality across the portfolio

-Own and continuously improve the knowledge base of sales plays, reusable content, and industry use cases that enables our sales field and assistance agents to help customers more effectively

-Influence cross-functional teams to design, build, and scale repeatable sales plays while driving a high bar for bills of materials that directly address friction points in the customer sales cycle, delivered through both traditional methods and agentic experiences

-Manage sales play and use case reporting, tracking performance metrics like pipeline generated, sales acceleration, and win/revenue realization rates, and continuously iterating based on what the data and anecdotes tell you

-Help develop industry-focused use cases (e.g., financial services, healthcare, manufacturing) that show customers exactly how AWS Data & AI solves their specific challenges

-Partner cross-functionally with product, solutions architecture, marketing, sales, and partner teams to ensure GTM initiatives are aligned, resourced, and landing with impact across regions

-Ensure the infrastructure of sales acceleration content is accurate, current, and structured to power both human sellers and agentic experiences at scale

-Drive executive-level alignment on GTM priorities, making the case for where to invest and ensuring stakeholders across the business are rowing in the same direction

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a call reviewing pipeline data to see which sales plays are gaining traction and which need retooling. By mid-morning, you're in a working session with product and marketing teams, pressure-testing a new set of industry use case for financial services before it goes live to the field. After lunch, you're collaborating with a specialist sales leader in Australia who's seeing friction in a deal cycle and needs a sharper bill of materials — and you're figuring out how to deliver it both through traditional enablement channels and agentic experiences. Late afternoon, you're pulling together an executive memo that makes the case for doubling down on a GTM motion that's outperforming expectations. No two days look the same, but the throughline is always the same: connecting strategy to execution and making sure what you build actually moves numbers.

About the team
We're a worldwide team that sits at the crossroads of AWS's Data & AI portfolio, working across categories rather than within a single product lane. Our job is to take everything AWS offers in the Data & AI space and package it into GTM sales motions that are clear, compelling, and easy for the AWS field to execute. That means driving campaigns, sales plays, field activations, and sales incentives, and doing it in close partnership with marketing, product, business development, and solutions architecture teams. We connect a lot of dots so that when a sales play lands in the hands of field teams anywhere in the world, it's sharp, complete, and ready to drive pipeline. If you like working horizontally across big organizations and turning complexity into simplicity, you'll feel right at home here.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.
Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

jobs.title: Finance Manager, NA Customer Fulfillment FP&A
jobs.description:
Do you want to build the financial governance layer for one of the largest fulfillment networks in the world? The North America Customer Fulfillment (NACF) Central Labor Planning team is looking for a Financial Analyst III to own labor plan reporting and variance analysis across the entire NACF network. This role sits at a strategic layer above site-level operations, providing the weekly glide path and narrative that goes directly to senior leadership. You will diagnose gaps in the labor financial plan, escalate structural issues before they surface in the weekly business review, and build the reporting framework from the ground up. If you thrive in high-visibility roles where you create the process rather than inherit it, this is your opportunity to shape how labor planning strategy is governed, reported, and understood at the highest levels.

Key job responsibilities

Own the weekly labor plan performance narrative and variance analysis, diagnosing deviations against the financial plan and determining when escalation to senior leadership is required versus continued monitoring
Build and refine the labor plan reporting mechanism in partnership with the Operational Finance Rotation Program, creating scalable processes for the weekly glide path and variance reporting to senior leadership
Coordinate across field Finance, analytics, and operations planning teams to align on data inputs, resolve discrepancies, and ensure accurate financial reporting without direct authority
Develop an escalation framework with clear criteria to distinguish short-term labor plan fluctuations from structural problems that require senior leadership attention before the weekly business review
Dive deep into financial and operational data to ensure reporting accuracy, deliver actionable business insights, and contribute to the broader NACF Labor Planning strategy as the function matures

A day in the life
Your week begins Monday with the labor plan call, where you own the variance story and flag issues that need escalation. Tuesday and Wednesday, you track actuals against the glide path, coordinate with field Finance and analytics on inputs, and partner with the Operational Finance Rotation Program on report preparation. Thursday is weekly business review finalization. Friday, you review next week's inputs and connect with planning teams on discrepancies. Beyond the weekly cycle, you field ad hoc requests from senior leadership, explain labor plan deviations to network Directors, and continuously refine the reporting methodology you are building.

About the team
NACF Central Labor Planning is a lean, high-impact Finance function that owns labor strategy and governance for the entire North America Customer Fulfillment network. If you are energized by ambiguity, by standardizing what has never been standardized, and by work that is foundational to the business, this is one of the highest-leverage seats in Inbound finance.

Global Logistics supports Amazon-managed Inbound transportation service offerings across Domestic and Import vendors and sellers. This role sits at the intersection of our Business Intelligence, Data Engineering, FP&A, Operations, Product and Controllership partners — building out the imports cost reporting pipeline, standardizing the definitions, metrics and KPIs the imports team reports on, and partnering with central FP&A to embed those standards in weekly business reviews, month-end close, and the OP and quarterly guidance cycles.

Key job responsibilities
- Build and own the US Imports cost reporting pipeline in partnership with Business Intelligence and Data Engineering teams, acting as the finance product owner from requirements through acceptance and validation.

In the afternoon you settle a definitional conflict with central FP&A where the same cost-per-container figure does not tie between the business review and the planning file because the denominators differ, and you update the template so the decision is enforced by the mechanism instead of by your memory. Throughout, you will balance the recurring weekly and monthly review cadences against the longer-horizon work to streamline and automate recurring issues.

We are looking for a Finance Manager to serve as the finance business partner to Prime Video Marketing across the APAC region, working alongside the APAC Marketing Director (based in Mumbai). - Process improvement: Drive automation across consolidation and reporting.

A day in the life

- You build and maintain the dashboards and views — increasingly using AI-enabled tooling — that give the business timely visibility into marketing performance and efficiency.

It's Day 1 for Amazon's next billion-dollar business, and we are looking for an entrepreneurial Finance Manager to work in a start-up environment and someone who is passionate about technology, financial strategy, and FP&A, who thinks and acts globally, and has the ability to create and implement solutions, processes, and controls from the ground up.

You will own end-to-end planning cycles, drive cross-functional alignment with senior stakeholders across the Business Development & Operations, Amazon Leo for Government, and Corporate FP&A teams, and build the analytical frameworks that give leadership visibility into the financial health of the Leo business.

The ideal candidate is strategic, analytically rigorous, and has a demonstrated ability to identify and resolve P&L integrity issues, influence without authority across complex organizational boundaries, and build scalable financial processes in ambiguous environments. - Serve as the primary P&L owner for Revenue, Gross Profit, and Variable OpEx across all of Amazon Leo, ensuring accurate, timely, and insightful financial results for leadership
- Own monthly MEC (Month End Close) reporting and QBR (Quarterly Business Review) and Annual Operating Plan planning, including variance commentary, trend analysis, and leadership narratives

As the Finance Manager for Revenue, Gross Profit, and Variable OpEx on the Leo FP&A team, your day sits at the intersection of financial strategy, operational rigor, and cross-functional leadership. You might start by reviewing MEC actuals that just landed and flagging a discrepancy between the Gross Profit deck and the P&L submission — tracing the root cause through the GL, coordinating with Accounting, and driving a same-day resolution before it reaches leadership. Mid-morning, you're in a working session with BizOps and ALG to align on OP2 target-setting methodology for the next planning cycle, escalating a $100M+ variance in AWS spending targets that needs executive visibility.

Between meetings, you're facilitating building out a new channel code structure to improve P&L business segmentation, coordinating submissions with Corporate FP&A, and reviewing a new product line's financial framework with the Mobility team. jobs.title: Finance Manager, Fulfillment by Amazon - AI Native Finance Analytics & Controls
jobs.description:
FBA Finance is seeking a Finance Manager who can do two things simultaneously: ensure the integrity of Amazon's largest seller fee revenue base AND turn that clean data foundation into profitability intelligence that drives fee strategy decisions.

This is not a traditional finance role — it's a hybrid that combines end-to-end FBA analytics and how we protect our fee revenue base, heavily powered by AI and automation,

You will own the connection between FBA fee revenue at the shipment level and operational costs across Amazon's fulfillment network — producing the fee-level P&L that tells leadership whether we're happy or sad with FBA economics and that our financial controls are working. You'll also own the GL reconciliation, revenue assurance, and quarterly inspection mechanisms that ensure those numbers are trustworthy. The controllership work is the foundation; the analytics work is the payoff.
This role sits at the intersection of all fee verticals, providing the consolidated profitability view that no single vertical can see alone. You'll partner across FP&A, Fee Strategy, Fee Technology, and Accounting.

The vision: Within 6 months, 80%+ of the controllership inspection work is automated through AI agents and intelligent workflows. Your time shifts from manual reconciliation to proactive anomaly detection, cross-fee profitability analysis, and producing the analytics that shape FBA's fee strategy.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end fee-level P&L: connect FBA revenue (by fee type, ASP band, size tier) to operational costs across the fulfillment network
- Build and maintain AI-powered variance decomposition and profitability reporting across fee activities (Supply Chain, Storage, Selling, Value Recovery)
- Perform key GL reconciliations to ensure complete, accurate, and timely financial reporting across multiple marketplaces
- Design and automate controllership inspection mechanisms — shifting from reactive audit to proactive, AI-driven anomaly detection
- Partner with Fee Strategy, Accounting, and Fee Technology teams to ensure fees are accurate, timely, and aligned with seller communication and internal strategy
- Deliver recurring revenue analytics with proactive signals for leadership; produce cross-fee margin analysis that informs fee strategy decisions

jobs.title: Senior Financial Analyst, Amazon Delivery FP&A
jobs.description:
Amazon Delivery FP&A sits at the center of one of the world’s largest and fastest-growing logistics networks — supporting a delivery operation that reaches hundreds of millions of customers globally. Our finance team partners directly with business leaders to drive the financial strategy behind this growth, and we are looking for a Senior Financial Analyst who is passionate about turning complex data into actionable insights at scale.

In this role, you will own Headcount (HC) and Operating Expense (OpEx) planning across 20+ cost centers, lead Infrastructure Market Rate (IMR) cost benchmarking for Amazon Delivery as the primary Finance point of contact, and drive key annual and mid-year planning cycles including OP1, OP2, and Quarterly Guidance (QXG) adjustments. You will work closely with cross-functional business teams, present financial narratives to senior leadership, and play a critical role in shaping how Amazon Delivery manages its cost structure.

This is a high-visibility role where you will not just report numbers — you will challenge assumptions, identify risks, build scalable financial models, and influence decisions that impact thousands of employees and billions of dollars in spend. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, love solving ambiguous problems, and want to work at the intersection of finance, automation, and last-mile operations — this is the role for you.

Key job responsibilities
Planning & Modeling

- End-to-End HC & OpEx Planning: Own headcount and operating expense planning across 20+ cost centers covering 3,500+ employees, including building and maintaining HC-driven OpEx models that translate headcount into projected spend across annual planning cycles (OP1/OP2) and quarterly guidance (QXG) adjustments.
- QXG Adjustment Cycles: Drive quarterly guidance adjustments including rate card validation, merit and band penetration assumptions, headcount transfers, and scenario modeling across cost centers — ensuring the plan reflects the latest organizational and compensation changes.
- Target Allocation & Distribution: Develop and maintain monthly target allocation models — including country-level splits, T&E budgets, and phasing adjustments — and distribute to business finance partners to enable decentralized planning.

Reporting & Close

- Monthly Close & Variance Analysis: Lead monthly close analysis, variance reporting, and MEC (Monthly Expense Close) bridge analysis — reconciling variances between actuals and plan, identifying cost drivers, and delivering detailed narratives and commentary to senior leadership (L10+), enabling corrective action within the month.
- Financial Reviews: Own the creation and delivery of Monthly Financial Reviews (MFRs) and Quarterly Financial Reviews (QFRs) — building decks, ensuring accuracy and narrative quality, and leading QFR discussions with senior leadership.

Stakeholder & Cross-Functional

- CHC Finance Partnership: Serve as the primary Finance point of contact for Amazon Delivery in all Compensation & HR Costing (CHC) communications — validating rate cards, challenging assumptions, and ensuring accurate cost inputs flow into the plan on time across all planning cycles.

Tools & Systems

- Headcount & Position Management: Manage headcount positions and cost center movements through Roster, including OpEx-only transfers, position management, and HCTR submissions — maintaining a clean and auditable headcount record across the organization.
- Dashboards & Reporting Tools: Build and maintain QuickSight dashboards and financial reporting tools to provide real-time visibility into HC and OpEx performance for senior leadership, reducing reporting lag from days to near real-time.
- Data Integrity & Governance: Identify and resolve complex data integrity issues across cost centers and planning systems (e.g., CPH rate corrections, overstatement prevention), ensuring the financial plan remains accurate and defensible.

Automation & Innovation

- Process Automation & AI Adoption: Drive process automation, standardization, and AI adoption within the Finance organization — building scalable tools, reducing manual reporting effort, and facilitating cross-functional knowledge sharing to raise the bar across the team.

A day in the life
As a Senior Financial Analyst on the Amazon Delivery FP&A team, no two days look exactly the same — but here's what you can expect:

You'll start your morning reviewing the latest HC and OpEx numbers, checking for data integrity issues across cost centers and validating model outputs before they go to leadership. During Monthly Close (MEC), your day revolves around pulling actuals, running variance analysis, identifying drivers behind cost movements, preparing commentary for senior leadership reviews, and owning MEC Bridging — reconciling variances between actuals and plan, explaining key bridges, and ensuring the numbers tell a complete and accurate story.

You'll own the creation and delivery of Monthly Financial Reviews (MFRs) and Quarterly Financial Reviews (QFRs) — building the decks, ensuring the numbers are accurate and well-narrated, and leading QFR review discussions with senior leadership. These reviews are a critical touchpoint where you translate financial performance into a clear story that drives business decisions.

You'll collaborate closely with business finance partners and cross-functional stakeholders across TTS teams — sharing monthly target allocation files, validating country-level splits, and aligning on T&E budgets. You'll serve as the primary Finance POC for Amazon Delivery in all CHC (Compensation & HR Costing) communications — validating rate cards, challenging assumptions, and ensuring the right cost inputs flow into the plan accurately and on time.

Mid-cycle, you'll be deep in planning work — building or refreshing HC-to-OpEx models for OP1/OP2/Q2G/Q3G/Q4G cycles, running scenario analyses, and working closely with the CHC team to validate and challenge rate card assumptions on behalf of Amazon Delivery. You'll own IMR reporting for Amazon Delivery, tracking fleet-level Infrastructure Market Rate submissions and benefit entitlement, and serving as the primary Finance POC for business teams on IMR-related questions.

You'll attend and moderate Weekly Business Reviews (WBRs) with L10 leadership, presenting financial performance, surfacing risks, and driving discussions on cost levers. You'll manage Roster for headcount changes — processing OpEx transfers, cost center swaps, and position management — and ensure all submissions are processed accurately through HCTR.

Throughout the week, you'll partner with your Finance Manager to prioritize deliverables, align on assumptions, and communicate proactively with stakeholders. You'll also look for opportunities to automate and improve — whether that's building a smarter model, creating a QuickSight dashboard, or eliminating a manual step that costs the team hours every month.

Your internal stakeholders include Finance Managers, senior business leaders, CHC teams, Accounting, and Financial Systems teams. Your customers are the business leaders who rely on your analysis to make resourcing and investment decisions for one of Amazon's most critical operations.

About the team
The Amazon Delivery FP&A team is part of WW Operations Finance, one of Amazon's most strategic finance organizations supporting one of the largest and fastest-growing delivery networks in the world. Our mission is to serve as the trusted financial steward for Amazon Delivery — providing the analytical rigor, strategic insights, and financial intelligence that enable business leaders to optimize cost-to-serve and deliver an exceptional customer experience.

We operate with a high degree of ownership and accountability. Our team partners directly with senior leadership across Last Mile, DEX, Speed, and R&R organizations to drive financial planning, performance management, and operational decision-making at scale. We are committed to continuous improvement — eliminating manual processes, building scalable financial tools, and leveraging technology and AI to make Finance faster, smarter, and more impactful.

Joining this team means being part of a culture that values intellectual curiosity, financial discipline, and a genuine bias for action. You will not inherit a playbook — you will help build one.
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of tax, finance or a related analytical field experience
- Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, economics, or a related analytical field (e.g., engineering, math, computer science)
- 3+ years of contributing to cross-functional initiatives that drive financial performance and strategy experience
- 3+ years of dissecting financial data and identifying patterns that support business strategy experience
Preferred qualifications:
- 4+ years of participating in continuous improvement projects in your team to scale and improve controllership with measurable results experience
- MBA, or CPA
- Knowledge of Tableau
- Experience working with large-scale data mining and reporting tools (examples: SQL, MS Access, Essbase, Cognos) and other financial systems (examples: Oracle, SAP, Lawson, JD Edwards)

jobs.title: Finance Manager, WW Operations Working Capital & Free Cash Flow
jobs.description:
Amazon's WW Operations Finance FP&A team is seeking a Finance Manager to own the Working Capital and Free Cash Flow agenda for our Insights, Planning, Analytics and Technology team. This is a highly visible, senior individual contributor role supporting senior finance and operations leaders, with end-to-end ownership of the worldwide operations working capital and free cash flow position.

At Amazon, we are working to be the world's most customer-centric company, and our Operations network is renowned for being world-class, delivering packages to customers across the globe. Behind that network sits one of the largest working capital and cash flow positions at the company, and how we plan, forecast, and optimize it directly shapes the free cash flow Amazon reports to investors.

You will own the worldwide free cash flow and working capital planning and reporting cycle from start to finish, translate complex cash movements into narratives that senior leaders act on, and drive the mechanisms that make cash forecasting more accurate and more automated over time. You will not simply report the numbers. You will decide what they mean, hold the line in front of senior leadership, and influence how regional and central teams plan cash across organizations you do not directly control.

The successful candidate will have exceptional communication and analytical skills, the ability to dive deep and succinctly communicate findings to senior leaders, and comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. You should hold a high bar on professional integrity, be energized by ambiguity, and be passionate about using data to solve big, complex cash flow problems.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end planning, forecasting, reporting, and controllership of worldwide operations working capital and free cash flow, holding accuracy and timeliness to a senior-leader-review standard.
- Author the free cash flow and working capital review documents presented to senior leadership, drive those reviews directly, and translate complex cash movements into clear narratives and recommendations.
- Own cash capital expenditure forecasting for worldwide operations, partnering with regional finance, supply chain, and treasury teams to phase spend accurately and close methodology gaps that affect the reported cash position.
- Drive automation and process improvement across the forecasting and reporting framework, including science-based forecasting approaches, and partner with shared services to scale mature workstreams.
- Identify incomplete or inaccurate data, determine root causes, implement escalation plans, and make sound judgment calls in ambiguous environments where data is difficult to procure.
- Influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners outside the direct reporting line, and mentor and develop analysts as the team scales.

A day in the life
You start the day reviewing worldwide cash flow and working capital performance, flagging where the forecast is moving and why. You spend part of the morning aligning a regional partner on an inventory or payables assumption, then translate it into a crisp recommendation for an upcoming senior leadership review. In the afternoon you pressure-test a cash capital expenditure phasing question with a regional team, work with a partner to harden a forecasting mechanism so the reporting cycle runs cleanly, and coach an analyst through a variance analysis. Throughout, you are deciding what matters, holding controllership, and shaping the cash narrative leaders rely on.

About the team
As part of the WW Operations FP&A team, you will join a collaborative and knowledgeable group that is passionate about numbers, data, and how to use them to generate insight and improve the business. We are the trusted business advisors who earn trust through accurate, reliable financial insight, and we work in a supportive environment where expertise is shared freely and Invent and Simplify is highly encouraged. The working capital and free cash flow workstream sits at the center of governance and executive cash narrative for worldwide operations, giving this role direct exposure to the most senior finance and operations leaders.

- Executive exposure: recurring engagement with senior leaders through cash flow reviews
- Diverse collaboration: partner with regional finance, supply chain, treasury, corporate finance, and investor relations

jobs.title: Partner Operations Manager, Amazon PARP
jobs.description:
This role can be based in Madrid or London.

The Partner Operations Manager (Inventory & Finance) owns hardware sourcing, demand planning, inventory lifecycle management, and financial planning for Amazon Hub PARP across European markets. This role is the single-threaded owner of the program's operational finance — driving planning cycles, building bottom-up budgets, monitoring spend, and delivering cost deep-dives that inform business decisions.
Sitting at the intersection of finance & supply chain, this individual ensures the right assets are available at the right time and cost while owning the financial rhythm of the business: annual operating plans, monthly forecasting, variance analysis, and cost-saving initiatives. The role demands the ability to translate every operational action — installation, refurbishment, decommissioning — into its P&L impact.
Amazon opened its virtual doors in 1995 and strives to be the world’s most customer-centric company, where customers can find and discover anything they might want to buy online. Amazon Hub PARP is growing and we are working to create a world class delivery experience for customers through alternate delivery options - lockers and pickup points. If you are passionate about delivery operations and look around corners for ways to serve customers, we want your help.

Key job responsibilities
Financial Planning & Analysis: Own budget cycles (OP1/OP2), monthly forecasts, actuals vs. plan reporting, variance analysis, accruals management, and cost deep-dives across all operational cost centres. Build unit economics models (cost per deployment, cost per touch) and financial models (NPV, scenario analysis) that inform sourcing and investment decisions.
Demand Planning & Procurement: Forecast hardware demand across countries and product generations, manage end-to-end sourcing and coordinate cross-border importation logistics.
Inventory Optimization: Own allocation strategy across new, refurbished, and surplus assets. Drive refurbishment and cross-country transfer programs to extend asset lifecycle and reduce procurement spend.
Process Automation: Leverage AI tools and low/no-code solutions to automate financial reporting, demand planning, and procurement workflows.
Stakeholder Management: Partner with Operations, Finance, Product/Tech, and Quality teams. Present cost analysis and strategic recommendations to senior leadership
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
- Experience with sales CRM tools such as Salesforce or similar software
- Experience using Microsoft Excel to manipulate and analyze data
- Experience defining, refining and implementing sales processes, procedures and policies or equivalent
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience working within a high-growth, technology company
- Experience in finance, business management and sales operations
