jobs.description:
This position requires in-role training at an operating site which will be 6+ weeks in duration. This training will be located 50+ miles away from the home site location. All travel accommodations for training will be booked and paid for by Amazon.

ABOUT AMAZON

Our Worldwide Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Operations Manager. In this role, you will play a key part in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location. You will lead and develop a team of salaried and hourly talent. You will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. To achieve this, managers are expected to provide their team with the tools needed for success while driving improvements through data-driven decisions and analytical problem-solving.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.

Rural Super Rural (RSR) is dedicated to ensuring our customers receive their deliveries and are satisfied with their service, even in our most remote area. We are a combination of operations and support teams aligned to continually strive to innovate the last mile delivery process while bringing smiles to our customer’s faces. Come build the future with us!

Key job responsibilities
- Support, mentor, and motivate your team
- Lead large-scope projects with site and regional impact
- Create and implement productivity plans through forecast reviews, determining productivity requirements, and partnering with other Leaders to load balance
- Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
- Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Ops Integration, Loss Prevention and Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
- Lift up to 49 pounds, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach, as well as continuously climb and descend stairs
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies and is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments, and grocery locations include refrigerated environments)
- Work a flexible schedule (weekends and/or overnight shifts)
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
Preferred qualifications:
- 1+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience

jobs.title: Program Manager, Ring Blink Customer Support New Product Introduction PMO
jobs.description:
Say hello to Ring and Blink. We're creating products that make homes more secure. The Ring team is making neighborhoods safer with innovative security products and services, including the Ring Video Doorbell, Cameras, and Neighbors App. The Blink team is on a mission to end homeowner worry by providing a reliable, affordable, and easy-to-use video monitoring system. We've created battery-powered indoor and outdoor cameras and are developing new products, from chip design to complete end-user systems.

The Customer Support New Product Introduction Program Management Office (CS NPI PMO) bridges innovation and implementation across Ring and Blink product lines. We orchestrate the integration of new programs, products, policies, and features into our customer support ecosystem, partnering closely with Product Management, Go-to-Market teams, and CS Operations to transform launches into frictionless customer experiences.

Key job responsibilities
• Own and manage customer support readiness projects for new Ring and Blink launches, ensuring all support touchpoints are prepared for day-one customer interactions
• Drive cross-functional collaboration across Product Management, Go-to-Market teams, and CS Operations to align on launch timelines and support requirements
• Leverage AI tools to accelerate NPI readiness workflows, including automated project intake, status reporting, risk identification, and stakeholder communication
• Use generative AI to draft, refine, and standardize NPI deliverables such as launch readiness assessments, support enablement plans, knowledge articles, and cross-functional communications
• Apply AI-driven analysis to identify patterns and risks across your project portfolio, proactively surfacing dependencies, timeline conflicts, and resource constraints
• Automate repetitive PM tasks (meeting notes, action item tracking, status roll-ups, stakeholder updates) using AI tools to increase capacity
• Identify risks early, ask the right questions, and drive timely decisions across stakeholder groups
• Clear blockers and escalate appropriately when dependencies threaten launch timelines or support quality
• Facilitate effective meetings with the right stakeholders, driving both detailed discussions and high-level alignment
• Incorporate customer feedback and support insights to inform launch readiness decisions
Basic qualifications:

jobs.description:
Do you want to help deliver cloud technology to the Department of War (DoW)? The DoW is scaling AI and modernizing its capabilities to get advanced technology into the hands of warfighters — and AWS is at the center of that effort. As a Program Integration Manager on the AWS Defense Program Management Office, you will be the connective tissue of a multi-billion dollar cloud computing contract, serving as the primary integration point between engineering, cybersecurity, vendor management, contract operations, and government stakeholders.

You will drive program reviews, manage vendor and third-party marketplace governance, and maintain the security and compliance posture of deliverables. Your work directly impacts how DoW customers receive, adopt, and operate AWS cloud services. This is also a role where you will sharpen your program management skills on a large, complex program where taking initiative and excelling in ambiguity are rewarded.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance.

Key job responsibilities
- Serve as the primary integration point between engineering, cybersecurity, and the program management office — lead cross-functional syncs and technical exchange meetings, track action items to closure, and provide program context and escalation support to senior leadership.
- Manage stakeholder relationships across internal teams and serve as the primary customer-facing integration lead, triaging government requests, supporting contract modifications, and coordinating deliverables with government agencies.
- Own the end-to-end vendor onboarding lifecycle — addendum negotiations, compliance verification, and approvals — and maintain the third-party product catalog for listing accuracy and vendor readiness.
- Own program security deliverables and vulnerability notifications; track cloud authorizations, accessibility compliance, and contract-driven security documentation in coordination with security, legal, and government reviewers.
- Develop and maintain program schedules and agile tracking boards, identify and mitigate risks, produce monthly and quarterly business reviews and executive briefing materials, and maintain program dashboards for vendor and customer visibility.

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing action items and emails from government stakeholders, then check in on progress across your workstreams through regular meetings with engineering, cybersecurity, and program management leads throughout the week. You flag items at risk and prepare for the weekly standup where the team aligns on priorities, as well as the weekly Technical and Cyber Sync with the government customer — walking through the action item tracker and closing out completed items. After drafting and distributing meeting minutes, you pivot to vendor management: reviewing a new addendum submission, triaging questions for legal, and updating the vendor status tracker. In the afternoon, you conduct a statement of work review for a professional services offer, run it through the compliance checklist, and coordinate with the account team on catalog access and procurement questions from government buyers. Between meetings, you update the program dashboard and draft content for the next business review. Later, you lead the schedule and scrum board review in a program implementation meeting, flag risks that need leadership attention, propose mitigation paths, and close the day by preparing a status update for senior leadership and queuing vendor onboarding approvals.

About the team
Our team sits at the intersection of Department of War mission needs and AWS cloud technology, managing a multi-billion dollar cloud computing contract that directly supports DoW operations. As the DoW accelerates its modernization and AI adoption, our work is more critical than ever. We partner closely with engineering, cybersecurity, legal, and government counterparts to deliver compliant, reliable cloud services at scale.

We operate in a collaborative environment where clear communication and disciplined execution matter. If you are excited about contributing to a program with real national impact alongside inclusive, motivated teammates, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Manager Operations, Fulfillment & Operations Management
jobs.description:
Amazon's MEX1 Fulfillment Center in Mexico City seeks a frontline Operations Manager to lead a team in our Outbound area the part of the warehouse where customer orders are packed, sorted, and shipped. You will supervise a team of 30-80+ hourly warehouse associates, drive daily productivity and quality targets, and ensure every package leaves the building safely, accurately, and on time. This role operates in a fast-paced, high-volume environment where hands-on leadership, clear communication, and a commitment to continuous improvement are critical to success.

Key job responsibilities
- Safety & compliance: Own your team's safety culture. Conduct daily safety walks, ensure all associates follow personal protective equipment and ergonomic standards, and address hazards immediately. Lead initiatives to reduce product damage and shipping defects.
- Shift management: Plan and assign work across your team to meet daily volume targets and shipping deadlines. Monitor real-time performance dashboards, adjust staffing levels, and reassign resources to close productivity gaps during your shift.
- Quality assurance: Audit packing accuracy, labeling compliance, and truck-loading standards. When defects arise, identify the root cause and implement corrective actions on the same shift.
- People leadership:Supervise, coach, and develop a team of hourly warehouse associates. Manage attendance, schedules, and timesheets. Conduct regular one-on-one conversations focused on strengths, development goals, and career growth.
- Hiring & onboarding: Participate in recruiting and interviewing to build a high-performing team. Design onboarding plans that accelerate new hires' learning and integration.
- Communication: Run daily pre-shift meetings to align the team on priorities and safety reminders. Write clear shift-handoff reports and present operational updates to senior leadership.

- Process improvement: Identify opportunities to improve tools, workflows, and standard operating procedures. Participate in structured problem-solving events to eliminate waste and improve efficiency.
- Cross-functional collaboration:Coordinate with receiving, inventory control, and transportation teams to ensure a smooth end-to-end order fulfillment flow.

A day in the life
You start your shift by reviewing the daily plan: expected order volume, available headcount, and shipping deadlines. In a quick pre-shift meeting you align your team on priorities, safety reminders, and quality focus areas. Throughout the shift you walk the warehouse floor observing packing stations, checking throughput, and coaching associates in real time. When a shipping deadline is at risk, you reallocate labor, remove bottlenecks, and communicate the recovery plan to your manager. You hold brief one-on-one conversations with associates about their performance and growth. At the end of the shift you hand off key metrics and open issues to the incoming manager. Your key stakeholders are the associates on your team, the senior manager you report to, and the downstream transportation network that depends on accurate, on-time shipments.

About the team
The MEX1 Outbound Operations team is responsible for the final stages of order fulfillment — packing, sorting, and shipping customer orders from one of Amazon's largest fulfillment centers in Mexico City. We operate in a high-volume environment where every unit matters. Our culture values ownership, speed of action, delivering results, and building trust. We put safety above everything, invest in our associates' development, and continuously raise the bar on quality and efficiency. You will join a team that is passionate about delighting customers while building a great workplace.

- 1+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Can push and pull wheeled dollies loaded with products up to 100 pounds during shifts
- Bachelor's degree
- Experience in English-language communication skills, both written and verbal
Preferred qualifications:
- 1+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience
- Experience with six sigma tools and Lean techniques

jobs.title: Security Program Manager,  U.S. Amazon Dedicated Cloud
jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) Infrastructure Physical Security is seeking a highly talented and motivated Security Program Manager to join our team. AWS is the leading cloud provider, providing virtualized infrastructure, storage, networking, messaging, and many other services to customers all over the world to include the international public sector community.
The role is responsible for overseeing physical security design and the installation of security features and systems including access control, intrusion detection, camera surveillance, passive and active barriers, and other security features and capabilities consistent with AWS security standards and public sector contract requirements.

This role will perform security program management in support of new data centers, a logistics warehouse, data center expansions, and special security programs and projects.

You will be an individual contributor and will work directly with the Cluster Security Managers (CSMs), the Data Center Engineering Operations Team, and other customers, both internal and external, to integrate business and operations requirements into long-term physical security design and implementation. You will work with limited guidance to support the design and deployment of physical security packages and security program enhancements for AWS data centers and supporting facilities. Additionally, you will work across multiple teams and serve as the subject matter expert to author security design, security installation and sustainment contracts, and other security documents for submittal to the public sector customer. You will lead projects and develop short-term solutions in the physical security program. You may influence and manage vendor contracts to ensure industry-leading systems are deployed and sustained.

The ideal candidate for the role will be willing and able to work autonomously with minimal guidance or supervision, to build relationships across peer teams, stakeholders, and partner organizations, at all levels, and to be able to influence cooperation without authority in order to achieve program and project progress and completion. You will have an in-depth knowledge of electronic security and physical security system capabilities and leverage that expertise to make the right decisions for physical security projects, site sustainment, and deliver results on time and on budget. You are able to solve ambiguous problems, proactively identify existing or imminent security vulnerabilities, and apply mitigation strategies to reduce overall risk. You may be asked to use your knowledge to assess processes, program plans, and operations requirements to find security solutions or enhancements for routine and unique security requirements.

Additionally, the candidate will work across multiple teams within an Amazon Security organization to influence external customers, system owners, and business leaders. The candidate will effectively communicate with stakeholder audiences in a single domain and actively participate in meetings both internally and with the customer to drive business and technical discussions and decisions. This candidate will support their Manager in AWS external engagements with the customer. The role is based in the Phoenix, AZ area and will support multiple campuses and site types in the local cluster.

Key job responsibilities
Physical Security Design & Installation
• Participate in physical security design for new data centers, data center expansions, logistics facilities, and special projects
• Manage the installation of security features and systems including access control, intrusion detection, camera surveillance, passive and active barriers, and other capabilities consistent with AWS security standards and government requirements
• Lead physical security team acceptance, sign-off, and operational readiness validation for high-security facilities in conjunction with other AWS teams
• Apply knowledge of ICD 705 (Fixed Facility SCIF Construction), ICD Chapter 7 (Intrusion Detection), Chapter 8 (Access Control), Chapter 11 (Telecommunications Systems), and UL 2050 standards to security design and installation
Project & Budget Management
• Provide physical security project lifecycle management including bid packages, specifications, drawings, code compliance, vendor management, budget tracking, change orders, and close-out documentation
• Effectively and accurately manage multi-million dollar security project budgets — own and track the finance and budgeting process for assigned security programs and projects
• Report performance metrics including vendor service delivery performance, actual spend vs. budget variance, cost reduction goal attainment, and post-installation defect rates
• Manage purchase orders, invoice reconciliation, and financial accruals for security projects
Vendor & Contract Management
• Manage vendor on-boarding, RFP/RFQ bidding, contracting, contract execution, QA/QC, and support processes for capital projects, preventative maintenance, and break/fix contracts
• Influence and manage vendor contracts to ensure industry-leading systems are deployed and sustained
• Monitor vendor performance against contract terms and delivery timelines; escalate underperformance through established channels
• Coordinate with Procurement on new contract vehicles, renewals, and amendments
• Manage preventative maintenance and break/fix contract execution to ensure security systems remain operational and compliant with accreditation standards
Security Program Support & Analysis
• Support Cluster Security Managers by providing physical security analysis and recommending program enhancements to maximize security at assigned locations
• Collaborate across teams to drive global, regional, and local security initiatives
• Author security design documents, security installation and sustainment contracts, and other security documents for submittal to government customers
• Provide physical security subject matter expertise on system capabilities, integration options, and compliance requirements
Stakeholder Engagement
• Work directly with Cluster Security Managers, Data Center Engineering Operations, and government customers to integrate security requirements into facility design and operations
• Serve as the physical security subject matter expert in cross-functional planning forums for new construction and facility expansion projects
• Coordinate with government customer security representatives on physical security design approvals and accreditation requirements
• Communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders regarding physical security standards and system designs

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we are looking for talented people who want to help.

You will join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards of safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at our scale.

- Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Ops Integration, Loss Prevention and Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
- Lift up to 49 pounds, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach, as well as continuously climb and descend stairs

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT AMAZON
Our Worldwide Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Operations Manager. In this role, you will play a key part in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location. You will lead and develop a team of salaried and hourly talent. You will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. To achieve this, managers are expected to provide their team with the tools needed for success while driving improvements through data-driven decisions and analytical problem-solving.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.

R2L is an exciting organization within Amazon specializing in delighting our customers with speed in which we can make items appear on their doorsteps. We are a combination of operations and support teams aligned to innovate for the last mile customer experience. Come build the future with us!

Key Responsibilities and Job Elements:
· Support, mentor, and motivate your team
· Lead large-scope projects with site and regional impact
· Create and implement productivity plans through forecast reviews, determining productivity requirements, and partnering with other Leaders to load balance
· Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
· Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Ops Integration, Loss Prevention and Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
· Lift up to 49 pounds, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach, as well as continuously climb and descend stairs
· Work in an environment where the noise level varies and is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments, and grocery locations include refrigerated environments)
· Work a flexible schedule (weekends and/or overnight shifts)
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
Preferred qualifications:
- 1+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Engineering Project Manager, Operations Engineering (MEATR)
jobs.description:
Do you want to be part of a team of builders, directly responsible for the expansion and upgrade of Amazon network across MEATR (Africa, Middle East and Turkey) region? Keep reading.

This Engineering Project Management role requires versatile and technical individuals with strong Ownership to deliver impactful results within:
- Multiple Business segments: The role will support both Amazon Fulfillment and Sort Centers (FC/SC), Delivery Stations (DS), Sub-Same-Day (SSD) and Quick Commerce (QC).
- Different Project types: The role will support both new launches (Greenfield), as well as retrofit of our existing buildings (Brownfield).
- Large engineering scope: The scope for this role is focusing on automation technologies (conveyance, sortation), Good-lifts (VRC) and Storage solutions (Pick Tower, Pallet racks, High Racks).
- E2E Project lifecycle: This role will own End-to-End project lifecycle for the above-mentioned systems. From business requirement to Go-Live, including concept design, budget request, vendor selection, detailed engineering, planning, execution, testing and qualification.

During pre-execution phase, the PM has 2 main responsibilities. (1) They are expected to develop the overall operational site design on CAD, influence building selection and building size, and define the technologies required to achieve capacity requirement. Their design will account for Operations, Safety, Maintenance, Engineering highest standards, while remaining optimized and frugal, aiming to design the most efficient buildings at Amazon (2) Specifically for MHE, Storage and goods-lift Systems, the PM is expected to own their E2E delivery, including developing the detail design and specify technical requirements; secure the budget (i.e. $50MM); run RFP with procurement teams; decide vendor selection; benchmark cost efficiency with Finance teams; understand individual pieces of equipment, their application, benchmark performance, propose innovation and value engineering. The PM will be focused on meeting the needs of our internal customers to deliver systems which are safe, easily maintainable, ergonomic and reduce manual labor.
The PM will thoroughly prepare the integration of these 3 key systems (MHE, Storage, Goods-lift) into the building shell and utilities (MEP, IT), with heavy interface with Pre-Construction teams.
In case of retrofit project within existing Amazon facilities, the PM is also expected to build the complete business case, demonstrate financial viability of the project, and prepare integration of new system within existing building without Operational disruptions.

During execution phase, the PM is responsible to install, test and commission the 3 above-mentioned systems they have designed (MHE, Storage, Good-lifts). This person will be responsible for the budget they requested (i.e. $50MM), quality, safety and schedule of the projects. They will act as the main interface point for both Amazon internal and external stakeholders. They will provide accurate updates and risk forecast to Senior Leaders. They focus on cost-saving while ensuring quality and performance.
They will manage multiple vendors and sub-contractors (~300-600 workers) to deliver these systems. In terms of magnitude, they are expected to simultaneously manage the deployment of multiple km of conveyance systems with WMS integration, a dozen of goods-lift handling multiple tons load, and ~400,000 cubic meters multi-tier storage system made of ~7,000 tons of steel. All this within a building under construction and with integrations with MEP and other GC deliverables. These deployments involve high risk operations (i.e. lifting activities with cranes) and the PM is expected to enforce highest standard of safety with their vendors. They are responsible for the supply chain of their material, overlooking >300-500 containers coming from different countries, ensuring on-time arrival and smooth custom clearance with brokers. Upon installation of the systems, they are responsible for testing and qualifying the system before handing over to Operations teams at Go-Live. For this, they define and lead the test plans, and extensively inspect the systems with Maintenance, Safety, Operations and 3rd party companies. Upon Go-live, the PM provide support to the Operations and maintenance team to ensure adoption of best practices and track, report performance of the systems, and take corrective action if needed.

Key job responsibilities:
- End-to-end ownership for large-scale engineering projects (Requirement gathering, planning, design, business case, procurement, installation, commissioning and qualification, launch support)
- Dive deep into technical details and provide value engineering and innovative solutions to drive frugality and continuous improvements
- Lead technical design reviews and propose design solutions for material handling and storage solutions that meet both business needs and Amazon high standards
- Create, submit and track relevant CAPEX requests to ensure that all projects are delivered within budget and best overall value
- Assess and communicate project status, drive escalations on potential risks and delays across multiple teams
- Own the budget for the scope of the project. Give accurate updates and risk forecast. Gain savings while ensuring quality and performance
- Assist in providing equipment specifications and technical support to Procurement, Change Management, Operations, Maintenance team.
- Collaborate closely with various internal teams such as Construction, Operations, Reliability Maintenance Engineering, Procurement and Change Management
- Responsible for contractor management & teams above 300 people in construction site
- Become Subject Matter Expert for a specific piece of technology/equipment used at Amazon, advising Engineering teams internationally.

For this experienced project manager role there is a high level of autonomy to manage the projects E2E and develop versatility. The role will be based in Cairo, between construction sites and corporate office, with expected travel within the MEATR region, up to 50% per year.

Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of industrial engineer, operations engineer, manufacturing engineer, or project engineer in a manufacturing environment experience
- Bachelor's degree
- Ability to speak Arabic and English. Other languages such as French, German, Polish, Arabic, Portuguese, Turkish, Chinese (Mandarin), South African local languages are considered preferred qualifications.
- Experience in managing cool chains, refrigeration equipment and installations, temperature-controlled environments are considered a strong plus.

Preferred qualifications:
- Knowledge of AutoCAD, VBA, and SQL at the intermediate level
- Experience working with and managing third party vendors
- Experience with Six Sigma, lean manufacturing

jobs.title: Sr. Analyst , Global Operational Excellence
jobs.description:
Please note: This job is advertised for Luxembourg but can be located in any of our EU sites or offices.

We are seeking a Senior Analyst to own the analytical backbone across multiple high-impact domains within EU Inbound Supply Chain. This is not a single-metric reporting role you will design scalable data architectures, build production-grade analytics systems, and drive strategic decisions through data, working across both real-time streaming and batch processing to get the team the right data at the right time.

The ideal candidate pairs deep technical expertise in data engineering and analytics with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and turn ambiguous business problems into measurable solutions. You're equally comfortable building scalable pipelines on AWS services over terabytes of data, architecting a real-time monitoring solution, presenting to senior leadership, or prototyping GenAI tools to scale analytical capacity.

What makes this role unique:
- Context-switching is the job - one week you're decomposing a delivery-accuracy variance across the EU network; the next you're building a real-time Inbound Management pipeline; the week after you're prototyping a GenAI tool that auto-generates root-cause narratives for business reviews.
- Federated stakeholder model - you'll work across Engineering, Science, Transportation, Planning, Finance, and Operations. Aligning on definitions and building shared analytical frameworks matters as much as writing the code.
- GenAI as a force multiplier - you won't just use AI tools, you'll build them: agentic deep-dives, automated narrative generation, and intelligent alerting that scale analysis across inbound speed, DEA, and transportation optimization.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and own end-to-end data architectures spanning real-time streaming (Kinesis, Flink) and batch processing (EMR, Redshift, Athena), selecting the right paradigm for the latency, volume, and criticality at hand.
- Build production-grade, scalable ETL/ELT pipelines processing multi-TB datasets daily across Redshift, Athena, S3, and DynamoDB with data-quality checks, monitoring, and alerting.
- Architect real-time analytics for operational monitoring: live visibility into inbound flows, delivery accuracy, dock congestion, and network disruptions.
- Own metric frameworks and reporting: design KPIs, build automated dashboards (QuickSight), support WBR/MBR narratives, and own the “why” through root-cause analysis when metrics move.
- Develop GenAI-driven tooling and agentic workflows that automate reporting narratives and root-cause analysis, reducing time-to-insight from days to minutes.
- Drive deep-dive investigations across complex, multi-source datasets tracing issues to specific products, warehouses, or routes, then quantifying network-wide impact with statistical methods.

A day in the life
You'll have exposure to the full data-product lifecycle — from defining metrics to designing architectures, building pipelines, and delivering insights to senior leadership. A typical week might include:
- Designing pipelines that unify real-time event streams (shipment scans, trailer movements, inventory updates) and batch sources (forecasts, historical performance) into a single analytical layer.
- Writing advanced SQL across multiple sources to investigate why delivery promises were missed from the customer order through placement, transportation, and fulfillment.
- Building Python-based automation for anomaly detection, statistical modeling, and reporting.
- Iterating on GenAI-powered tools and presenting data-driven recommendations, with clear quantification of customer and cost impact, to senior leadership.
- Triaging emerging operational issues from real-time dashboards and providing data-backed context.

About the team
The Global Operational Excellence (GOX) team drives operational improvements across Amazon’s EU fulfillment network and ROW. We work at the intersection of technology and operations to optimize how inventory is placed, moved, and delivered reducing costs while improving customer experience. Our team leverages large-scale data analysis, automation, and cross-functional collaboration to solve complex supply chain challenges across Inbound Speed, Delivery Estimate Accuracy (DEA), and network performance.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, data science, computer science, economics, engineering, or operations research.
- Experience in analytics, data engineering, or business intelligence at a large-scale enterprise, including data-warehouse architecture, data modeling, and ETL/ELT pipeline design.
- Advanced SQL and programming (Python or equivalent) to extract, transform, and clean large (multi-TB) datasets, plus scripting for pipeline automation and scheduling.
- Experience with both real-time streaming (e.g., Kinesis, Kafka, Flink) and batch processing (e.g., EMR, Hive) systems, and with data-visualization tools (QuickSight, Tableau, or similar).
- Experience translating operational problems into analytical solutions and communicating results to senior leadership (Director/VP) with clear business-impact quantification.
Preferred qualifications:
- Master's degree in statistics, data science, computer science, operations research, or an equivalent quantitative field.
- Experience with AWS services including S3, Redshift, Athena, EMR, Kinesis, Lambda, Glue, Step Functions, SageMaker, and DynamoDB.
- Experience with GenAI/LLM integration - building AI-assisted analytical tools, prompt engineering, RAG architectures, or agentic workflows.
- Experience with statistical analysis and experimentation (design of experiments, causal inference, A/B testing) and ML/data-mining pipelines.
- Knowledge of supply-chain operations (inventory placement, network optimization, transportation, fulfillment) and Amazon internal data systems (Andes/Redshift, Cradle, Data Central, EDX).

Amazon is an equal opportunities employer. We believe passionately that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We make recruiting decisions based on your experience and skills. We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build. Protecting your privacy and the security of your data is a longstanding top priority for Amazon. Please consult our Privacy Notice ( https://www.amazon.jobs/en/privacy_page ) to know more about how we collect, use and transfer the personal data of our candidates.

If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

Amazon reserves the right to offer a higher base salary, depending on the candidate's skills, competencies, and experience. Amazon's package may include a sign on payment. In addition, the candidate may be eligible to participate in a restricted stock unit scheme operated independently by Amazon.com Inc. in USA. jobs.title: Sr Program Manager, North America Selection Strategy
jobs.description:
The Sr. Program Manager for NAS Selection owns the end-to-end program cadence and operational mechanisms that drive selection strategy across North America Retail. This role operates within a VP-level organization, coordinating across 6+ VP organizations and multiple category and technology teams to deliver selection coverage, competitive benchmarking, and gap-closure outcomes at scale.

Key job responsibilities
• Program Ownership: Own the lifecycle of complex, cross-functional selection programs, including Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), sprint planning, and Subject Matter Expert coordination. Author QBR narratives and present findings to L10+ leadership.
• Cross-Org Coordination: Align priorities, secure commitments, and drive execution across 6+ VP organizations, category teams, and technology partners. Negotiate resources and unblock teams to increase speed of delivery.
• Strategic Initiative Management: Own flagship strategic goals (e.g., Key SIC competitive coverage), converting goals from red to green through stakeholder influence, data-driven strategy, and systematic execution.
• Process Improvement & Automation: Identify, design, and implement mechanisms that move work from manual tracking to automated remediation (e.g., CBR methodology automation, SIC integration into RBS automation). Streamline and simplify processes for predictable delivery.
• Metrics & Reporting: Define and maintain P0 metrics, establish data quality standards, and build audit mechanisms to track program health and selection outcomes.
• Stakeholder Communication: Drive detailed discussions and high-level alignment with leadership, category teams, and tech partners. Produce clear, concise documents (narratives, status reports, PR/FAQs). Contribute to OP1/OP2.

A day in the life
Your morning starts by assessing priorities and keeping the right people aligned on milestones. By mid-morning, you're leading cross-org syncs, aligning teams on sprint priorities and clearing the path forward. Afternoons shift to writing mode, shaping QBR docs, pulling metrics, and pressure-testing your narrative before it reaches senior leadership. The rest of your day moves between strategic work (like scoping a new automation) and tactical follow-through (confirming timelines, tightening definitions). No two days look the same, but this role always comes back to influencing without authority, writing clearly through ambiguity, and driving programs toward measurable outcomes.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree
- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience in verbal and written communication for executive level leaders
- Experience in automation or monitoring frameworks, deployment or development
- Experience building cross-functional partnerships and influencing stakeholders across the organization to act without having a direct reporting relationship
Preferred qualifications:
- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
- Experience with advanced use of SQL for data mining and business intelligence

jobs.description:
Operations is the beating heart of Amazon. This key part of our business makes sure we fulfil and dispatch orders efficiently so that our customers get their items on time. It’s driven by Operations Managers who bring the team together to push excellence in safety, quality and productivity across our sites. At your site, you’ll lead other managers and create the operational plan that helps your teams meet their targets. This role is all about driving operational excellence to create the Amazon of tomorrow.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage and develop a team of Area Managers
- Lead operational teams on a shift, deal with issues, and positively impact site performance
- Analyse shift performance against relevant business objectives, and put in place actions to improve our operational excellence
- Work closely with other support teams, including HR, Finance, Health and Safety, and Security
- Design and deliver initiatives across the sites to improve operational performance

A day in the life
You’ll lead shifts at one of our operational sites. You’ll also be the key link between a number of teams, including finance, safety and operations integration teams. That means you’ll be close to the day-to-day operations at your site but also contribute to new ways to innovate at your site.

A typical day will involve meetings with different areas of the business, deep diving into performance and risk metrics for sites, and looking ahead to prepare for different levels of demand. Every day will also involve mentoring and coaching your team. You’ll be a source of leadership and support your team to be the best managers they can be.

Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles ‘last mile’ delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses. We utilise creative thinking and continuous improvement initiatives to get millions of physical products into the hands of our customers. Our goal is to make our customers’ delivery experience as smooth as possible and roll out global delivery solutions for our newest concepts, like Amazon Fresh, Prime Now and Amazon Restaurants.

There are two sides to what we do. Our ‘under the roof’ associates process millions of products for dispatch to our delivery teams. Our team is people-focused and supportive, particularly as lots of our people work through the night. We focus mostly on operations, with 24/7 shifts in most of our locations.

Meanwhile, our ‘on the road’ people work with Amazon Flex - a network of delivery contractors. Every year, we continually raise the bar for customer experience with new, innovative delivery services. We look for new ways to overcome industry wide logistics challenges and new ideas to reduce our carbon footprint, supported by a portfolio of cutting-edge vehicles (including Electric Vehicles) and technology to help us do just that.

jobs.title: Manager, Program Management, Brand Protection
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about protecting the world's most recognized brands and ensuring customers can shop with confidence on Amazon? Join the Intellectual Property Protections (IPP) team — the central hub for addressing complex brand protection challenges across Amazon's global marketplace.

The IPP team designs and builds high-performance systems leveraging machine learning and cross-functional collaboration to identify, prevent, and remediate intellectual property abuse on behalf of rights owners worldwide. As the single-threaded owner for end-to-end brand protection solutions, IPP ingests and prioritizes critical brand pain points, conducts comprehensive root cause analysis, develops sustainable mechanisms, and drives continuous improvement across Amazon's brand protection ecosystem.

We are seeking a strategic, experienced Manager, Program Management to lead a team of program managers responsible for the strategy, execution, and cross-organizational integration of Brand Protection programs. This is a hybrid people-leadership and program-delivery role and you will own the performance, growth, and delivery output of your team while individually driving high-impact programs that turn reactive enforcement into proactive, scalable prevention, directly reducing brand abuse for rights owners globally.

This role operates in ambiguous, cross-functional environments where problem definition and strategy are not always predetermined. You will shape the direction of your team's work, define what success looks like, and build the organizational capability to deliver with senior leadership visibility.

This is a global role requiring effective communication and understanding of the diverse needs of international brands, operational teams, and stakeholders across countries.

Key job responsibilities
1. Lead and develop a team of program managers, setting clear expectations, providing direct and constructive feedback, and coaching each team member to operate at the top of their level.
2. Build a high-performing team culture centered on ownership, bias for action, and customer obsession fostering an environment where PgMs can tackle ambiguous, high-stakes problems independently.
3. Establish team-level mechanisms (e.g., weekly business reviews, program health checks, retrospectives) that drive operational rigor and continuous improvement.
4. Develop and execute comprehensive strategies to address complex, high-ambiguity brand protection challenges, owning the most critical and cross-cutting programs.
5. Analyze defect trends, abuse patterns, policy gaps, and process inefficiencies to design scalable mechanisms that support evolving business needs and strengthen Amazon's enforcement posture.
6. Establish key mechanisms, dashboards, and self-service tooling that eliminate manual dependencies and enhance Amazon's brand protection capabilities at scale.

jobs.location: Pasay City, National Capital Region, PHL
jobs.description:
The SPIV In Person Investigations [IPI] team is responsible for removing the incentive for Bad Actors while accurately and fairly paying millions of third-party sellers along with disrupting the bad actor flywheel and change the economics of abuse within our store. The team works to ensure that bad actors cannot profit from using our services to abuse customers, selling partners and Amazon. While we obsess over customers, we specialize in obsessing over bad actors to identify their friction points and multiply them exponentially in ways that don’t impact good sellers. jobs.description:
Operations is the beating heart of Amazon. This key part of our business makes sure we fulfill and dispatch orders efficiently so that our customers get their items on time. It’s driven by Operations Managers who bring the team together to push excellence in safety, quality and productivity across our sites. At your site, you’ll lead other managers and create the operational plan that helps your teams meet their targets. With the help of emerging technology, we’re always looking for ways to offer a bigger, better product range – delivered quickly and affordably.

Our centres are sometimes referred to as the ‘First Mile’ because it’s where most Amazon packages start their journey. jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, Talent Acquisition Learning
jobs.description:
The Global Talent Acquisition (GTA) Learning team is seeking a Sr. Program Manager, Knowledge Management to own the establishment of a knowledge management system in PXT's Create Once, Reuse Everywhere (COREx) system, supporting an initiative to certify 100% of GTA standard work content in COREx for AI assistant consumption. This role is the operational engine of that mission: driving migration execution, enforcing content governance, and managing the end-to-end content lifecycle so that Talent Acquisition and AI tools draw from a single, certified source of truth. The Sr. Program Manager reports directly to the Sr. Manager of TA Learning.

You will own the strategy and operational execution that turns fragmented, legacy knowledge into governed, discoverable, certified content: batching and migrating content from a variety of source material, running the intake mechanism for ad hoc certification requests, maintaining the Playbook and SOPs, and driving down the content backlog. You operate independently, bring order to ambiguity, and hold partner teams accountable to governance standards without direct authority. This role partners closely with the COREx Integration Lead, who owns Aza integration, retrieval accuracy, and TA Hub evolution. Where that role ensures certified content surfaces accurately in AI-powered tools, this role ensures the content is migrated, governed, and certified in the first place — together forming the two halves of the COREx content operating model.

Key job responsibilities
Content Migration & Execution: Own end-to-end content migration—batching pages by parent process or topic, running them through AI quality scoring, and driving owner review to migration or deprecation. Keep prep for the next batch running concurrently with current reviews to protect timelines. Drive down the content backlog using phased prioritization by content pillar.

Governance & Content Lifecycle: Maintain the COREx Migration Playbook and SOPs for Talent Acquisition, keeping submission, certification, and publication standards current as the program scales. Enforce the governance framework across Recruiting Operations Center (ROC) teams, tying certification to disposition criteria (Migrate, Consolidate, Retire, Defer). Own the post-migration lifecycle, running maintenance cycles that validate the governance model and flag content needing updates.

Intake & Coordination: Run central intake for ad hoc certification requests—triaging against criteria, leading a ROC tiger team to identify owners and next steps, and defining response SLAs. Design change management campaigns that drive adoption of COREx standards, measuring adoption and self-service use. Establish the partner-team checkpoint tying Mercury publishing to COREx upload confirmation.

Quality Assurance & Certification: Operate the QA framework governing quality scoring against COREx standards. Leverage AI-assisted review to scale checks across accuracy, completeness, voice, terminology, and accessibility. Ensure migrated content is certified, accessible, discoverable, and clearly owned, with deprecation/redirect paths in place.

Metrics & Reporting: Define, track, and report core metrics alongside migration completion data. Report to three audiences: the migration team (operational), ROC leadership (status), and ROC stakeholders (goal attainment).

A day in the life
You operate the system that moves GTA's knowledge base from fragmented tribal content into a governed, certified single source of truth on COREx — owning the pipeline end-to-end and holding the org accountable to quality and timeline.

On a typical day, you run batch triage on incoming certification requests, dispositioning each against governance criteria and routing owners into the pipeline. You monitor active migration batches — nudging content owners through their 30-day review window, clearing permissions blockers, and escalating unresponsive owners per the defined path. You review AI-generated quality scores, refine change recommendations, and maintain the Asana board that tracks status across the portfolio.

You partner outward as much as inward: working with ROC PMs to drive self-service adoption, unblock complex content sets, and reinforce upload SLAs; aligning with the COREx Integration Lead to ensure certified content surfaces accurately in Aza and the TA Hub; and keeping the Playbook and SOPs current as the operating model evolves — all in service of a governed, certified, single source of truth for GTA knowledge.

About the team
TA Learning sits within the Recruiting Operations Center (ROC) and owns the enablement and knowledge management for Global Talent Acquisition. The team leads the COREx migration — consolidating fragmented recruiting knowledge scattered across Wiki, Sage, Broadcast, AtoZ, and other platforms into a single certified source of truth that both recruiters and AI assistants can trust. The team is also responsible for onboarding, skills development, interviewer readiness, and product education.

This role is one of two that operationalizes the TA knowledge management system. You own the knowledge management engine: Migration, governance, lifecycle, and intake. While your partner owns Aza integration: Retrieval accuracy, and the evolution of the TA Hub into a multi-audience, AI-enabled enablement platform. Together, the two roles ensure content is both certified at the source and surfaced accurately at the point of need.
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience with content or knowledge management systems, content lifecycle management, and governance frameworks.
Preferred qualifications:
- 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Experience leading organizational change initiatives across multiple locations
- Experience defining and enforcing taxonomy, information architecture, or content certification standards at scale.
- Experience establishing intake mechanisms, SLAs, and operational cadences (batch triage, maintenance cycles) for a content or process program.
- Experience working with AI-powered content tooling (quality assessment, retrieval, or AI assistants) and understanding how certified content feeds AI systems.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager - FinOps, FinOps PMO
jobs.description:
At Amazon we strive to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Our passion for invention leads us to continually pioneer and globalise new businesses and customer offerings. As a result, Amazon continues to grow and evolve across many different business lines. In supporting this growth and evolution, Amazon Finance Operations (FinOps) goal is to deliver seamless procure-to-pay, order- to-cash and payroll processes that enable geographic and market expansion across all Amazon's businesses, from Retail, Digital and Advertising through to AWS and Logistics, while ensuring regulatory and legal compliance. As part of this growth we now seek a Customer Obsessed, Results Driven Senior Program Manager for our FinOps Program Management Office (PMO) in the APAC region.

This is no ordinary Program Management role. You will own the lifecycle of complex, cross-functional programs that touch every aspect of our diverse, fast-paced global operations — from defining program strategy and vision through to sustained delivery and continuous improvement. As a Senior Program Manager, you will lead cross-functional teams to deliver large-scale business transformations, working backwards from the core problem to challenge assumptions, develop clear program tenets, and make smart trade-offs between competing priorities.
You will leverage AI as a force multiplier across the entire delivery lifecycle, not as a peripheral tool, but as an integral part of how you plan, coordinate, track, communicate, and deliver. From generating and stress-testing program plans, to automating status aggregation across workstreams, to producing launch readiness assessments and synthesising post-launch operational data into actionable improvements, you will set the standard for AI-augmented program delivery.

You will bring high judgment to distinguish between one-way and two-way door decisions, driving rapid experimentation where possible while ensuring rigour for irreversible choices. You will take calculated risks in pursuit of breakthrough results, understanding that significant progress on a bold objective often creates more value than perfectly delivering incremental improvements. Are you ready to redefine what's possible in Program Management? Apply now and join the Amazon team driving the future of global technology and innovation.

Who Are We Looking For?
The successful candidate will bring a demonstrated ability to manage the lifecycle of complex, cross-functional programs with considerable business impact. You will have a proven track record of delivering large-scale, highly complex business program implementations in fast-paced, deadline-driven and virtual environments, ideally involving systems development and integration.

You will demonstrate:
• Active, demonstrable use of AI across the program delivery lifecycle: from planning and dependency mapping through to launch coordination, status synthesis, risk identification, and post-launch analysis. We do not want someone who knows about AI; we want someone who delivers programs differently because of it.
• The ability to work backwards from the problem: challenging assumptions about how things have been done, questioning whether existing approaches are still the right ones, and designing solutions from the core problem rather than defaulting to precedent.
• High-judgment decision-making: distinguishing reversible from irreversible decisions, applying appropriate rigour to each, and driving decisions confidently when data is incomplete.
• A metrics-driven approach that goes beyond tracking numbers to designing measurement frameworks that distinguish output metrics (delivery completion) from outcome metrics (business impact, stakeholder satisfaction), while knowing when to trust judgment over data.
• The ability to distil complex scenarios into clear, compelling narratives and communicate persuasively at all levels — from technical engineering teams to VPs.
• A track record of force multiplication: creating mechanisms, frameworks, and reusable approaches that deliver value beyond a single program.
• Superior influencing and interpersonal skills to resolve conflicts, build consensus across organizations with different priorities, and drive cross-functional decision making without authority.

Key job responsibilities
Your responsibilities will span seven core dimensions:
• Stakeholder & Customer Understanding: Engage systematically with stakeholders across FinOps and partner organisations to understand business problems, constraints, and scaling factors. Gather requirements from diverse personas, distinguish representative signal from isolated requests, and drive mindful discussions that lead to crisp decisions and aligned outcomes.
• Systems & Technical Awareness: Understand the systems landscape deeply — automation limitations, integration dependencies, and scaling factors. Leverage AI across the full program lifecycle: generating and stress-testing program plans, mapping dependency chains, automating status aggregation, accelerating testing coordination, producing launch readiness assessments, and synthesising post-launch data into actionable recommendations.
• Strategic Thinking & Decision-Making: Work backwards from the problem — questioning proposals and testing
assumptions rather than perpetuating approaches because "that is how it has always been done." Distinguish between one-way and two-way door decisions, develop clear program tenets that guide prioritisation, and make smart trade-offs between time, effort, and deliverables with measurable success criteria.
• Solution Design & Process Architecture: Design scalable program mechanisms that create predictable process paths and ensure long-term success. Streamline or eliminate excess process, steer teams away from classic failure modes, and continually strengthen FinOps PMO effectiveness by delivering innovative, think-big improvement opportunities.
• Metrics & Judgment: Design measurement frameworks that distinguish output metrics from outcome metrics. Identify the highest-leverage input metrics, use AI to synthesise cross-team status inputs and identify leading indicators of delivery risk, and drive decisions confidently when data is incomplete — using judgment calibrated by experience.
• Execution & Results Delivery: Lead cross-functional teams to deliver highly complex, large-scale programs from initiation through to delivery, on time and with quality. Take calculated risks where bold programmatic moves could deliver disproportionate impact, use AI to amplify personal capacity across the delivery lifecycle, and learn systematically from outcomes.
• Cross-Functional Leadership: Effectively communicate with and influence senior, VP-level stakeholders across multiple parts of the organisation. Write effective narratives, influence without authority across organisations with different
priorities, and actively mentor and develop others.

- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English, and have the ability to take direction in English
- Demonstrated, active use of AI tools across the program delivery lifecycle - not just awareness, but proven application in planning, tracking, communication, risk identification, or launch coordination
Preferred qualifications:
- 6+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Experience designing and embedding AI-augmented workflows into program delivery (e.g., automated status synthesis,
- AI-generated launch readiness assessments, predictive risk models)
- Bachelor's degree, or MBA in supply chain, business, engineering, finance or related technical or quantitative field
- Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification
- Experience managing programs in finance operations, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, or payroll domains
- Track record of creating reusable mechanisms and frameworks adopted beyond a single program

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, WW Benchmarking and Scorecard (GSCE)
jobs.description:
Amazon's Global Standards & Customer Excellence (GSCE) organization owns the Worldwide Scorecard - the mechanism that provides a holistic view of operational performance across Safety, People, Customer Experience, Quality, Cost, and Sustainability pillars for 1,000+ last-mile delivery stations and sort centers spanning North America, Europe, Japan, India, and ECCF. The WW Benchmarking team within GSCE manages performance benchmarking using the Continuous Benchmarking Rate Setting (CBRS) methodology - clustering stations into peer groups and setting statistically rigorous performance targets that control for non-ops factors.

As the Senior Program Manager for the Quality Pillar, you will own end-to-end benchmarking and scorecard strategy for First Pass Yield (FPY), Stow Buffer Compliance, and emerging quality metrics across all regions. You will drive the CBRS methodology for quality KPIs, launch and scale benchmarking studies that close performance gaps at underperforming stations, develop next-generation metrics that replace legacy measurements, and feed input-level KPIs into the Risk Engine that powers predictive operational alerts. You will partner with Operations, ACES, BIE (Analytics), and Finance teams to ensure quality benchmarks are accurate, equitable, and drive measurable operational improvement across stations worldwide.

This role requires strong analytical thinking, program management rigor, and the ability to translate complex statistical methodologies into operator-friendly insights. You will manage multiple concurrent workstreams - from quarterly benchmark refreshes, to multi-month benchmarking studies with site-level interventions, to expanding quality benchmarks to new regions and business units where none previously existed. You will also build AI-powered tooling that accelerates validation and delivery, and contribute input signals to the Gravion Risk Engine. Cross-team coordination, data fluency, stakeholder communication to senior leadership, and a bias for automation are essential.

You will be a strong partner of Central and Field ACES teams - delivering operator sentiment of the metrics, benchmarking the metrics and aligning closely with their OP process, initiating metric changes, and maintaining metric parity around the world.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the Quality Pillar benchmarking portfolio end-to-end — vision, methodology, and cadence for FPY, Stow Buffer Compliance, and future quality metrics across NA, EU, JP, ECCF, RSR, and RoW
- Drive benchmarking methodology for quality KPIs — quarterly benchmark generation, cluster design, sub-cluster coefficients, and statistical model improvement
- Design benchmarking studies identifying root causes at underperforming stations, sharing best practices, and driving measurable quality improvement
- Expand quality benchmarks to new regions and BUs — adapting methodology for local data, gaining alignment, and launching benchmarks where none existed
- Own Road to CBRS (benchmarking) for quality metrics — translating benchmarks into actionable station-level insights that close the gap
- Partner with Central and Field ACES on operator sentiment, OP alignment, and worldwide metric parity
- Define upstream quality KPI signals for the Risk Engine — early-warning indicators and data integration partnership
- Build AI-powered validation tooling — cluster analyzers, anomaly detection, and self-service analytics for operators
- Partner with BIE on data pipeline requirements — freshness, accuracy, and scalability in Andes/Redshift
- Present insights, study results, and methodology recommendations to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders
- Write quality pillar narratives for quarterly publications and stakeholder newsletters

A day in the life
- Monday: Review CBRS cluster refresh — identify sub-cluster movements, flag quality KPI anomalies, prep stakeholder insights. Tuesday: Triage Asana intakes, meet operators to answer benchmark and cluster placement questions.
- Mid-week: Strategic alignment with stakeholders on metric logic, long-term vision, and network performance. Meet cross-BU stakeholders on benchmarking expansion needs for quality metrics.
- Thursday: Deep methodology work — review site outliers per Quality Pillar KPI, discuss logic changes with regional stakeholders, assess network impact.
- Friday: Document weekly quality benchmarking performance, update study progress, share best practices from top stations, field operator gap-closure questions.

The WW Benchmarking & Standards team establishes the performance truth for Amazon's global last mile network — defining what "good" looks like across 1,000+ delivery stations through statistically validated benchmarks and engineering-grade standards. It’s driven by Operations Managers who bring the team together to push excellence in safety, quality and productivity across our sites. A day in the life
You’ll lead shifts at one of our operational sites. You’ll also be the key link between a number of teams, including finance, safety and operations integration teams. That means you’ll be close to the day-to-day operations at your site but also contribute to new ways to innovate at your site.

About the team
Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles ‘last mile’ delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses. We utilise creative thinking and continuous improvement initiatives to get millions of physical products into the hands of our customers. Our goal is to make our customers’ delivery experience as smooth as possible and roll out global delivery solutions for our newest concepts, like Amazon Fresh, Prime Now and Amazon Restaurants.

There are two sides to what we do. Our ‘under the roof’ associates process millions of products for dispatch to our delivery teams. Our team is people-focused and supportive, particularly as lots of our people work through the night. We focus mostly on operations, with 24/7 shifts in most of our locations.

Meanwhile, our ‘on the road’ people work with Amazon Flex - a network of delivery contractors. Every year, we continually raise the bar for customer experience with new, innovative delivery services. We look for new ways to overcome industry wide logistics challenges and new ideas to reduce our carbon footprint, supported by a portfolio of vehicles (including Electric Vehicles) and technology to help us do just that.

1. Cross-Initiative Program Execution - Own the integrated delivery of our growth initiative portfolio, including but not limited to: Warranty, Trade-in (AI-powered self-grading, Instant Trade-in Credit, multi-category expansion etc.), Installments (integration with trade-in, affordability mechanisms), and Professional Services (delivery, installation, post-sale support). jobs.title: Sr. Analyst , Global Operational Excellence
jobs.description:
Please note: This job is advertised for Luxembourg but can be located in any of our EU sites or offices.

We are seeking a Senior Analyst to own the analytical backbone across multiple high-impact domains within EU Inbound Supply Chain. This is not a single-metric reporting role you will design scalable data architectures, build production-grade analytics systems, and drive strategic decisions through data, working across both real-time streaming and batch processing to get the team the right data at the right time.

The ideal candidate pairs deep technical expertise in data engineering and analytics with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and turn ambiguous business problems into measurable solutions. You're equally comfortable building scalable pipelines on AWS services over terabytes of data, architecting a real-time monitoring solution, presenting to senior leadership, or prototyping GenAI tools to scale analytical capacity.

What makes this role unique:
- Context-switching is the job - one week you're decomposing a delivery-accuracy variance across the EU network; the next you're building a real-time Inbound Management pipeline; the week after you're prototyping a GenAI tool that auto-generates root-cause narratives for business reviews.
- Federated stakeholder model - you'll work across Engineering, Science, Transportation, Planning, Finance, and Operations. Aligning on definitions and building shared analytical frameworks matters as much as writing the code.
- GenAI as a force multiplier - you won't just use AI tools, you'll build them: agentic deep-dives, automated narrative generation, and intelligent alerting that scale analysis across inbound speed, DEA, and transportation optimization.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and own end-to-end data architectures spanning real-time streaming (Kinesis, Flink) and batch processing (EMR, Redshift, Athena), selecting the right paradigm for the latency, volume, and criticality at hand.
- Build production-grade, scalable ETL/ELT pipelines processing multi-TB datasets daily across Redshift, Athena, S3, and DynamoDB with data-quality checks, monitoring, and alerting.
- Architect real-time analytics for operational monitoring: live visibility into inbound flows, delivery accuracy, dock congestion, and network disruptions.
- Own metric frameworks and reporting: design KPIs, build automated dashboards (QuickSight), support WBR/MBR narratives, and own the “why” through root-cause analysis when metrics move.
- Develop GenAI-driven tooling and agentic workflows that automate reporting narratives and root-cause analysis, reducing time-to-insight from days to minutes.
- Drive deep-dive investigations across complex, multi-source datasets tracing issues to specific products, warehouses, or routes, then quantifying network-wide impact with statistical methods.

A day in the life
You'll have exposure to the full data-product lifecycle — from defining metrics to designing architectures, building pipelines, and delivering insights to senior leadership. A typical week might include:
- Designing pipelines that unify real-time event streams (shipment scans, trailer movements, inventory updates) and batch sources (forecasts, historical performance) into a single analytical layer.
- Writing advanced SQL across multiple sources to investigate why delivery promises were missed from the customer order through placement, transportation, and fulfillment.
- Building Python-based automation for anomaly detection, statistical modeling, and reporting.
- Iterating on GenAI-powered tools and presenting data-driven recommendations, with clear quantification of customer and cost impact, to senior leadership.
- Triaging emerging operational issues from real-time dashboards and providing data-backed context.

About the team
The Global Operational Excellence (GOX) team drives operational improvements across Amazon’s EU fulfillment network and ROW. We work at the intersection of technology and operations to optimize how inventory is placed, moved, and delivered reducing costs while improving customer experience. Our team leverages large-scale data analysis, automation, and cross-functional collaboration to solve complex supply chain challenges across Inbound Speed, Delivery Estimate Accuracy (DEA), and network performance.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, data science, computer science, economics, engineering, or operations research.
- Experience in analytics, data engineering, or business intelligence at a large-scale enterprise, including data-warehouse architecture, data modeling, and ETL/ELT pipeline design.
- Advanced SQL and programming (Python or equivalent) to extract, transform, and clean large (multi-TB) datasets, plus scripting for pipeline automation and scheduling.
- Experience with both real-time streaming (e.g., Kinesis, Kafka, Flink) and batch processing (e.g., EMR, Hive) systems, and with data-visualization tools (QuickSight, Tableau, or similar).
- Experience translating operational problems into analytical solutions and communicating results to senior leadership (Director/VP) with clear business-impact quantification.
Preferred qualifications:
- Master's degree in statistics, data science, computer science, operations research, or an equivalent quantitative field.
- Experience with AWS services including S3, Redshift, Athena, EMR, Kinesis, Lambda, Glue, Step Functions, SageMaker, and DynamoDB.

- Knowledge of supply-chain operations (inventory placement, network optimization, transportation, fulfillment) and Amazon internal data systems (Andes/Redshift, Cradle, Data Central, EDX).

We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

AWS is responsible for driving revenue adoption and growth from the largest and fastest growing small- and mid-market accounts to enterprise-level customers including public sector. The AWS Global Support team interacts with leading companies and believes that world-class support is critical to customer success. AWS Support also partners with a global list of customers that are building mission-critical applications on top of AWS services.

Amazon's technology business is carrying on that tradition while leading the world in Cloud technologies. As a member of the AWS Support team in AWS India you will be at the forefront of this transformational technology with interactions with leading companies in this space and engineers within Amazon developing the capability. AWS Support provides technical support to a global list of customers that are building mission-critical applications on top of AWS services.

Our customer facing Support Engineers provide customer's workload review and resolve technical issues ranging from general guidance through technical deep-dives identifying and resolving complex configuration and 3rd party integration issues. Support engineers also develop many of their own tools and interact heavily with their peers developing the offerings.

Apart from working on a broad spectrum of technical issues an AWS India Support Manager may also coach/mentor new hires develop internal and external facing contents deliver trainings partner with development teams on complex issues or contact deflection initiatives participate in new hiring write tools/script to help the team or work with leadership on process improvement and strategic initiatives.
