jobs.title: Operations Manager III
jobs.description:
Amazon's Last Mile network delivers millions of packages to customers' doorsteps every day, and our Rural Super Rural (RSR) team takes on some of the most challenging delivery territory — longer routes, lower stop density, and greater distances between stops. We are looking for an Operations Manager to run an entire delivery station, owning everything from cost and budgeting to productivity, quality, and on-time delivery. In this role, you will operate as the general manager of your building, leading a team of exempt leaders and frontline associates while applying Lean continuous improvement methods to solve complex problems unique to rural logistics. Our RSR network is growing, and this is a great time to step into a leadership role where you can shape how we deliver for customers in some of the hardest-to-reach areas.

Key job responsibilities
- Own building-level performance across cost, payroll, productivity, budgeting, quality control, and on-time delivery, using data and Lean continuous improvement methods to drive results.
- Lead, hire, and develop exempt leadership and frontline associates, building a culture of accountability, continuous feedback, and professional growth across all shifts.
- Drive safety as the top priority by modeling safe behaviors, conducting regular gemba walks, integrating safety into daily planning, and holding your leadership team accountable for improvements.
- Collaborate with cross-functional partners including Safety, Human Resources, Engineering, and Loss Prevention to develop and execute plans that meet building objectives and improve the associate experience.
- Identify systemic operational issues through root cause analysis, develop solutions that account for upstream and downstream impacts, and implement scalable process improvements across the building.

A day in the life
You will start your day reviewing safety metrics and building performance with your leadership team, then set clear priorities for the shift ahead. From there, you will walk the floor to observe operations firsthand, coach managers in real time, and work through emerging challenges. You will also partner with support teams on improvement initiatives and join planning discussions that connect your building's results to broader RSR network goals. Our buildings operate 24 hours a day, and this position may require nights and/or weekends.

About the team
Rural Super Rural (RSR) sits within Amazon's Last Mile network, focused on delivering packages to customers in rural and less densely populated areas. These regions present unique operational challenges that require thoughtful planning and strong execution to maintain speed and reliability. Our network is growing, and our team is powered by a combination of delivery partners, technology, and the frontline teams who bring the customer experience to life every day. If you are excited about leading an entire building and making a direct impact on how customers receive their orders, we would love to hear from you.

- 3+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
Preferred qualifications:
- 3+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience

jobs.title: ICQA Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Do you aim to have a dynamic impact on the world?

Are you up for creating solutions and solving tomorrow’s problems today?

Then we have the opportunity for you!

We’re seeking an efficient ICQA Operations Manager to take ownership of our fulfillment center Inventory Control and Quality Assurance (ICQA). Our fulfillment centers sit at the heart of Amazon’s rapidly growing operations network: they are where we manage our fast-moving inventory. In each fulfillment center, our teams stow deliveries, pick products, package them up and ship them out; each of these groups have played their part in taking us where we are today.

These fulfillment centers are fast-paced and high reward environments, where adherence to policies and procedures is key. We need the right type of leader to ensure that we deliver as reliably as ever to our customers, while making sure our teams deliver on customer obsession.

Key job responsibilities
Your Role and Responsibilities in the ICQA Team:

- Lead and manage the ICQA department including; Area Managers, Process Assistants, hourly ICQA count associates, the Inbound Service Support team and the hourly damage processing associates
- Own the implementation of network safety actions and an create FC specific ICQA safety actions and compliance to the safety goals for ICQA (RIR, SIR, LTR, MSDRIR, RIR DMR); including reporting, investigations and corrective actions to ensure a safe work environment for all associates.
- Manage the ICQA team count and execution strategy to achieve the department goals (% to RO, record cleaned %, ICQA rate. FLCM27 roster compliance) while ensuring compliance and consistency with Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controllership.
- Manage the ICQA FCLM27 roster and actions for labor planning assumptions accuracy including; ICQA attendance, attrition and cross trained targets.
- Own the implementation of PXT required programs in ICQA; including ADAPT feedback, Connections, Thrive.
- Manage Area Manager(s) through monthly 1:1s and implementation of Career Growth Actions
- Own the quality strategy in conjunction with the FC Site leader/General Manager to achieve the FC quality goals for IRDR, GUV, NUV, Gross Adjustments, Dwelling Inventory, FC concessions, Concessions Missorts, Net Damages
- Own site Quality CAMP Flags and DBR/WBR cadence; partnering with the FC senior team to ensure accurate CAMP Bridges including RCA/Action Plan/Glide path are well defined and matching the site quality plan
- As part of the FC quality strategy, deliver high quality deep dive and root cause attribution as well as recommended actions and mechanisms to influence excellence and Inbound and Outbound departmental ownership of their own defect injection actions on every shift.
- Own Site Quality Benchmark Audit Program including the audit compliance, improvement plan, and execution.
- Own FC root cause deep dive bridges, actions and mechanisms for the ICQA WBR, as well as accountability to improvement in the ICQA goals and action plans
- Support the FC in deep dive and root cause attribution for the Network WBR quality flags, while influencing accountability to the actions to the Inbound and Outbound Senior teams.
- Drive process improvements and team members’ ability to keep pace with our rapid growth, while motivating others and reducing employee turnover.
- Contribute to Network and NACF level projects as a key leader on one of the network Vertical Project teams in one of the following groups: Concessions, Gross Adjustments, Dwelling Inventory.

Your Role and Responsibilities in your FC and within Operations:

- Adhere to the roles and responsibilities as per the Quality RACI
- Gain expertise in key fulfillment center process paths, as well as exception handling; we’ll need you to ensure that process discipline is adhered to across all shifts and departments
- Ensure KPIs are reviewed on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis and perform control and quality analysis on any behaviors/processes that could impact on inventory integrity
- Collaborate with all department managers to identify and understand key projects, initiatives and defect injection actions
- Liaise with Operations Managers, Senior Operations Managers, and General Managers to aid the communication of all policies related to standard work
- Create mechanisms and reporting to hold Inbound and Outbound operations teams accountable to their department defect injection, as per the roles are responsibility
- Hold Inbound and Outbound teams accountable to defect injection CAMP bridges and ownership for action compliance for their departments
- Complete a weekly deep dive and bridges for ICQA performance metrics, and be prepared to talk through your FC performance on the regional ICQA WBR weekly
- Work with Loss Prevention teams to establish, influence and adhere to Loss Prevention policies and procedures to reduce cost of inventory loss
- Support in Interviewing and hiring new Managers
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Excellent verbal and written communications skills (English)
Preferred qualifications:
- Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited university or equivalent qualification
- Demonstrated solid proficiency in time management skills, alongside confidence in organizing vast amounts of data
- Proven ability to influence, with varying levels of seniority within an organization
- A resilient, focused problem solver and self-starter, with the ability to multi-task and prioritize in a complex, occasionally ambiguous environment
- Strong commitment to employee development, as well as an exceptional level of dedication, motivation and intelligence
- Previous supervisory experience in a distribution or manufacturing environment
- Able to swiftly pick up new software systems, data analysis tools, and program management tools
- Fluent user of the entire MS Office suite, especially Excel
- Degree in a science or logistics-based discipline, with a strong bias towards analytics and data would be advantageous
- Background in a logistics, distribution or similar environment

- Experience with Lean and Six Sigma methodologies and techniques

jobs.title: ISX Program Manager, Reverse Logistic Services (RLS)
jobs.description:
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) exists to make returns effortless and reliable for every Amazon customer — no matter which store or partner they walk into. In Italy, we deliver that experience across more than 17,000 partner and carrier locations, through convenience-led options such as Label-Free, Box-Free (LFBF) drop-off and every other way a customer can return an item in-store.
The ISX Program Manager, Italy owns the quality and consistency of that experience across the whole Italian network. Because returns run through thousands of independent partner sites, the experience can vary widely from one location to the next and the core of this role is closing that gap. You will get into the field, see how returns actually happen at partner locations, coach partners and their teams to the standard customers expect, and use data to focus your time on the sites that need help most. Your mission is holistic: improving in-store returns execution across all return types, so a customer's experience is just as good at the busiest location as it is at the smallest.
This is not only a field-execution role. It carries a strategic remit that reflects its level. Beyond coaching individual sites, you will help design and deploy the network-wide improvements that lift the entire Italian network at once: in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment mechanisms, associate support and training, and the tools partners rely on to process returns. You will translate what you learn in the field into scalable programs, work across internal teams to launch them in Italy, and help shape how the broader EU standards themselves are built, turning local, on-the-ground insight into lasting structural improvement.
This is also a founding, build-from-scratch role. You'll be the first ISX Program Manager in Italy and one of the earliest members of the EU field team, reporting directly to the EU ISX Senior Manager. There's no established playbook yet, you'll help create it. We're looking for someone with real ambition, comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to focus relentlessly on the initiatives that matter most while the team, tools, and standards are still taking shape.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the in-store returns experience across ~17,000 partner and carrier locations in Italy — ensuring returns are fast, easy, and reliable.
- Get into the field and coach. Visit locations, observe how returns are handled, and coach partner teams to Amazon's standards.
- Use data to prioritize. Focus your effort on the locations and partners falling furthest behind where improvement matters most.
- Drive measurable improvement on key metrics: service speed, processing reliability, customer satisfaction, and site readiness.
- Deploy network-wide improvements. Roll out scalable programs (signage, supplies, training, tools) across the Italian network, adapting them based on field insight.
- Shape strategy from the field. Turn on-the-ground observations into recommendations that influence EU-wide returns standards and programs.
- Manage performance to resolution. Run a structured coaching and follow-up cycle for underperformers; escalate to Business Partnerships or Transportation when needed.
- Build the foundation. As a founding team member, help define how the EU field team audits, coaches, and reports, adapting NA practices to Italy and feeding insights into monthly ISX reporting.

A day in the life
You start the week by reviewing performance data for Italy and identifying the partner locations and carriers falling furthest behind on the customer experience. You spend time in the field visiting a risk-weighted set of those sites, watching real customers complete returns, checking that the process is running smoothly, and coaching partner teams on the spot. Back at your desk, you're also driving the Italy rollout of a new signage standard and a store-supplies replenishment mechanism, using what you saw in the field to shape how they're deployed. You log your findings, build improvement plans for the sites that need them, escalate the bigger systemic issues to the right internal team, and close the week by capturing insights for the monthly ISX report and re-planning around wherever the customer experience needs you most.

About the team
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) owns the returns journey end-to-end for Amazon, everything that happens after a customer decides to send something back until delivery at our FC. Our purpose is simple but hard: make returns effortless and reliable for every customer, while running one of the largest, most complex reverse-logistics networks in retail.

Within RLS, the In-Store Experience (ISX) team focuses on where returns meet the real world, the thousands of partner and carrier locations customers walk into to drop off an item. We turn a single promise into a consistent reality across every one of them: fast, easy, dependable returns, no matter which door a customer chooses. Working from the field, we close the gap between the best and worst locations, coach partners to a standard customers can count on, and build the mechanisms that lift the whole network at once.

Our culture is hands-on, data-driven, and high-ownership. We obsess over the customer, thrive in ambiguity, dive deep into the details on the ground, and think big about how to scale what works — because the best decisions about in-store returns are made by people who've seen them happen firsthand.

The applicable collective agreement for this role is CBA for employees of Telecommunication Sector. The position is classified at level Quadro or above, depending on the candidate’s skills, competences and experience.

jobs.description:
The EU Continuous Improvement Program (CIP) Manager owns the delivery of AMZL design improvement initiatives within Amazon's Global Building Design and Engineering (GBDE) team. The role leads the Design Change Request and Design Change Implementation (DCR-DCI) pipeline end-to-end, manages cross-functional workstreams, and drives improvements from idea to adopted standard with rigor and pace. Working across regional and global frameworks, the role supports cross-regional programs to ensure EU standards are globally informed and transferable. The ideal candidate combines technical grounding in the built environment with strong program management skills, benchmarks EU performance against Amazon's fastest-moving regions, and operates effectively in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the EU AMZL Continuous Improvement Program (CIP) end-to-end, managing the Design Change Request and Design Change Implementation (DCR-DCI) pipeline from idea to adopted standard
- Lead design change and standards-governance processes across multiple stakeholders, including documentation, review, and approval workflows
- Drive value-engineering and cost-reduction initiatives using structured benchmarking methodologies to challenge existing standards and define improvements
- Benchmark EU design standards against Amazon's fastest-moving regions to identify best practices and raise the quality of EU standards
- Coordinate cross-functional workstreams across the EU AMZL network, ensuring programs are delivered with precision and pace
- Support cross-regional programs and initiatives, bringing EU perspective to global conversations and translating global best practice back to EU operations
- Produce clear, data-driven program documentation and communicate findings and recommendations effectively to senior stakeholders
- Travel across the EU up to 40% of the time to support site engagement, stakeholder alignment, and program delivery

A day in the life
Indicative - You start the day reviewing the DCR-DCI pipeline — tracking active design change requests, unblocking stalled approvals, and aligning stakeholders on next steps. Mid-morning, you join a cross-regional call to share EU benchmarking findings and pressure-test a proposed standard update. After lunch, you review value-engineering analysis submitted by an external design team, sharpen the data, and prepare a recommendation for sign-off. You close the day updating program documentation and flagging two improvement opportunities identified during a recent site visit. No two days are identical — but every day moves a standard forward.

About the team
Amazon's Global Building Design and Engineering (GBDE) team defines and maintains the physical infrastructure standards behind one of the world's most complex logistics networks. Operating across multiple regions — including North America, Europe, and International (covering markets such as LATAM and India) — GBDE works at the intersection of design, engineering, and program delivery, translating strategic direction into standards that scale across hundreds of facilities globally. The team collaborates closely with construction, operations, and technology partners to ensure standards are rigorous, globally informed, and continuously improved through cross-regional benchmarking and alignment.

jobs.title: Design Program Manager – EU Amazon Logistics (AMZL) Continuous Improvement Program, Global Building Design and Engineering
jobs.description:
The EU Continuous Improvement Program (CIP) Manager owns the delivery of AMZL design improvement initiatives within Amazon's Global Building Design and Engineering (GBDE) team. The role leads the Design Change Request and Design Change Implementation (DCR-DCI) pipeline end-to-end, manages cross-functional workstreams, and drives improvements from idea to adopted standard with rigor and pace. Working across regional and global frameworks, the role supports cross-regional programs to ensure EU standards are globally informed and transferable. The ideal candidate combines technical grounding in the built environment with strong program management skills, benchmarks EU performance against Amazon's fastest-moving regions, and operates effectively in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the EU AMZL Continuous Improvement Program (CIP) end-to-end, managing the Design Change Request and Design Change Implementation (DCR-DCI) pipeline from idea to adopted standard
- Lead design change and standards-governance processes across multiple stakeholders, including documentation, review, and approval workflows
- Drive value-engineering and cost-reduction initiatives using structured benchmarking methodologies to challenge existing standards and define improvements
- Benchmark EU design standards against Amazon's fastest-moving regions to identify best practices and raise the quality of EU standards
- Coordinate cross-functional workstreams across the EU AMZL network, ensuring programs are delivered with precision and pace
- Support cross-regional programs and initiatives, bringing EU perspective to global conversations and translating global best practice back to EU operations
- Produce clear, data-driven program documentation and communicate findings and recommendations effectively to senior stakeholders
- Travel across the EU up to 40% of the time to support site engagement, stakeholder alignment, and program delivery

A day in the life
Indicative - You start the day reviewing the DCR-DCI pipeline — tracking active design change requests, unblocking stalled approvals, and aligning stakeholders on next steps. Mid-morning, you join a cross-regional call to share EU benchmarking findings and pressure-test a proposed standard update. After lunch, you review value-engineering analysis submitted by an external design team, sharpen the data, and prepare a recommendation for sign-off. You close the day updating program documentation and flagging two improvement opportunities identified during a recent site visit. No two days are identical — but every day moves a standard forward.

About the team
Amazon's Global Building Design and Engineering (GBDE) team defines and maintains the physical infrastructure standards behind one of the world's most complex logistics networks. Operating across multiple regions — including North America, Europe, and International (covering markets such as LATAM and India) — GBDE works at the intersection of design, engineering, and program delivery, translating strategic direction into standards that scale across hundreds of facilities globally. The team collaborates closely with construction, operations, and technology partners to ensure standards are rigorous, globally informed, and continuously improved through cross-regional benchmarking and alignment.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field
- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Construction Management or an equivalent engineering science
- Experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's project management representative or in other Commercial Development and Construction related disciplines
Preferred qualifications:
- Master's degree in Construction Management, Architecture, Structural, Civil, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering
- Experience in a logistics/operations environment
- Experience in program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, transportation, or equivalent
- Knowledge of building codes and regulations for your region
- Speak, write, and read fluently in French, Spanish, German or Italian

jobs.title: Program Manager, Supply Chain / S&OP, AMXL JP
jobs.description:
Are you excited to drive high-visibility, strategic logistics and technology solutions? Amazon Extra Large (AMXL) Japan is looking for a Program Manager who continuously engages across business, technical and operational teams to deliver bigger smiles for our customers.

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. Amazon is one of the most recognizable brand names in the world and we distribute millions of products each year to our loyal customers. Amazon has great opportunities to pursue a career as a leader in Operations Planning & Management. We know that learning through experience is what transforms talented people into great leaders. Our roles are designed to accelerate the growth of leaders through challenging field experiences that stretch individual capability. Our operations environment presents the candidates with great challenges in dealing with front line management, and driving scalable and continuous improvements across our Fulfillment Centers, Supply Chain & Transportation execution teams.

At Amazon, we're dedicated to being Earth's most customer-centrist company while pursuing our ambitious Climate Pledge to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040 while expanding all ranges of fleet vehicle possibilities. To reduce carbon emissions while expanding our fleet vehicle variance out of our last mile operations while increasing the vehicle, we're seeking an exceptional Program Manager for our Japan Amazon Fleet Team.

In this role, you will be responsible to conceptualize innovative and disruptive solutions while working closely with operations, tech, finance, and deployment teams to implement customer experience improvements, sustainability initiatives, and cost-saving measures. As Fleet Program Manager you are responsible for the safety, compliance, availability, and cost of the Fleet in Japan, leveraging our Fleet Management and leasing companies as well as vendors, suppliers and manufacturers in the best way and setting up a long term vision strategy with them and our Japan business.

We are making significant long-term investments in building our Fulfillment and Transportation infrastructure in Japan and scaling our last-mile delivery capacity. As Program Manager, you will drive national expansion of strategic on-road programs and work with multiple teams within Supply Chain and Retail functions to deliver a World-Class Customer Experience while working on long term Net-Zero Carbon Initiatives. You will lead fleet projects for Amazon Logistics Last Mile Delivery, partnering with tech, BI, Operations, Program, and analytics teams to create a robust, sustainable and long-term carbon-free infrastructure. That involves conceptualizing, planning, executing, tracking, evaluating and presenting pilot results for different modes of transportation that will be potential enablers for all of our business lines in Japan, with partial focus on micro-mobility solutions.

jobs.title: Logistics Program Manager, AWS Cloud Logistics
jobs.description:
As a Cloud Logistics Program Manager, you will serve as the connective tissue between operations execution and performance measurement across both logistics and warehousing services. You will own the full metrics lifecycle — from establishing goals and targets, to tracking performance, to reporting actuals vs. targets for stakeholders across the network. You will simultaneously drive day-to-day operations execution while identifying and implementing structural efficiency improvements that reduce cost, improve throughput, and elevate service levels.

Key job responsibilities
Design and own the performance metrics framework for transportation and warehousing operations, establishing baseline targets, stretch goals, and tolerance thresholds across key indicators including on-time delivery, warehouse utilization, and carrier performance
Partner with Operations teams and senior leadership to align metrics targets with organizational objectives and network strategy goals.

Build and maintain a unified scorecard spanning both logistics (carrier, lane, mode) and warehousing (throughput, labor, space utilization) dimensions, ensuring end-to-end supply chain visibility.

Reporting & Actuals vs. Targets Tracking

Develop and publish recurring performance reports — daily, weekly, and monthly — tracking actuals against established targets and surfacing variance trends requiring intervention.

Build automated reporting pipelines and dashboards that translate raw operational data into clear, actionable insights for operations managers and senior leadership
Own root cause analysis for metric deviations, documenting findings and driving corrective action plans with accountable stakeholders.

Support QBR and MBR reporting cycles with structured narratives that contextualize performance trends against operational and market conditions.

Operations Execution

Lead day-to-day transportation and warehousing operations execution, ensuring service continuity, compliance with SOPs, and alignment with carrier and LSP commitments
Serve as an escalation point for operational issues — carrier failures, capacity shortfalls, warehouse throughput bottlenecks — coordinating rapid resolution across internal teams and 3P providers.

Operational Efficiency & Continuous Improvement

Identify inefficiencies across transportation lanes and warehousing operations through data analysis, and develop structured improvement initiatives with measurable outcomes
Build and maintain a continuous improvement pipeline — tracking initiative status, projected savings, and realized impact against plan.

Develop supplier and carrier performance measurement frameworks that drive accountability and continuous improvement

Partner with category, procurement, and systems teams to align operational efficiency initiatives with broader network strategy and cost reduction goals
Stakeholder Alignment & Cross-functional Partnership.

Align with building leadership, regional operations, Finance, and centralized procurement to ensure metrics and efficiency programs reflect both site-level realities and network-wide priorities.

Develop relationships across the operations network to ensure best practices in reporting, tracking, and performance management are shared and implemented consistently.

A day in the life
You will start your morning reviewing deployment metrics and triaging incoming requests from teams who rely on your tools and reports. By midday, you might be deep in a design review for a new supplier scoring module or pairing with a teammate to debug a data ingestion issue. Afternoons often involve syncing with stakeholders to understand evolving operational needs and translating those into priorities.

About the team

jobs.description:
Are you excited to drive high-visibility, strategic logistics and technology solutions? AMXL Japan is looking for a Program Manager who continuously engages across business, technical and operational teams to deliver bigger smiles for our customers.

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. Amazon is one of the most recognizable brand names in the world and we distribute millions of products each year to our loyal customers. Amazon has great opportunities to pursue a career as a leader in Analytical Planning & Management. We know that learning through experience is what transforms talented people into great leaders. Our roles are designed to accelerate the growth of leaders through challenging field experiences that stretch individual capability. Our Operations environment presents the candidates with great challenges in dealing with front line management, and driving scalable and continuous improvements across our Fulfillment Centers, Supply Chain & Transportation execution teams.

The Program Manager will join the AMXL JP Planning & Insights program, which owns the planning mechanisms that AMXL JP's supply chain, first mile, middle mile, last mile and program teams make decisions on: S&OP and inbound planning inputs, forecast and capacity models, automated insights for weekly and monthly business reviews, and the measurement systems behind them. The Program Manager will own these mechanisms end to end, from defining the decision a stakeholder needs to make, through building the data logic and models that inform it, to driving adoption in the business review cycle. jobs.title: Program Manager III, Strategic Initiatives Team
jobs.description:
The NAMER Cloud Sales Center (CSC) is AGS's primary scale revenue engine and its most important talent developer, delivering $4B in revenue and ambitious annual growth. Early career talent sits at the heart of that engine: these sellers feed up to 60% of Field sellers and contribute an outsized share of CSC pipeline. This role owns the front door to that system.

As Senior Program Manager for Early Career Talent & Employer Brand, you own how CSC attracts, selects, and launches the next generation of sellers, and how the market sees CSC as the place to start a career in cloud sales. You will own the internship program, the co-op program, and the broader early-career strategy that shapes the caliber, diversity, engagement, and readiness of everyone who enters AGS through this door. This is a role that is strategic and tactical in equal measure: you will set multi-year strategy while running live cohorts that deliver measurable, in-year business impact.

You will join a team of senior program leaders in the CSC Strategic Initiatives Team, each owning a connected part of the talent flywheel — enablement, talent strategy and matriculation, platforms and data, and partner activation. You own the top of that flywheel and the employer brand that fills it. Success looks like a high-caliber, diverse, engaged early-career pipeline that converts faster, ramps faster, and strengthens CSC's competitive position for the next generation of GenAI-native sellers.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the early-career talent portfolio end to end: Connect the internship program, co-op program, and strategy into a single entry-point to the CSC’s integrated talent engine
• Own CSC's early-career employer brand and talent profile: Define who we attract and how we are seen, while treating the caliber, diversity, and engagement of incoming talent as a strategic lever
• Set strategy and run execution: Design the multi-year early-career model while owning live cohorts and their in-year pipeline and conversion outcomes
• Feed the talent flywheel: Partner with leadership on matriculation timing and workforce-planning inputs so early-career talent flows predictably into onboarding, development, and Field roles
• Set and hold the intake quality bar: Ensure new talent is prepared for full-time roles, accelerating time to productivity and increasing impact
• Prove impact with data: Collaborate with data teams to instrument early-career conversion, ramp, and diversity metrics to clearly articulate ROI

• Operate with executive visibility: Represent early-career talent as a named pillar of the org's talent strategy, with regular exposure to senior leadership and Field partners

You start the morning reviewing conversion and pipeline data from the current cohort with the data team, then join a working session with talent-strategy leadership on matriculation timing for the next intake. jobs.description:
The EU Continuous Improvement Program (CIP) Manager owns the delivery of AMZL design improvement initiatives within Amazon's Global Building Design and Engineering (GBDE) team. The role leads the Design Change Request and Design Change Implementation (DCR-DCI) pipeline end-to-end, manages cross-functional workstreams, and drives improvements from idea to adopted standard with rigor and pace. Working across regional and global frameworks, the role supports cross-regional programs to ensure EU standards are globally informed and transferable. The ideal candidate combines technical grounding in the built environment with strong program management skills, benchmarks EU performance against Amazon's fastest-moving regions, and operates effectively in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the EU AMZL Continuous Improvement Program (CIP) end-to-end, managing the Design Change Request and Design Change Implementation (DCR-DCI) pipeline from idea to adopted standard
- Lead design change and standards-governance processes across multiple stakeholders, including documentation, review, and approval workflows
- Drive value-engineering and cost-reduction initiatives using structured benchmarking methodologies to challenge existing standards and define improvements
- Benchmark EU design standards against Amazon's fastest-moving regions to identify best practices and raise the quality of EU standards
- Coordinate cross-functional workstreams across the EU AMZL network, ensuring programs are delivered with precision and pace
- Support cross-regional programs and initiatives, bringing EU perspective to global conversations and translating global best practice back to EU operations
- Produce clear, data-driven program documentation and communicate findings and recommendations effectively to senior stakeholders
- Travel across the EU up to 40% of the time to support site engagement, stakeholder alignment, and program delivery

A day in the life
Indicative - You start the day reviewing the DCR-DCI pipeline — tracking active design change requests, unblocking stalled approvals, and aligning stakeholders on next steps. Mid-morning, you join a cross-regional call to share EU benchmarking findings and pressure-test a proposed standard update. After lunch, you review value-engineering analysis submitted by an external design team, sharpen the data, and prepare a recommendation for sign-off. You close the day updating program documentation and flagging two improvement opportunities identified during a recent site visit. No two days are identical — but every day moves a standard forward.

About the team
Amazon's Global Building Design and Engineering (GBDE) team defines and maintains the physical infrastructure standards behind one of the world's most complex logistics networks. Operating across multiple regions — including North America, Europe, and International (covering markets such as LATAM and India) — GBDE works at the intersection of design, engineering, and program delivery, translating strategic direction into standards that scale across hundreds of facilities globally. The team collaborates closely with construction, operations, and technology partners to ensure standards are rigorous, globally informed, and continuously improved through cross-regional benchmarking and alignment.

We are looking for a motivated, organized self-starter to join as a Program Manager I on the Delivery Feedback and Insights (DFI) Performance team!

In this role, the Program Manager will work closely with senior leaders in the Last Mile space as well as key partner organizations (e.g., Operations, Customer Service, LMAQ, WHS) to ensure success. jobs.title: Sr. Preconstruction Program Manager, Prime Air Expansion
jobs.description:
As a Senior Preconstruction Program Manager within Prime Air (PA) Expansion, you are Amazon's senior owner's representative during the preconstruction phase. You source and engage Architects of Record (AORs), coordinate design completion, permitting, and contract execution for your assigned locations. Preconstruction services refers to the planning of a construction project before actual construction begins.

You will partner with internal and external stakeholders to ensure scope, budget, and schedule definition are established, including timely receipt of building and site permits. You own project budgets, oversee design management, select external vendor partners, and lead project procurement. You show excellent judgment when driving project escalations and make difficult trade-off decisions between short-term and long-term needs, defending those decisions to internal stakeholders.

Beyond project delivery, you contribute to developing Amazon's internal and external construction networks. You write effective narratives and present complex decisions and trade-offs to Directors and VPs. You actively recruit, mentor, and develop other preconstruction managers.

This role requires 20% regional travel on a yearly basis.

Key job responsibilities
- Work with internal and external teams — including Real Estate, Design Engineering, Entitlements, Construction, Finance, Launch/Startup, architects, engineers, permitting agencies, developers, and landlords — to secure resources, scope infrastructure builds, set priorities and milestones, and drive delivery to meet deadlines
- Lead coordination with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to ensure regulatory compliance, smooth permitting execution, and timely approvals
- Keep scope under control and accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and managing escalations with excellent judgment
- Own project budgets and oversee spend approvals across all assigned preconstruction projects
- Lead external partner selection, contract negotiations, and project procurement functions; ensure contracts are fit for purpose, cost-effective, and incorporate appropriate service level agreements
- Communicate budgets, schedules, project status, and priorities clearly to internal teams and external partners
- Run preconstruction meetings effectively — putting the right people in the room, driving detailed discussions, and achieving high-level alignment and consensus
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project developments
- Represent Amazon's interests in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions

About the team
If you are seeking an iterative environment where you can drive innovation, apply state-of-the-art technologies to solve real world delivery challenges, and provide benefits to customers, Prime Air is the place for you.

How do you get items to customers quickly, cost-effectively, and most importantly safely, in less than an hour? And how do you do it in a way that can scale? Our teams of hundreds of scientists, engineers, aerospace professionals, and futurists have been working hard to do just that! We are delivering to customers, and are excited for what's to come. Check out more information about Prime Air on the About Amazon blog (https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/transportation/amazon-prime-air-delivery-drone-reveal-photos).

Amazon Prime Air is revolutionizing delivery through autonomous drone technology, aiming to deliver packages to customers in 30 minutes or less. Our breakthrough technologies, including advanced BVLOS (Beyond Visual Line of Sight) capabilities and sophisticated detect-and-avoid systems, have earned FAA approvals and are setting new standards in autonomous delivery.

jobs.title: Program Manager Intern (3 months) - FY27
jobs.description:
There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon.

At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact.

You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?

What’s in it for you?

An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Key job responsibilities
You will collaborate with different internal stakeholders to learn how to improve a program’s offering and its benefits for our customers. This internship provides an opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional teams, demonstrate project management skills in a competitive and dynamic business climate.

You will work on one or several projects with your hiring team in tracking open actions, conduct deep dives, provide data insights, analyse processes to identify critical points and anticipate risks.

You will support the team in recommending and executing network improvements.

You will contribute with innovative long-term and lasting solutions beneficial for the entire team.

A day in the life
Every day is different as a Program Manager Intern. You'll work alongside your dedicated mentor and team on real improvement and innovation projects that support the growth of Amazon's European network. You might spend your morning analysing a large dataset to identify operational bottlenecks, then spend your afternoon aligning with stakeholders across different countries on a project rollout plan. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, track project milestones, and share updates with senior management.

Amazon is a data-driven business, so no matter which project you are working on, part of your role will involve extracting insights from data to drive decisions. You'll develop solutions to real operational challenges, test different approaches, and present your findings to leadership — building your analytical, communication, and project management skills in a fast-paced, international environment.

Note: You must have the right to work in the country of employment by the start date.

About the team
Intern Community:

As an Amazon Intern, you'll be part of a dynamic, supportive community that empowers your growth and development. You'll collaborate with interns from around the world, networking and participating in social events to broaden your perspectives. You can also join specialized groups focused on areas like sustainability to explore your diverse interests.

Support:

The internship program provides a robust support system, including weekly intern office hours, dedicated IT and HR support, and a program team committed to your success. This ensures you have the guidance and assistance needed to thrive.

Learning Sessions:

Exclusive learning sessions will further enhance your skills, granting you access to Amazon's industry-leading learning platforms and the expertise of industry leaders. These structured development opportunities will prepare you for the next step in your career.

Opportunities:

Upon successful completion of the internship, you may be considered for a graduate role or a second internship, allowing you to continue your journey with Amazon. Additionally, you'll enjoy a competitive monthly salary, relocation support, and access to a range of employee benefits.

Internship Start Dates across the year:

We are hiring interns to start anytime from January through September 2027. Each month, we'll hold 1-2 onboarding days for new hires.

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English at C1 level or above
- Available for a full-time internship (40 hours/week) and commit to a 3 month internship
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience working with clients
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to identify process improvements and innovative solutions.
- Excellent communication and teamwork skills, able to collaborate effectively with others.
- Demonstrated curiosity, proactivity, and willingness to take on challenges in an ambiguous, fast-paced environment.

jobs.description:
Un univers d'opportunités chez Amazon.
Chez Amazon, votre carrière ne suit pas une ligne droite. Elle accélère, prend des tournants et vous met au défi d'une manière que vous n'auriez jamais imaginée. Dès votre arrivée, vous faites partie de quelque chose de grand : créer des produits ou des services qui touchent des millions de personnes et façonnent la manière dont elles vivent, travaillent et interagissent au quotidien. C'est ici que vos idées se transforment en un véritable impact.
Vous travaillerez avec des outils de premier plan, des plateformes mondiales et des systèmes conçus pour fonctionner à une échelle extraordinaire. Vous avancerez vite, expérimenterez et lancerez des solutions qui comptent vraiment. Grâce à des opportunités infinies à explorer au sein de différentes équipes et fonctions, vous apprendrez rapidement, mettrez en pratique vos connaissances et découvrirez des compétences dont vous ignoriez l'existence. C'est un environnement pensé pour les bâtisseurs qui veulent voir l'impact concret de leur travail dans le monde.

Prêt(e) à commencer votre aventure ?
Qu'est-ce que cela vous apporte ?
Un stage chez Amazon, c'est de vraies responsabilités dès le premier jour. Vous construirez, testerez et apprendrez aux côtés de personnes qui veulent vous voir réussir, tout en ayant un impact qui va bien au-delà du campus.

Key job responsibilities
Vous collaborerez avec différentes parties prenantes internes pour apprendre à améliorer l'offre d'un programme ainsi que ses avantages pour nos clients. Ce stage offre l'opportunité de travailler avec des équipes transversales et de développer des compétences en gestion de projet dans un environnement commercial compétitif et dynamique.
Vous travaillerez sur un ou plusieurs projets au sein de votre équipe d'accueil afin de suivre les actions en cours, mener des analyses approfondies, fournir des recommandations basées sur les données, analyser les processus pour identifier les points critiques et anticiper les risques.
Vous accompagnerez l'équipe dans la recommandation et la mise en œuvre d'améliorations au sein du réseau.
Vous contribuerez en proposant des solutions innovantes, durables et bénéfiques pour l'ensemble de l'équipe.

A day in the life
Chaque jour est différent en tant que stagiaire Program Manager. Vous travaillerez aux côtés de votre mentor dédié et de votre équipe sur de véritables projets d'amélioration et d'innovation qui soutiennent la croissance du réseau européen d'Amazon. Vous pourriez passer votre matinée à analyser un large jeu de données pour identifier des goulots d'étranglement opérationnels, puis consacrer votre après-midi à échanger avec des parties prenantes de différents pays sur un plan de déploiement. Vous collaborerez avec des équipes transversales, suivrez les jalons des projets et partagerez des mises à jour avec la direction.
Amazon est une entreprise guidée par les données : quel que soit le projet sur lequel vous travaillez, une partie de votre rôle consistera à en extraire des enseignements pour orienter les décisions. Vous développerez des solutions à de véritables défis opérationnels, testerez différentes approches et présenterez vos conclusions à la direction, renforçant ainsi vos compétences analytiques, en communication et en gestion de projet dans un environnement international au rythme soutenu.
Remarque : Vous devez disposer du droit de travailler dans le pays d'emploi à la date de début du contrat.

About the team
Communauté des stagiaires : En tant que stagiaire Amazon, vous ferez partie d'une communauté dynamique et solidaire qui favorise votre croissance et votre développement. Vous collaborerez avec des stagiaires du monde entier, en tissant des liens et en participant à des événements sociaux pour élargir vos perspectives. Vous pourrez également rejoindre des groupes spécialisés axés sur des domaines tels que le développement durable, afin d'explorer vos centres d'intérêt variés.

jobs.title: Benchmarking Program Manager, Cloud Economics Scale
jobs.description:
Build the proof that convinces customers to move to AWS. As a Benchmarking Program Manager, you will create and evangelize new benchmarking studies that quantify the KPI-driven benefits customers can achieve on AWS — the credible, data-backed evidence that AWS field teams and customers rely on to build the business case for cloud. You own these studies end to end, and once they scale, your work becomes the standard the field sells on. This is a rare seat with real autonomy: you will own the full study lifecycle, including the external vendor relationship, and you will shape how cloud value is measured and communicated across internal and external audiences. You will partner across teams to understand the needs of internal and external users, develop plans to scale each study's impact, and find innovative ways to apply benchmark insights to value-based business cases for cloud adoption. - Develop and execute go-to-market and scaling mechanisms that put new studies in front of the field and customers.

jobs.description:
Join the Seller AI team where you'll lead benchmarking and evaluation of AI models that enhance the seller experience across Amazon's global marketplace. You'll manage a team dedicated to validating, testing, and improving Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) that power innovative seller tools. This role combines strategic leadership with hands-on technical oversight, requiring exceptional communication skills, team management, and stakeholder engagement.

In this position, you'll drive the development and implementation of comprehensive benchmarking methodologies to evaluate AI model performance across accuracy, robustness, bias, and reliability metrics. Your expertise will be crucial in translating technical findings into actionable insights that improve Seller Assistant's performance and contribute to the growth of Amazon's seller community worldwide.

Key job responsibilities

1. Lead LLM based automated evaluations program, Plan and execute benchmarking exercises for AI models, defining test plans, metrics, and acceptance criteria across accuracy, robustness, bias, and reliability dimensions.
2. Lead a team responsible for validating data based on specific annotation guidelines, ensuring accuracy and quality while escalating potential regulatory risks
3. Prepare comprehensive audit and benchmarking reports, including error ratings, root-cause analysis, and recommendations for senior stakeholders
4. Drive process efficiencies and explore automation opportunities to enhance the productivity of data generation initiatives
5. Mentor team members and help develop their skills while managing overall schedules, proactively mitigating risks, and keeping project scope under control.

A day in the life
Your day begins with prioritizing benchmarking tasks for your team based on current business requirements. You'll review progress on ongoing audits, provide guidance where needed, and ensure deliverables meet quality standards. Throughout the day, you'll analyze performance data from Seller Assistant tools, identifying patterns and insights that could improve AI model effectiveness. jobs.title: Sr Program Manager – Central Selection, WWGS (Worldwide Grocery Stores)
jobs.description:
The Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS) Central Selection team is responsible for governing selection strategy and execution across Amazon's grocery portfolio. We operate at the intersection of category management, operations, and technology, building the mechanisms and guardrails that ensure each banner delivers a differentiated and complementary customer experience. Our work directly impacts millions of grocery customers and shapes how Amazon's grocery banners coexist and grow together.

This Sr Program Manager role will lead critical workstreams including selection analysis and optimization, banner assortment strategy, and selection governance across banners. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented self-starter who thrives in ambiguity, can translate complex merchandising problems into structured program plans, and is energized by the pace of grocery retail. You will ensure end-to-end accountability for selection health, from initial strategy and category planning through ongoing optimization, leveraging shared metrics and dashboards across banners

The ideal candidate combines strong business and product sense with a solid understanding of technical concepts. You can think strategically, analyze data, influence without authority, and provide strong customer service support. You must thrive in an entrepreneurial environment and not be hindered by ambiguity or competing priorities. High judgment, analytical talent, ability to influence, and exceptional communication skills are essential to success in this role.

Key job responsibilities
• Develop and execute location and format-driven selection strategies using competitor benchmarking, capacity inputs, sales analysis, and market data to inform market-specific selection across banners, both online and physical stores
• Drive automation and leverage AI Tools to simplify processes and improve operational efficiency
• Coordinate with cross-functional teams and communicate program updates with internal and external stakeholders, including leadership reviews
• Drive automation and leverage AI tools to simplify selection planning processes and improve operational efficiencies
• Collaborate with cross-functional partners to deliver results in an ambitious, fast-paced environment, working across many time zones
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience with selection strategy, category management, or space planning
- Advanced Excel proficiency and experience with Microsoft Access or SQL
- 5+ years experience in business roles requiring data analysis, process improvements, creative problem solving, and cross-functional collaboration
- High attention to detail and proven ability to manage multiple, competing priorities simultaneously
- Excellent communication (verbal and written) and interpersonal skills with ability to effectively communicate with both business and technical teams
- Passionate and knowledgeable about customer behavior
Preferred qualifications:
- Familiarity with databases and SQL
- Experience leveraging automation and AI tools to streamline operational processes and improve efficiency
- Ability to analyze data quantitatively and use customer research, data and metrics to back up assumptions and identify opportunities
- Experience creating and/or improving operational processes across teams and stakeholders, with bias toward automation
- Proven track record of taking ownership and driving results

jobs.title: Program Manager, Central RME
jobs.description:
Amazon's Reliability, Maintenance & Engineering (RME) team ensures that our global fulfillment and operations networks run safely, efficiently, and at peak performance. A Program Manager in Central RME will drive initiatives that optimize operational capacity, enhance network performance, and deliver measurable improvements. This role focuses on program execution, addressing operational barriers, implementing standard work practices, and collaborating with RME, non-RME stakeholders, and Operations teams.

Key job responsibilities
- Drive cross-functional programs, projects, and initiatives impacting operations; develop solutions collaboratively with RME, non-RME, and Ops stakeholders.
- Partner with RME, non-RME, and Ops stakeholders to conduct root cause analysis, eliminate operational barriers, and deliver continuous improvement initiatives across the network.
- Maintain and update capacity models including data inputs, methodology documentation, and output validation to support capacity utilization goals.
- Use analytics for data-driven decision-making; monitor performance and escalate issues requiring corrective actions.
- Create and maintain program artifacts including business requirement documents, initiative plans, and status reports.
- Implement standard work practices that improve key business metrics and translate lessons into standards across assigned sites or programs.
- Communicate program status, risks, and outcomes to stakeholders and management; inform decision-making through clear narratives and data-backed recommendations.
- Remove operational barriers through hands-on problem-solving to deliver immediate results.
- As a Program Manager, contribute to a culture of operational excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, DC Power Utilization Management
jobs.description:
About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About the team
The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

- Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management

- Documentation Standardization & Governance: Lead the standardization of documentation across the team's knowledge base, conducting a comprehensive audit and establishing consistency in format, structure, and content quality. Ensure all customer-facing information is current, accurate, and accessible, implementing a sustainable refresh cadence with clear ownership. This project-based deliverable offers clear scope and measurable outcomes, making it an ideal, high-visibility contribution for an intern.

- Onboarding & Enablement Flows: Partner with the onboarding and enablement team to design end-to-end flows and playbooks that map the full customer journey within AWS Cloud Logistics. Translate complex, cross-functional processes into clear, repeatable guides that help new joiners and stakeholders ramp quickly and consistently.

Build feedback loops and review mechanisms so content stays accurate and sustainable well beyond your tenure.

- Continuous Improvement & Automation: Identify opportunities to simplify and streamline how knowledge is captured, maintained, and surfaced - including exploring AI and automation to reduce manual effort and improve discoverability of enablement resources.

No two days look the same, but every day has a rhythm. Your morning might start by supporting an operational task for the team - pulling data, updating a tracker, or preparing materials for an upcoming review. The afternoon is heads-down time on one of your dedicated projects - maybe drafting a playbook, building out a knowledge base page, or redesigning an enablement module. Between project sprints, you are meeting with teams across different functions and geographies to learn how our end-to-end supply chain operates and how AWS services underpin it. You also have a regular check-in with your manager to review progress, remove blockers, and discuss your development goals. Most days end knowing you have contributed to something the team will use long after your internship ends - and that you understand a little more about how the cloud gets built.

AWS Cloud Logistics (ACL) manages a continuously evolving portfolio of shipments through a worldwide supply chain. We deliver the right product at the right time, cost, and place - ensuring our AWS supply chain is reliable. jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, Vendor Management, Worldwide Grocery Stores - Growth & Development
jobs.description:
Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Stores - Growth & Development team is hiring for a Sr. Program Manager, Vendor Management position.

As a Sr. Program Manager for Vendor Management, you will set and enforce the financial terms that govern how we engage, compensate, and hold accountable the service providers who keep our stores running - and build the partnerships with those providers that set them up to succeed. You will run the RFPs that determine which vendors earn our business, negotiate the contracts that protect us when things do not go as planned, own the process that validates whether a vendor's rate increase request is actually justified, and engage directly with service providers to understand their business and create the conditions for a win-win relationship.

Every time one of our vendors shows up at a Whole Foods Market or Daily Shop location, there is a contract behind that visit - defining the rates, the scope, and appropriate metrics to support the business. This role owns that contract infrastructure across 600+ grocery locations.

Here is what makes this role stand out:
- You are the owner, not the approver. You do not route contracts to someone else to negotiate - you lead the negotiations, draft the terms, and own the outcomes across R&M vendor relationships for Whole Foods Market and Daily Shop locations.
- Your work protects the business at scale. Every contract template you improve, every unjustified rate increase you reject, and every RFP you execute with rigor makes the entire vendor management system more defensible and more cost-efficient across a 600+ location portfolio.
- You will see the spend, not just the invoices. This role comes with direct visibility into R&M vendor spend trends, trade-level cost drivers, and budget impact analysis - so your decisions are grounded in data, not just process.
- You will improve and scale the frameworks, not just follow them. The RFP process documentation, the rate validation workflow, the contract compliance tracking system - these foundations exist and you will own them, sharpen them, and evolve them as the portfolio grows.
- You sit at the center of legal, procurement, and operations. You will bring Indirect Procurement, Strategic Procurement, Legal, and Facilities Leadership to the table - and make sure every vendor decision has the right stakeholders aligned and moving at pace.
- You build partnerships that deliver. Holding vendors accountable and setting them up to succeed are not competing goals - they are the same goal. You will engage directly with service providers, understand their business, and create the win-win conditions that make vendors want to perform. The strongest contracts are the foundation of strong partnerships, and you will build both.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead contract negotiations and manage the full RFP lifecycle for R&M trades.
- Own the Rate Increase Validation Process - formalizing and strengthening the evaluation mechanism that ensures every vendor rate increase request is reviewed against consistent legitimacy criteria and market benchmarks.
- Maintain 100% contract status visibility for all active R&M vendors - tracking expiration timelines, renewal requirements, and compliance across Corrigo.
- Partner with Facilities Operations and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure preventive maintenance configurations in Corrigo align with contracted scopes of work, SLA requirements, and program standards.
- Lead business reviews with Indirect Procurement and Facilities leadership - facilitating alignment on contract priorities, RFP activity, and vendor cost trends.
- Own and continuously evolve the RFP Process framework, including timelines, Scope of Work (SOW) review with stakeholders, RFP Abstract templates, and the Vendor Management/Indirect Procurement stakeholder RACI.
- Own portfolio-level spend analysis and vendor performance monitoring to identify cost-saving opportunities - bringing the contract compliance, rate benchmarking, and spend trend data that Indirect Procurement cannot fully replicate - and partnering with IP and Strategic Procurement to validate findings and drive action.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a vendor rate increase request - pulling spend trends and drafting a response that either validates the increase or documents why it does not hold up. From there, you partner with Indirect Procurement, tracking two active RFPs through the selection process and aligning on approval timelines. In the afternoon, a Facility Manager surfaces a contract scope gap - you know the contract well enough to bridge the conversation, and connect the right partners. On other days, you are learning about new programs or formats that require new service provider support and finding appropriate vendors to engage.

About the team
The Vendor Management Program Team is the partner that keeps store operations running by holding vendors accountable. We own the full R&M vendor lifecycle - from selection and onboarding through contracting, performance management, and invoice auditing - across 600+ grocery locations. We conduct almost 100 vendor business reviews per year, manage complex contracts across hundreds of service providers, and make sure store teams never have to worry about whether their vendor will show up and do the job they were contracted to do. We are a direct execution team: we do not advise on problems, we own and solve them.

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- 5+ years of work in a procurement organization, performing vendor management, contract management, negotiating complex purchases, and bidding experience
- Experience managing and negotiating contracts and vendor relationships
- Experience using financial models, KPIs, and data analysis to inform business decisions with proven business impact (e.g., financial savings, operational improvements, or customer benefits)
- Experience developing, reviewing, and managing Statements of Work (SOW), including defining project scope, deliverables, timelines, and criteria for construction or facilities projects.
Preferred qualifications:

- Experience in reviewing, drafting, and negotiating commercial contracts

- Experience working with CMMS software, or experience in similar environments
- Experience with procurement platforms such as Coupa
- Experience building RFP frameworks, process documentation, or SOPs in a program management context

Join Amazon’s Employee Services team and help make a difference for all Amazonians! We are seeking an experienced Program Manager to own and oversee the operations of Amazon's Medical Clinics across 40+ office locations in India. In this high-impact role, you will be responsible for ensuring continuous, uninterrupted availability of clinical services — including on-site medicines and qualified nursing staff — at every clinic, at all times. You will manage vendor and staff transitions seamlessly, drive standardization and compliance across sites, and partner with a broad set of stakeholders spanning Procurement, GREF (Global Real Estate & Facilities), clinical teams, local site leaders, and HR partners. This is a role for a self-starter who thrives on operational excellence, ambiguity, and scaling employee health services across a large, geographically distributed footprint.

Note - This is a contract only role.

Key job responsibilities
Clinic Operations Oversight: Own end-to-end operations of medical clinics across 40+ Amazon office locations in India, ensuring consistent service quality, availability, and compliance with applicable regulations and Amazon standards.
Continuity of Care: Guarantee uninterrupted availability of essential medicines, medical supplies, and nursing/clinical staff at all clinics at all times, including proactive planning for demand, stock-outs, and coverage gaps.
Transition & Change Management: Plan and manage all staff and vendor transitions (onboarding, offboarding, replacements, contract changes) with zero disruption to clinic availability or employee experience.
Vendor Management: Partner with Procurement to select, onboard, and govern clinical service and pharmacy vendors; monitor SLAs, service quality, and contractual compliance, and drive corrective action where needed.

Compliance & Risk: Ensure clinics operate in accordance with local statutory, medical, and licensing requirements; identify and mitigate operational and clinical risks.
Metrics & Reporting: Define, track, and report on key operational metrics (availability, staffing coverage, medicine stock levels, incident response, employee utilization/satisfaction) and drive data-informed improvements.
Escalation Management: Serve as the primary escalation point for clinic-related operational issues, resolving them promptly and implementing preventive measures.

You start your day by reviewing the operational dashboard across all 40+ clinics — checking overnight incidents, medicine stock levels, and any staffing gaps flagged by site teams. meet with the clinical team to review a new standardized triage protocol, connect with a local site leader across India who have concerns about clinic timings/availability/Medicines. You update your weekly metrics report — tracking availability, staffing coverage, and stock.

Bringing a new AWS data center online starts with fiber in the ground. In this role you own that work across high-volume US metro markets, taking a metro fiber route from approved plan to live capacity and managing the construction vendors who build it.

You will run several builds at once, hold vendors to schedule and quality, inspect sites to confirm the work was done right, and keep a wide group of stakeholders current on where each project stands.
