jobs.title: ACES Program Manager, Delivery Experience Accuracy Process Excellence, Amazon Customer Excellence System
jobs.description:
As an ACES Process Manager focused on DEA (Delivery Experience Accuracy) Process Excellence, you will own the end-to-end identification, analysis, and resolution of delivery promise failures across Brazil's fulfillment network. Beyond data — you will connect the numbers to real-world operations, finding root causes where packages fail, designing corrective actions, and implementing sustainable improvements that protect 130M+ annual customer promises.

You will apply Lean Six Sigma methodology (DMAIC) to systematically reduce DEA defects across all owners: Planning Systems, FC Execution, Linehaul, Sort Center, Air, AMZL, and Commercial Carriers. You will lead cross-functional improvement projects, manage stakeholders across 10+ teams, and drive accountability through structured governance mechanisms.

Key job responsibilities
• Leading root cause analysis for DEA failures using structured problem-solving (5-Why, Fishbone, FMEA, FFaLS logic)
• Owning DMAIC projects targeting the highest-impact defect buckets (Planning Systems, Last Mile, FC Execution, Linehaul)
• Connecting data patterns to physical process failures — understanding how a "Rolled Freight" in the data maps to a real truck departure issue at the FC
• Designing and implementing corrective actions (process changes, system configurations, SOP updates) with measurable impact on DEA
• Building and maintaining Control Plans (SPC, OCAP) to sustain improvements and detect regressions early
• Leading Kaizen events and War Rooms during Sev1/Sev2 DEA events, coordinating containment and permanent fixes
• Managing the DEA governance cadence: daily callouts, weekly reviews, monthly goals reporting
• Identifying waste (Muda) and variation in the promise-to-delivery chain and proposing structural improvements
• Driving cross-functional alignment between Planning Systems, FC Ops, Transportation, and Last Mile teams to close systemic gaps
• Benchmarking Brazil DEA processes against other geographies (MX, NA, EU) to identify best practices

A day in the life
You will start your day reviewing yesterday's DEA performance — identifying which nodes, carriers, or programs missed target. You will then dive deep into the top offenders, walking the Gemba (virtually or physically) to understand what went wrong operationally. You will present findings in the daily War Room, propose countermeasures, and track implementation.

Your week includes cross-functional meetings with:
• FC Operations (GRU9, REC3, CWB1) for FC Execution issues
• ATS Linehaul & Sort Center teams for middle-mile failures
• AMZL (DSP, Flex, Hub) for last-mile delivery failures
• Planning Systems & Tech (F2P, Promise, ATROPS) for systemic/configuration issues
• Finance for impact quantification and business case development

About the team
Amazon Customer Excellence System (ACES) is a team of highly qualified individuals responsible for the quality, productivity, safety, and speed of Amazon Operations. The DEA program within ACES owns the governance and continuous improvement of delivery promise accuracy — ensuring that when Amazon commits a delivery date to a customer, we deliver on that promise.

- Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification
- Experience running an effective operational excellence program
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience in program or project management
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English at C1 level or above
- Experience with root cause analysis methodologies (5-Why, Fishbone, FMEA)
- Intermediate level in Spanish
Preferred qualifications:
- Lean-Six Sigma Black Belt certification
- Experience in operational logistics/supply chain, manufacturing, transportation, general management or an engineering role
- Knowledge of SQL
- Experience with SPC (control charts, process capability analysis, OCAP)
- Experience managing cross-functional improvement programs with 5+ stakeholder teams
- Postgraduate degree in Engineering, Operations Management, or MBA
- Experience with Amazon operational systems (PerfectMile, ATROPS, FMC, SSP) is a strong plus

We are a team of highly motivated, engaged, and responsive professionals who enable the core sustainable infrastructure of AWS — powering thousands of businesses across more than 190 countries.

The Data Center Sourcing & Procurement (DCSP) team is seeking a results-oriented, technically-minded Program Manager to lead our team of Category Managers and Supply Chain Managers from a data and AI perspective, supporting AWS Data Center build projects across the Americas region. jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, Non-Standard Infrastructure Delivery (NSID)
jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.
You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
About the Role
The AWS Non-Standard Infrastructure Global Delivery Team builds and scales infrastructure for AWS programs that don't fit neatly into traditional data center models. Our projects are tailored to the specific needs of internal and external customers — from satellite ground stations that downlink data from orbit, to specialized labs where engineers develop custom silicon and push the boundaries of quantum computing, to purpose-built environments with precision environmental controls for archival storage systems, to infrastructure that extends the AWS network to the furthest edge of its global footprint. Each program brings its own constraints, its own technical requirements, and often its own first-of-kind design challenges.
What makes this team unique is the degree of ambiguity we operate in. Many of our projects begin as loosely defined requests from internal customer teams who know what they need to accomplish but not necessarily what infrastructure it takes to get there. A significant part of this role is working upstream with those customers to develop initial requirements, define technical scope, build demand forecasts, and refine scaling models — often for infrastructure types where no established playbook exists. The solutions we deliver are boutique by nature: custom-designed to meet specific programmatic needs, site constraints, and operational models that vary from project to project.
The scope is broad, the problems are novel, and the pace of growth means we are constantly onboarding new infrastructure types and scaling models.
If you thrive in ambiguity, enjoy the challenge of translating vague asks into engineered solutions, and want to shape how AWS builds and scales its infrastructure globally — this role is for you.
We have an immediate opening for a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager III to drive capacity delivery across multiple non-standard infrastructure programs worldwide. You will lead cross-functional teams through the full lifecycle of infrastructure delivery — from upstream requirements definition and demand forecasting through design development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment. You will develop and implement scalable mechanisms for tracking program health, drive data-driven decisions influencing significant capital investments, and work with stakeholders across AWS to solve constraints, remove blockers, and accelerate delivery.
Your work will span:
- Requirements development — Working with internal customer teams to translate ambiguous needs into defined technical requirements, scope documents, and infrastructure specifications for novel deployment types
- Stakeholder management and influence — Navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures and influencing without authority to align diverse teams, secure resources, drive decisions, and maintain momentum across programs where no single team owns the end-to-end outcome
- Demand forecasting and capacity planning — Building initial demand models and scaling forecasts for programs where historical baselines don't exist, and refining them as programs mature
- Boutique design coordination — Partnering with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions that meet unique programmatic constraints (environmental, regulatory, physical, operational)
- Multi-year delivery execution — Driving complex, globally distributed projects from conceptual feasibility through budget approval, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
- Cross-program coordination — Identifying synergies, shared solutions, and lessons learned across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure types
- Mechanism development — Building scalable processes and reporting to monitor delivery health, drive accountability, and escalate to leadership as the portfolio grows
This role offers an opportunity to drive and influence business-critical decisions impacting the long-term future of AWS, working at the leading edge of emerging capability and service offerings. You must be comfortable managing remote project teams delivering novel — and sometimes pioneering — solutions across multiple countries and time zones; operating as the connective tissue between customer teams with undefined needs and engineering teams who build solutions; assessing and mitigating downstream risk; troubleshooting unforeseen implementation issues; removing barriers to project success; and operating effectively amid persistent uncertainty and change.
Up to 15% domestic and international travel may be necessary to support AWS non-standard infrastructure planning and scaling efforts.

Key job responsibilities
- Work upstream with internal customer teams to elicit, define, and document technical requirements for infrastructure programs that are often undefined or loosely scoped at inception
- Develop initial demand forecasts and capacity scaling models for emerging programs; refine forecasts as programs mature and data becomes available
- Lead end-to-end delivery of boutique infrastructure projects from requirements definition through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment
- Manage project budgets, schedules, and resource plans for programs with diverse and evolving technical requirements and site conditions
- Partner with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions — working within unique constraints that vary by program, site, and customer need
- Coordinate cross-program activities to gain cost and execution efficiencies; identify and drive shared solutions and reusable design patterns
- Build and maintain relationships with internal customers (service teams, lab teams, engineering organizations) to align infrastructure delivery with evolving demand
- Convene partners and stakeholders to architect end-to-end process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs
- Identify and mitigate risks in environments with limited precedent; develop contingency plans for first-of-kind deployment scenarios
- Develop scalable mechanisms, standard operating procedures, and process improvements to support rapid portfolio growth and new program onboarding
- Create data visualization reports and KPIs illustrating program health; escalate issues with clear recommendations to executive leadership

A day in the life
No two days are the same. You might start the morning in a requirements-definition session with a lab team that has a new hardware validation need but no infrastructure spec — helping them articulate what they actually need built. Then you shift to reviewing a demand forecast for a program expanding into new geographies, working with limited data and a lot of assumptions to refine. After lunch you're troubleshooting a procurement constraint on a boutique design that doesn't fit standard ordering mechanisms, followed by a cross-functional review of site conditions for a deployment in a venue that's never hosted this type of infrastructure before. You'll also spend time convening partners and stakeholders to architect process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs. You'll regularly work with finance to secure capital, partner with engineering to translate customer intent into buildable designs, and look downstream to identify risks before they become blockers. The variety is the appeal — and the ability to navigate ambiguity, define scope where none existed, and drive delivery across technically diverse programs is what makes this role unique.

About the team
The Non-Standard Infrastructure team exists because AWS's growth doesn't stop at the walls of traditional data centers. We deliver capacity for programs whose infrastructure needs are unique, evolving, and often undefined at the outset. Our work starts upstream — helping customer teams figure out what they need — and carries through to handing over operational infrastructure that meets exacting requirements we helped define. Our team members are builders and translators: people who can sit with a scientist, engineer, or service owner, understand what they're trying to achieve, and turn that into a deliverable infrastructure program. If you're energized by variety, comfortable building the plane while flying it, and motivated by the impact of enabling AWS's most innovative services — you'll fit right in.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in engineering, project management, construction management or similar technical focus
- Experience identifying, mitigating, and managing business risks and tradeoffs
- Experience identifying and mitigating project risks in ambiguous or unprecedented deployment environments
- 3+ years of program management or technical project management experience
- 3+ years of directly managing and being responsible for multiple large projects experience
Preferred qualifications:
- 5+ years of experience in technical infrastructure delivery, data center construction, telecommunications, or mission-critical facilities
- Track record of building program management mechanisms from scratch to support a growing and diversifying portfolio of project types
- Strong data analysis skills; experience building dashboards and metrics to drive program health visibility
- Familiarity with AWS infrastructure concepts, data center design principles, or cloud computing architecture

We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build. Protecting your privacy and the security of your data is a longstanding top priority for Amazon. jobs.description:
Amazon provides a highly reliable, scalable, low-cost infrastructure platform in the cloud that powers hundreds of thousands of businesses in 190 countries around the world.

The Amazon Cloud infrastructure is built around Regions and Availability Zones. Our Regions provide multiple, physically separated and isolated Availability Zones which are connected with low latency, high throughput, and highly redundant networking.

These Availability Zones offer AWS customers an easier and more effective way to design and operate applications and databases, making them more highly available, fault tolerant, and scalable than traditional single data centre infrastructures or multi-data centre infrastructures.

How would you like to come be part of the team that builds Fiber to the Cloud?

We are looking for a highly motivated Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) with a strong civil construction background to help develop and scale one of the world's largest and most complex fiber networks. Based in Dublin and working across multiple EMEA Regions, you will own the end-to-end delivery of outside plant (OSP) fiber civil works, including trenching and excavation, duct and conduit installation, directional drilling (HDD), chambers and handholes, and surface reinstatement, managing the civil contractors who build them to schedule, cost, and quality.

jobs.title: Manager II Program Management, Global Catalog Operations
jobs.description:
Amazon.com operates in a global eCommerce environment without boundaries, and operates a diverse set of businesses worldwide, including Retail, third party marketplaces, eCommerce platforms, web services for developers.

The Amazon product catalog is a set of records; each record being a set of facts describing a physical or digital product. These records are often organized by defined relationships (e.g. variations such as different sizes of the same shoe). Our ability to provide a good product discovery experience and empower our customers to make well informed purchase decisions is dependent on the quality of our product catalog. In a high quality catalog, every product is described with a complete, structured, accurate and correctly normalized set of facts. Every product is represented by a unique record appropriately related to one another.
The Global catalog operations (GCO) team is part of Amazon Selection & Catalog services (ASCS) teams in India focus on leveraging human intelligence, external or internal, to measure and improve the quality of the catalog: Global catalog operations (GCO) charter is to make Catalog engineering programs more effective by providing expert human judgment. Catalog Operations from its inception has been partnering with engineering teams to run programs focused on improving the data quality of catalog in all market places.

We are seeking an experienced people leader to join our rapidly growing team as a Manager II, Program Management. In this role you will build and lead a team of SMEs, auditors and Program Managers responsible for developing insights and eliminating quality defects that affect business metrics. You will own a portfolio of catalog quality programs rather than a single workstream, set the direction and mechanisms your team operates by, and be accountable for the aggregate delivery and business outcomes of the programs under you. As part of this role, you will 1) hire, develop, and lead a team of auditors, SMES and program managers, growing the bench and the capability of the function, 2) own a portfolio of quality programs, prioritizing across competing initiatives and allocating capacity to the highest impact opportunities, 3) set the operating mechanisms, standards, and roadmap that make your team's programs measurable and repeatable, and 4) work collaboratively across partner teams (Science, PMs, Engineering, Business, etc.) and represent catalog quality program management to senior leadership across GCO and partner orgs.

Key job responsibilities
As a Manager II, Program Management you will:

- Build, lead, and develop a team of auditors, SMEs and program managers, owning hiring, performance management, coaching, and career growth
- Own catalog quality programs, setting priorities across competing initiatives and allocating team capacity to the highest impact work
- Establish the operating mechanisms, standards, and roadmap that ensure your team's programs deliver measurable business and operational outcomes
- Be accountable for the aggregate delivery and business/operational metrics of the programs under your team
- Drive quantitative, data-oriented decision making across the portfolio and champion the adoption of technology solutions and process improvements
- Communicate program progress, risks, and results to senior leadership, ensuring transparency and alignment with key business goals
- Identify systemic gaps across process areas and mobilize your team and stakeholders to resolve them
- Serve as an escalation point and senior partner for in-house and customer teams across Science, Engineering, Product, and Business
- Ensure effective risk controls are developed and maintained across programs, with corrective actions that keep commitments on track and minimize losses
- Develop and influence new ideas, establishing procedures and practices that promote long-term, scalable solutions in dynamic environments
- Drive continuous improvement and decision-making strategies across the team and the broader function
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- 3+ years of delivering cross functional projects experience
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements
- 5+ years of team management experience

- Experience in data mining, data management, reporting, and SQL queries

jobs.description:
You will own the end-to-end delivery of network infrastructure at scale — from customer demand signal through manufacturing, shipping, and site landing — ensuring the world's largest cloud network gets built on time. This is a high-visibility, high-autonomy role where you directly influence whether critical network capacity arrives when customers need it.

Key job responsibilities
Why this role:
You own outcomes, not tasks. CDR operates at the intersection of supply chain, network engineering, and program execution — you'll drive delivery across all of them.

You'll lead through ambiguity. When demand shifts, vendors miss, or builds slip, you're the one who finds the path forward.

What you'll do:

Drive delivery performance across network rack demand streams (Bricks, Spines, Loose Gear, Scaling, New DC) from order through site installation

Own stakeholder communication for delivery status, risks, and blockers — proactively surfacing issues before they become escalations.

Manage cross-functional dependencies across procurement, manufacturing, logistics, construction, and network deployment teams.

Build and maintain mechanisms (dashboards, WBRs, escalation paths, SOPs) that make delivery health visible and actionable.

Identify systemic bottlenecks and drive structural improvements.

Partner with automation and data engineering teams to scale delivery insights through tooling

What you'll bring:

Track record of program-managing complex, multi-stakeholder hardware or infrastructure delivery at scale.

Ability to synthesize across data sources and present the "so what" — not just the status.

Comfort operating in ambiguity with incomplete information and competing priorities.

Strong written communication: you produce artifacts that drive decisions without requiring follow-up questions.

Bias toward mechanisms over heroics — you build systems that make the next delivery easier, not just this one.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a miss that threatens a site deadline — you assess impact and draft the recovery path before your first meeting. Mid-day, you're connecting supply chain signals across procurement, manufacturing, and logistics to catch cascading risks early. You prep a delivery narrative for leadership where the goal is zero follow-up questions. You close the day unblocking your team and documenting the pattern so it doesn't take heroics next time.

You're executing today's deliveries while building the mechanisms that make tomorrow's easier.

About the team
The CDR Networking team ensures on-time delivery of critical networking hardware — racks, optics, and loose gear — that connects every AWS service to the backbone. We operate at the intersection of supply chain, manufacturing, and network engineering, owning delivery end-to-end from customer order through site landing. Our culture is built on transparency, disciplined execution, and continuous improvement. This is not an easy job. Our customers are demanding. The timelines are short. The constraints are real. The means we challenge the status quo, proceduralize what's repeatable, automate what's possible, and focus our people on the problems that actually require their expertise. Our mission: rack delivery never impacts a customer commitment date.

Own stakeholder communication for delivery status, risks, and blockers — proactively surfacing issues before they become escalations.

Track record of program-managing complex, multi-stakeholder hardware or infrastructure delivery at scale.

Comfort operating in ambiguity with incomplete information and competing priorities.

jobs.title: Sr. Tech Infra Program Manager, Non-Standard Infrastructure Delivery (NSID)
jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain, and we're looking for talented people who want to help.
You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
About the Role
The AWS Non-Standard Infrastructure Global Delivery Team builds and scales infrastructure for AWS programs that don't fit neatly into traditional data center models. Our projects are tailored to the specific needs of internal and external customers, from satellite ground stations that downlink data from orbit, to specialized labs where engineers develop custom silicon and push the boundaries of quantum computing, to purpose-built environments with precision environmental controls for archival storage systems, to infrastructure that extends the AWS network to the furthest edge of its global footprint. Each program brings its own constraints, its own technical requirements, and often its own first-of-kind design challenges.
What makes this team unique is the degree of ambiguity we operate in. Many of our projects begin as loosely defined requests from internal customer teams who know what they need to accomplish but not necessarily what infrastructure it takes to get there. A significant part of this role is working upstream with those customers to develop initial requirements, define technical scope, build demand forecasts, and refine scaling models. often for infrastructure types where no established playbook exists. The solutions we deliver are boutique by nature: custom-designed to meet specific programmatic needs, site constraints, and operational models that vary from project to project.
The scope is broad, the problems are novel, and the pace of growth means we are constantly onboarding new infrastructure types and scaling models.
If you thrive in ambiguity, enjoy the challenge of translating vague asks into engineered solutions, and want to shape how AWS builds and scales its infrastructure globally, this role is for you.
We have an immediate opening for a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager III to drive capacity delivery across multiple non-standard infrastructure programs worldwide. You will lead cross-functional teams through the full lifecycle of infrastructure delivery — from upstream requirements definition and demand forecasting through design development, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment. You will develop and implement scalable mechanisms for tracking program health, drive data-driven decisions influencing significant capital investments, and work with stakeholders across AWS to solve constraints, remove blockers, and accelerate delivery.
Your work will span:
- Requirements development - Working with internal customer teams to translate ambiguous needs into defined technical requirements, scope documents, and infrastructure specifications for novel deployment types
- Stakeholder management and influence - Navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures and influencing without authority to align diverse teams, secure resources, drive decisions, and maintain momentum across programs where no single team owns the end-to-end outcome
- Demand forecasting and capacity planning — Building initial demand models and scaling forecasts for programs where historical baselines don't exist, and refining them as programs mature
- Boutique design coordination - Partnering with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions that meet unique programmatic constraints (environmental, regulatory, physical, operational)
- Multi-year delivery execution - Driving complex, globally distributed projects from conceptual feasibility through budget approval, design, procurement, construction, and commissioning
- Cross-program coordination - Identifying synergies, shared solutions, and lessons learned across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure types
- Mechanism development - Building scalable processes and reporting to monitor delivery health, drive accountability, and escalate to leadership as the portfolio grows
This role offers an opportunity to drive and influence business-critical decisions impacting the long-term future of AWS, working at the leading edge of emerging capability and service offerings. You must be comfortable managing remote project teams delivering novel, and sometimes pioneering, solutions across multiple countries and time zones; operating as the connective tissue between customer teams with undefined needs and engineering teams who build solutions; assessing and mitigating downstream risk; troubleshooting unforeseen implementation issues; removing barriers to project success; and operating effectively amid persistent uncertainty and change.
Up to 15% domestic and international travel may be necessary to support AWS non-standard infrastructure planning and scaling efforts.

Key job responsibilities
- Work upstream with internal customer teams to elicit, define, and document technical requirements for infrastructure programs that are often undefined or loosely scoped at inception
- Develop initial demand forecasts and capacity scaling models for emerging programs; refine forecasts as programs mature and data becomes available
- Lead end-to-end delivery of boutique infrastructure projects from requirements definition through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and deployment
- Manage project budgets, schedules, and resource plans for programs with diverse and evolving technical requirements and site conditions
- Partner with engineering teams to develop tailored infrastructure solutions — working within unique constraints that vary by program, site, and customer need
- Coordinate cross-program activities to gain cost and execution efficiencies; identify and drive shared solutions and reusable design patterns
- Build and maintain relationships with internal customers (service teams, lab teams, engineering organizations) to align infrastructure delivery with evolving demand
- Convene partners and stakeholders to architect end-to-end process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs
- Identify and mitigate risks in environments with limited precedent; develop contingency plans for first-of-kind deployment scenarios
- Develop scalable mechanisms, standard operating procedures, and process improvements to support rapid portfolio growth and new program onboarding
- Create data visualization reports and KPIs illustrating program health; escalate issues with clear recommendations to executive leadership

A day in the life
No two days are the same. You might start the morning in a requirements-definition session with a lab team that has a new hardware validation need but no infrastructure spec — helping them articulate what they actually need built. Then you shift to reviewing a demand forecast for a program expanding into new geographies, working with limited data and a lot of assumptions to refine. After lunch you're troubleshooting a procurement constraint on a boutique design that doesn't fit standard ordering mechanisms, followed by a cross-functional review of site conditions for a deployment in a venue that's never hosted this type of infrastructure before. You'll also spend time convening partners and stakeholders to architect process flows, delineate roles and responsibilities, and establish governance frameworks — transforming ambiguity into operational clarity, eliminating friction, and driving repeatable efficiencies across maturing programs. You'll regularly work with finance to secure capital, partner with engineering to translate customer intent into buildable designs, and look downstream to identify risks before they become blockers. The variety is the appeal — and the ability to navigate ambiguity, define scope where none existed, and drive delivery across technically diverse programs is what makes this role unique.

About the team
The Non-Standard Infrastructure team exists because AWS's growth doesn't stop at the walls of traditional data centers. We deliver capacity for programs whose infrastructure needs are unique, evolving, and often undefined at the outset. Our work starts upstream — helping customer teams figure out what they need — and carries through to handing over operational infrastructure that meets exacting requirements we helped define. Our team members are builders and translators: people who can sit with a scientist, engineer, or service owner, understand what they're trying to achieve, and turn that into a deliverable infrastructure program. If you're energized by variety, comfortable building the plane while flying it, and motivated by the impact of enabling AWS's most innovative services — you'll fit right in.
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of program management or technical project management experience
- 5+ years of data center or network capacity planning, data center or network infrastructure program/project management, or related technical experience
- Experience identifying, mitigating, and managing business risks and tradeoffs
- 5+ years managing complex, cross-functional infrastructure build programs where strategy and deployment plans were not fully defined, requiring the ability to independently drive clarity, define scope, and deliver outcomes with limited guidance.
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field (or equivalent technical experience), with demonstrated ability to evaluate whether a technical design fits a given deployment scenario and to identify when deployment issues stem from underlying design gaps — particularly in environments with high variability and incomplete requirements
Preferred qualifications:
- Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification
- Experience with analytical tools and ability to dive deep into metrics and reporting
- 7+ years of experience in technical infrastructure delivery, data center construction, telecommunications, or mission-critical facilities
- Track record of building program management mechanisms from scratch to support a growing and diversifying portfolio of project types
- Familiarity with AWS infrastructure concepts, data center design principles, or cloud computing architecture
- Experience defining and documenting new deployment processes or build plans for infrastructure products where no established playbook existed, including making trade-off recommendations across competing priorities at the organizational level

Amazon is looking for a talented and self-motivated Principal Environmental Technical Program Manager to serve as a senior individual contributor and a trusted part of the technical and business leadership of the organization. Reporting directly to the Director of AWS Environmental, this global Principal tackles intrinsically hard environmental problems, those that are complex, ambiguous, and undefined, with less existing structure and significant business risk, and delivers solutions with complete independence in partnership with teams across AWS.

This is a role for a seasoned environmental expert whose influence spans multiple organizations and who leads through expertise rather than positional authority. The Principal is an exemplary, hands-on practitioner who is technically deep, brings clarity to complexity, and has resounding impact by aligning teams toward coherent strategies. The Principal drives cross-functional alignment before decisions reach the field, resolves disagreements at the peer level rather than escalating them, and serves as the escalation point on the largest and most complex issues. Success is measured by the ability to move the hardest, cross-cutting problems to durable resolution across environmental media, regions, and partner teams.

Technical Leadership & Influence. Serve as a recognized technical authority on the organization's hardest environmental problems, leading initiatives whose impact spans multiple organizations. Lead through influence rather than authority, aligning teams on coherent strategies so they deliver independently toward an integrated whole. Set the standard for technical excellence and share expertise across regions to raise the bar organization-wide. Mentor technical talent and program teams without direct-management responsibility.

Environmental Compliance. Serve as the deepest technical resource and escalation point for the most complex, ambiguous compliance challenges across media and regions. Define and influence regional and global environmental standards and policies, aligning teams on coherent approaches. Lead resolution of undefined, high-complexity compliance issues and analyze regulations across jurisdictions to anticipate requirements. Strategy & Program Management. Define environmental strategy where none exists and deliver with complete independence, owning large programs in new territory. Lead external initiatives such as advancing regulatory frameworks, contributing to advocacy, engaging regulators and communities, and designing assessment programs. Make organization-level trade-offs and implement durable mechanisms that reduce risk and increase efficiency. Define and track program-delivery and performance metrics, and work escalations to mitigate risk. Improve regulations by negotiating with regulators, and support community interactions.

The AWS Environmental team supports the full lifecycle of infrastructure development, beginning with site selection and due diligence and continuing through design, construction, and operations. Getting this right requires tight coordination across forecasting, placement, capacity, and seller behavior — and a clear line of sight into what is driving outcomes at the country level.
We are looking for a Program Manager who will partner closely with in-country FBA, Supply Chain, Retail, and Operations teams in International Emerging Stores (IES) stores to drive key FBA inventory metrics — covering areas such as inventory availability, excess/Aged inventory. In the near term, this role is focused on building the operating mechanisms, measurement frameworks, and cross-functional alignment needed to move these metrics. Over time, as ownership matures, this person is expected to take on deeper accountability for metric outcomes, drive programs informed by experimentation and country-level insights, and work directly with engineering, science, and BI teams to build scalable solutions. You will need to be comfortable operating without a fully defined playbook — diagnosing problems using data you pull yourself, influencing teams you do not manage, and making decisions in the face of incomplete information. The ability to think in terms of systems, design experiments with sellers, and approach problems with an AI-first mindset will be critical to succeeding in this role and growing it over time.

• Partner with in-country FBA, Supply Chain, Retail, and Operations teams to drive key FBA inventory metrics taking progressively deeper ownership of outcomes over time.
• Build and maintain root-cause attribution frameworks that connect upstream inputs (forecasting gaps, inbound defects, seller restock adoption, FC constraints) to downstream metric outcomes, enabling clear and consistent diagnosis across teams.
• Lead weekly, monthly, and quarterly review mechanisms for your metric areas, representing FBA in country Business Review forums and ensuring that system-driven insights are correctly communicated and acted upon.
• Design and run structured experiments with sellers - adoption levers, communication treatments, and incentive mechanisms, etc. and use findings to build an evidence-based product and program roadmap.
• Work with Product, science, and BI teams to translate operational insights and experiment results into scalable product improvements; identify IES-specific requirements and ensure they are reflected in WW roadmaps.

• Coordinate peak readiness (Prime Day, BFCM) by identifying inventory risks early, stress-testing operational workflows, and working with partner teams on mitigation plans.

jobs.title: Program Manager II, Risk Mining, Account Integrity
jobs.description:
Amazon's Account Integrity Team (AIT) within Buyer Risk Prevention (BRP) protects hundreds of millions of customers by identifying and stopping fraudulent activity before it causes harm. The Risk Mining function is where human ingenuity meets machine learning - our team detects emerging modus operandi (MOs) that automated systems alone can't catch, and feeds those signals back into scalable upstream defenses. If you want your program management skills to directly translate into customer trust at global scale, this is the team.

The Program Manager (PM II) will own the operational rhythm and cross-functional coordination for Risk Mining across four verticals spanning India and Costa Rica. This is a role where you will have real ownership from day one - partnering with Risk Mining leadership to scope processes, define goals, build reporting mechanisms, and drive delivery against them. You will work with a high degree of autonomy, collaborating across Engineering, Machine Learning, Product, and partner risk teams to improve workflows, champion AI-enabled solutions, and deliver measurable gains in detection speed, quality, and operational efficiency.

This is an execution-focused role with broad cross-team influence, reporting to the Risk Mining leadership team. The PM is accountable for scoping processes, owning the operating cadence, driving programs to delivery, mitigating risk, and clearing blockers.

Key job responsibilities
1. Operating Cadence & Reporting
- Own Weekly Program Review (WPR) and Quarterly Program Review (QPR) reporting for the Risk Mining function, ensuring data accuracy, timely delivery, and clear path-to-green commentary on key goals.
- Own Flash preparation and build a self-sustaining reporting rhythm where leadership always has an accurate, on-time view of the org.
- Track and drive closure of action items stemming from business reviews and COE findings.
- Accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately.
2. Cross-Team Collaboration & Standardization
- Drive cross-RM initiatives with Payment Risk (PRISM-I) and Abuse Risk Mining (ARM) teams.
- Serve as the operational point of contact for joint MO investigations and deep dives.
- Lead coordination and sync between India and Costa Rica sites to reduce operational drift across verticals.
- Standardize processes, tooling, and communication cadences across all Risk Mining verticals to ensure consistent quality and velocity.
- Own the program for feedback loops from Risk Mining MOs back into ML, Engineering, and Product teams.
3. SOP Governance & Audit-Readiness
- Lead SOP lifecycle management - author, review, deploy, and ensure parity or superiority of SOPs across BRP.
- Keep SOPs audit-ready with periodic reviews and documentation updates tied to policy changes.
- Manage the goals document and quarterly planning cycles to keep the team aligned with org-level priorities.
- Drive efficiency in rule management - create paths to offline monitoring, and partner with ML teams on rule lifecycle.
4. Innovation & GenAI Enablement
- Identify automation and GenAI opportunities within Risk Mining workflows.
- Reduce manual effort and improve throughput and quality in MO identification, triage, and reporting.
- Partner with Engineering, ML, and Product teams to pilot and adopt AI-assisted workflows across Risk Mining operations.
- Develop the RM MO Repository - a scalable knowledge base of modus operandi patterns for reuse across AIT and partner teams.
- Propose and implement programs such as Hackathons, Innovation Workshops, and AI Proficiency sprints.
- Establish mechanisms to measure realized ROI from AI investments.
5. ML & Engineering Intake & Prioritization
- Own the ML and Engineering intake mechanism with AIT and IDS engineering teams.
- Ensure the team's highest-value asks are consistently landed, not stuck in ad-hoc queues.
- Lead OP1 planning - build intake processes within Risk Mining that produce scalable, long-term roadmap ideas.
- Enable prioritization of requirements with Engineering and ML partners.
- Own communications for new tool rollouts to ensure smooth adoption across all verticals and sites.
6. Escalation Management
- Single point of contact for all escalation action items - Sev-2 tickets, executive escalations, and COE action items.
- Manage prioritization and tracking of external requests from partner teams on MO investigations and deep dives.
- Ensure operational readiness for process changes, transitions, and high-severity incident response.

A day in the life
Your week will blend tactical execution with strategic thinking - no two days look identical, but here's the rhythm:
Tactical (Keeping the Engine Running)
- Follow up on ageing Risk Mining tickets, drive root-cause analysis, and close action items.
- Report out metrics and path-to-green on key goals in WBR and WPR forums.
- Follow up on Rule Governance action items, SEV-2 reduction efforts, and audit readiness reviews.
- Coordinate with cross-site teams (India and Costa Rica) to ensure consistent execution and information flow.
- Participate in weekly project stand-ups and initiative check-ins.
Strategic (Building What's Next)
- Participate in GenAI and Innovation forums to identify and champion automation opportunities across Risk Mining workflows.
- Join Engineering and ML connects to stay close to the technical roadmap and drive intake priorities.
- Facilitate cross-functional partner connects - collaborating with Payment Risk, Abuse Risk Mining, and broader BRP stakeholders on joint MO investigations and risk signals.
- Prepare documents for weekly and quarterly reviews, metric deep-dives, and OP1 planning cycles.
- Drive new project kick-offs and workshops with ML, Engineering, and Product partners.

About the team
The Risk Mining team within Account Integrity spans India and Costa Rica, and works for Amazon's worldwide marketplace to detect and disrupt bad-actor behavior. We are analysts, investigators, and builders - using a powerful combination of analytics, code, GenAI tools, and deep-dive investigations to uncover fraud patterns that automated systems alone can't catch.

Our mission is simple: find the signal in the noise before bad actors cause harm. We partner closely with Machine Learning, Engineering, and Product teams to turn our investigative findings into scalable upstream defenses. The team operates across four risk verticals: Anti-Automation, Account Takeover, SMS Pumping, and Bad Actor Account - and collaborates with Payment Risk and Abuse Risk Mining teams across Buyer Risk Prevention (BRP) to drive end-to-end fraud mitigation.

If you want to work where your program management skills directly translate into customer trust at global scale, this is the team.

- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience

- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

jobs.title: Sr Technical Infrastructure Program Manager, EMEA Data Center Delivery
jobs.description:
Amazon are seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to support our European Data Center infrastructure growth initiatives. Based in London, the TIPM will lead cross functional teams to drive the implementation and deployment of data center expansion projects to meet the demands of our rapidly growing business.

Our Technical Program Managers are strong communicators both written and verbally and lead multi-discipline, highly technical physical infrastructure project teams. They lead teams of internal and external stakeholders through all stages of the Data Center development lifecycle from initial site due diligence through Construction and into Operation. The core role of the TIPM is to deliver capacity for our customers through developing delivery programs and working closely with stakeholder teams to identify risks and resolve issues to ensure those programs are delivered on time and within budget.

The TIPM partners with various stakeholder teams during data center delivery; Real Estate to support the feasibility and selection of new sites; Energy to ensure suitable grid connection is available; Design Engineering to coordinate project specific inputs, constraints and risks into designs; Procurement to secure on time delivery of critical equipment; Construction Management to track budget & progress; and Operations to complete the project with successful handover, to name but a few.

Key job responsibilities
• Take large, complex projects and break them down into manageable pieces,
• Clearly communicate goals, roles, responsibilities, and desired outcomes to internal cross-functional and remote teams.
• Up to 25% travel is envisaged within EMEA.
• Be responsible for end-to-end program delivery from pre-contract design up to final handover to Operations of Colo, Hybrid Colo & AWS Leased/Owned Data Centers in the EMEA region.
• Manage interface between internal (Real Estate, Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Infrastructure Deployment, Networking, Operations, Security, Fiber, Finance etc.) and external stakeholders (Contractors, Colo Vendors) to ensure on time and on budget delivery of Data Center projects.
• Build and maintaining overall delivery program and project budget, submitting Capital Allocation Requests to Senior leadership to secure finance for project delivery.
• Work with Capacity Planning, Energy and Real Estate teams to develop short & long term build strategies to meet forecast demand.
• Support continuous process improvement through leading workflow updates, documenting & implementing lessons learned and sharing knowledge across delivery teams to ensure EMEA wide efficiency improvements.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

- Experience working with multiple stakeholders at various levels and in different locales to drive alignment

jobs.title: Program Manager II, Buyer Abuse
jobs.description:
Amazon's Buyer Abuse Prevention (BAP) team sits within the broader Buyer Risk Prevention (BRP) organization — a centralized technology and program team whose mission is to make Amazon the safest and most trusted place worldwide to transact online. Buyer abuse is defined as the risk associated with customers repeatedly violating Amazon's policies and affecting the profitability, brand, and reputation of Amazon or its Selling Partners.

BAP sits at the intersection of technology, policy, and operations to detect, investigate, and prevent abusive behaviors across Amazon. Our work directly impacts Amazon's bottom line, protecting hundreds of millions of dollars in concession losses annually while preserving the customer and seller experience.

BAP is seeking an innovative, results-oriented, and customer-centric Program Manager to own and drive the Automation program across the Buyer Abuse Prevention organization. In this role, you will be responsible for scaling Amazon's ability to investigate and act on risky orders and concessions at billions-of-transactions scale — without relying on manual effort. You will define the automation strategy, manage a portfolio of automation initiatives, and balance the dual mandate of maximizing automation rate while carefully managing enforcement quality through leakage (under-enforcement) and customer experience (over-enforcement) metrics.

The successful candidate will be highly analytical, resourceful, customer focused, team oriented, and have an ability to work independently under time constraints to meet deadlines. He or she will have a proven track record in taking on end-to-end ownership and successfully delivering results in a fast-paced and dynamic business environment.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end Automation program strategy, roadmap, and execution across BAP, including setting goals, success metrics, and mechanisms to track progress against automation rate targets.
- Balance the core automation tradeoff: maximizing automation rate while managing leakage (under-enforcement risk) and customer experience metrics (over-enforcement risk), ensuring precision thresholds are maintained across all deployed models and workflows.
- Define and manage key success metrics for the Automation program, including automation rate, task coverage, precision, leakage rate, false positive rate, and customer-facing impact metrics.
- Partner with Product, Engineering, Machine Learning, and Data Science teams to design, test, and launch new automation capabilities — including LLM-powered enforcement, model-based auto-decisions, and workflow automation.
- Interact with key stakeholders to define the metrics, measurements, and tools to quantify automation program goals and communicate results to Senior Leaders across Amazon.
- Conduct in-depth reviews of automation performance data to identify patterns, gaps, and opportunities; develop reports and narratives for leadership and partner teams.
- Communicate (both verbally and in writing) program successes, failures, lessons learned, and mitigation plans to stakeholders.
- Champion on behalf of Amazon and our Customers and help uncover issues currently impacting our Customer Experience as a result of automation decisions.
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

- 3+ years of driving process improvements experience

jobs.title: Program Manager, Middle Mile, ATS - Amazon Transportation Services
jobs.description:

Our team takes a transversal view of the transportation network, identifying and correcting defects end-to-end while uncovering opportunities to improve service levels, reduce cost, and raise the quality of every package we move — on the way out and on the way back. We don't own a single node or a single lane: we own the outcome.

This role requires someone who is as comfortable diving into data to find a root cause as they are influencing a cross-functional team to act on it. You will represent a critical function at the intersection of outbound execution and returns operations, working across Sort Centers, Middle Mile, Last Mile, and 3PC networks to ensure our customer promises are met — every time.

Your Responsibilities:

Monitor and analyze end-to-end outbound and returns performance metrics (OTA, DEA, EAD, Returns OTA, HUB OTD, cancellation rate), proactively detecting defects and driving corrective actions with the relevant owners across the network;
Pull and synthesize data from multiple sources (SQL, Excel, internal dashboards) to generate both recurring and ad hoc analyses; build and maintain metrics that expose operational gaps and measure the effectiveness of improvement actions;
Act as the connective tissue between operational, commercial, and tech teams — translating field-level defects into structured problem statements and ensuring resolution is tracked through to closure;
Lead and coordinate cross-functional initiatives with Fulfillment Centers, Supply Chain, Procurement, Finance, AMZL, and Carrier teams to address structural gaps in outbound flow and returns processing;
Identify and size improvement opportunities across the network — whether in capacity allocation, transit time, sort quality, carrier mix, or returns routing — and build the business case to prioritize and execute them;
Support demand forecasting and peak planning (Prime, Black Friday, seasonal surges) in partnership with Planning and S&OP teams, ensuring capacity is secured and risks are surfaced in advance;
Prepare and present performance updates, escalation briefs, and strategic documents for MBRs, QBRs, and leadership reviews; ensure the right story is told with the right data;
Partner with central tech and automation teams to translate operational requirements into technology asks, and champion tooling improvements that reduce manual effort and improve decision quality across the Outbound & Returns operation.

- Monitor end-to-end outbound and returns network performance (OTA, DEA, EAD, Returns OTA, cancellation rate), identifying defects and leading root cause analysis and corrective action plans with accountable owners across Sort Centers, Middle Mile, Last Mile, and 3PC operations
- Pull, consolidate, and analyze data from multiple sources (SQL, Excel, internal dashboards) to generate operational insights, build recurring and ad hoc reports, and measure the effectiveness of improvement initiatives
- Drive cross-functional resolution of structural network gaps by aligning Fulfillment Centers, Supply Chain, Procurement, Finance, AMZL, and Carrier teams around shared priorities and trackable action plans

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Voice of the Customer , Leo Global Customer Operations
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to own the Voice of the Customer (VoC) program for Amazon Leo — a greenfield build spanning both consumer (B2C) and enterprise (B2B) customer segments. This is a high-visibility, cross-functional role responsible for designing and operating the systems that transform customer feedback into actionable business intelligence, driving continuous improvement across the full customer journey from purchase through active service. This role is the architect of tools, systems, and customer connections — someone with a strong appetite for big data, technical depth to build and operate analytics infrastructure, and marketing acumen to translate customer signals into compelling narratives that drive action across the organization.
You will set the strategy, build the operational infrastructure, and run the day-to-day program, working across product, engineering, customer service, field service, marketing, legal, and data science to close the loop on customer feedback at scale.

Key job responsibilities
• Own end-to-end VoC program design and operations across B2C and B2B segments, including survey strategy, feedback touchpoint mapping, and escalation frameworks
• Partner with third-party vendors and internal engineering teams to integrate survey delivery across web, in-app, email, and field service channels
• Define and maintain VoC metrics, including CSAT, NPS, and operational proxy metrics, and establish escalation thresholds that trigger cross-functional action
• Build and operate real-time monitoring mechanisms, including flash reports, dashboards, and daily standup cadences, especially during high-intensity launch windows
• Lead cross-functional triage for customer-reported issues, routing signals to the appropriate owning teams (product, network engineering, hardware, CS, field service) and tracking resolution
• Design and operate business review cadences (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly) that connect customer feedback to leadership decision-making
• Collaborate with legal, privacy, and security teams to ensure survey and data handling practices meet compliance requirements
• Define go/no-go quality gates for new market launches using VoC-derived customer satisfaction and service reliability metrics
• Build and maintain the VoC analytics infrastructure in partnership with BI engineers, ensuring data from multiple feedback channels feeds a single source of truth

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience working cross functionally across several teams
Preferred qualifications:

- Knowledge of general AI tools

- Experience building and operating customer feedback or VoC programs at scale
- Background in consumer electronics, connectivity services, or hardware-as-a-service products

jobs.title: Program Manager I - Sales Enablement,  Global Logistics Domestic First Mile
jobs.description:
Amazon’s Global Logistics organization is looking for a Program Manager to build and manage the sales enablement tools used by our shipper engagement team. The team works with sellers and vendors to increase adoption of Amazon-managed inbound transportation services and improve the customer experience.

In this role, you will own our customer relationship management (CRM) system and related sales tools from requirements through launch and ongoing improvement. You will work directly with business development and account management users to understand their workflows, build practical solutions, automate manual processes, maintain data quality, and create reporting that helps the team manage customer relationships and sales opportunities. You will partner with product, engineering, and analytics teams when solutions require broader technical support.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on builder who can translate business needs into tools that teams use. You are comfortable working with data, learning new systems, and coordinating work across business and technical teams. You will use customer feedback and performance data to improve the tools over time and increase sales-team productivity.

Key job responsibilities
Key Job Responsibilities

Own the development, maintenance, and improvement of the team’s customer relationship management system and related sales enablement tools.
Work with business development and account management users to understand their workflows and translate their needs into clear requirements.
Build and configure workflows, dashboards, reports, automations, and other lightweight solutions that improve sales-team productivity.
Maintain data quality, user access, documentation, and operating procedures for the tools.
Manage the enhancement backlog, test changes with users, coordinate launches, and measure adoption after release.
Partner with product, engineering, analytics, and operations teams on integrations or changes that require technical support.
Use customer feedback and performance data to identify tool gaps and prioritize improvements.
Train users and create self-service guidance that supports consistent use of the tools.

A day in the life
In this role, you own the tools and mechanisms our sales team relies on to grow shipper adoption. A typical day blends building, program management, and cross-functional coordination.

You might start by reviewing the team's CRM and pipeline dashboards, spotting a data gap, and working with a business development lead to close it. In the afternoon, you automate a report that was being built by hand each week, so the team gets it reliably without manual effort. You'll also translate an ambiguous leadership goal into a metric, a dashboard, and a repeatable mechanism.

The best candidates for this role Dive Deep into data, Invent and Simplify manual processes into durable mechanisms, and Deliver Results that let the team scale.

About the team
Amazon Global Logistics (GL) is responsible for optimizing cost-effective flow throughout Amazon’s inbound network while providing Amazon with greater control, performance, and inbound visibility. The Domestic First Mile (DFM) team within GL is responsible for pricing, cost, growth, speed, and profitability of the domestic inbound business. Our customer is the shipper who utilizes DFM programs (vendors and sellers). Our objective is to execute on time, save shippers money, and offer distinctive features and services to all shippers regardless of size.

- 2+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of advanced Microsoft Word and Excel experience
- Bachelor's degree in relevant field, or 2+ years of Amazon RME (BB/3P) full time experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- 2+ years of project/program management experience
- 2+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- Experience translating customer needs into business requirements
- Experience developing and implementing systems/tools utilized for CRM, variable compensation, revenue reporting, forecasting, Salesforce automation, etc.
- Experience using data and metrics to back up assumptions, evaluate outcomes, and make data-driven decisions

- Knowledge of Lean principles and DMAIC methodology
- Experience in MS Access and SQL
- Experience in requirement gathering and ability to write clear and detailed requirement document
- Experience using Microsoft Projects software
- Experience with material handling systems (MHS) installation, operation and maintenance
- Experience working in an analytical environment with cross-functional teams

jobs.title: Tech Infrastructure Program Manager, AWS Data Center Planning & Delivery
jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Service (AWS) is a comprehensive, evolving, and growing business unit within Amazon.com. Since early 2006, AWS has provided a highly reliable, scalable, low-cost cloud infrastructure platform that empowers hundreds of thousands of businesses in 190 countries to innovate and invent.
Do you have the business background, complex cross functional program management experience, financial expertise, legal/regulatory comprehension and technical understanding? Can you communicate effectively, find clarity in ambiguity, and simplicity in complexity ?
If yes, then come and explore this exciting role. This role in Amazon Data Services India Private Limited (ADSIPL) Telengana builds infrastructure that hosts AWS cloud services. It delivers AWS cloud infrastructure in a challenging, high growth, fast paced and customer focused work environment. In this role, you will lead cross functional teams to deliver usable data center capacity. You will partner with senior stakeholders to develop, document, manage and deliver infrastructure designs, implementation schedules and budgets. You will earn trust of your partners in your ability to solve complex issues and steer teams in right direction to deliver results, on-time and at-cost.
You must be an exceptionally strong communicator (both written and verbal), and possess relevant experience in managing technical and strategic programs. If you bring past experience in data center deployment programs, great. If not, then having a background in program and project management, architecture/design, mechanical/electrical engineering, software/hardware engineering with strong urge to learn will be essential.
Come Join us, have fun, and create history!!

Key job responsibilities
Infrastructure TPM owns delivery of new DC across one or more availability zones in India. They manage 10+ projects at any time. They bridge internal customers, business functions, (Planning, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Policy, Operations), and functional delivery teams (Construction, Commissioning, Controls, Fiber and Network) to enable on-time and right sized delivery of new DC capacity.
The scope begins with early expansion planning, which includes a feasibility analysis to approve expansion plans and associated build timelines. They evaluate multiple factors prior to approving a new plan of record, including owned/leased/collocated DC supply, utility delivery (power, water, and fiber), and long lead equipment (LLE) availability. It requires region-wide knowledge and monitoring of in-flight projects, major risks, and remediation efforts to ensure DC delivery is not only on track to meet supply commitments but also to meet customer demand, which is constantly changing.
A successful TPM must be capable of managing a combination of metrics, tools, and mechanisms to remain aware of ongoing risks or issues that require their action, decision, mitigations, or effort to identify alternative solutions communicating up, down, and across the organization to align direction, gain support and drive remediation efforts

About the team
Diverse Experiences:
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth:
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

- Enjoy a high degree of ownership: Drive the commercial levers for Global Store, from identifying high-potential international selection, to building promotional and marketing strategy, to understanding and shaping pricing levers.

jobs.title: Engineering Program Manager, NA Field Engineering
jobs.description:
Application deadline: Oct 13, 2026

Amazon is seeking an Engineering Program Manager to support the Amazon Logistics North America (AMZL NA) Engineering team, part of Amazon's Last Mile organization. The Last Mile team helps get customer packages from delivery stations to a customer's doorstep.

This is a unique opportunity to own high-impact engineering programs and mechanisms that advance the intelligence and reliability of our last mile business. We are looking for an individual who has experience creating scalable, data-driven solutions to complex reliability and engineering problems. In this role, you will be responsible for driving engineering program governance, compliance reporting, data analytics, and documentation systems that enable leadership visibility, cross-functional alignment, and operational excellence across a portfolio of automation and electrical infrastructure projects.

You will build and maintain the mechanisms that keep our engineering organization running at the highest standard—from automated dashboards and compliance reporting to documentation platforms and stakeholder coordination. You will partner with field engineers, electrical contractors, supply chain teams, and operations leaders to deliver scalable processes that reduce rework, improve quality, and accelerate project delivery.

Key competencies of this position include insisting on the highest standards in root cause quality and corrective action effectiveness; analyzing and deep diving systems performance; inventing and simplifying solutions that improve installation and operational processes; and providing technical expertise to internal customers and stakeholders.

Key job responsibilities
• Design and maintain automated reporting pipelines and performance dashboards (e.g., equipment health trends, failure rates, system uptime) that provide leadership with real-time visibility into program health and enable data-driven decisions

• Translate complex data sets into clear narratives and actionable recommendations for stakeholders at all levels, supporting weekly business reviews and program prioritization

• Build and maintain AI-powered compliance tools that aggregate multi-source data (invoices, training records, action items) into consolidated weekly leadership reports

• Manage multiple concurrent engineering projects (electrical, automation, MHE) across the NA delivery station network, coordinating timelines and deliverables with external contractors

Amazon is seeking an Engineering Program Manager to support the Amazon Logistics North America (AMZL NA) Engineering team, part of Amazon's Last Mile organization. The Last Mile team helps get customer packages from delivery stations to a customer's doorstep.

This is a unique opportunity to own high-impact engineering programs and mechanisms that advance the intelligence and reliability of our last mile business. We are looking for an individual who has experience creating scalable, data-driven solutions to complex reliability and engineering problems. In this role, you will be responsible for driving engineering program governance, compliance reporting, data analytics, and documentation systems that enable leadership visibility, cross-functional alignment, and operational excellence across a portfolio of automation and electrical infrastructure projects.

You will build and maintain the mechanisms that keep our engineering organization running at the highest standard—from automated dashboards and compliance reporting to documentation platforms and stakeholder coordination. You will partner with field engineers, electrical contractors, supply chain teams, and operations leaders to deliver scalable processes that reduce rework, improve quality, and accelerate project delivery.

Key competencies of this position include insisting on the highest standards in root cause quality and corrective action effectiveness; analyzing and deep diving systems performance; inventing and simplifying solutions that improve installation and operational processes; and providing technical expertise to internal customers and stakeholders.

Key job responsibilities
• Design and maintain automated reporting pipelines and performance dashboards (e.g., equipment health trends, failure rates, system uptime) that provide leadership with real-time visibility into program health and enable data-driven decisions

• Translate complex data sets into clear narratives and actionable recommendations for stakeholders at all levels, supporting weekly business reviews and program prioritization
